text: Yes, of the Gentiles also, since there is only one God, and he will pronounce those who are circumcised righteous as the result of faith, and also those who are uncircumcised on their showing the same faith.

title: Romans 3:31
text: Do we, then, use this faith to abolish Law? Heaven forbid! No, we establish Law.

title: Romans 4:1
text: What then, it may be asked, are we to say about Abraham, the ancestor of our nation?

title: Romans 4:2
text: If he was pronounced righteous as the result of obedience, then he has something to boast of. Yes, but not before God.

title: Romans 4:3
text: For what are the words of Scripture? 'Abraham had faith in God, and his faith was regarded by God as righteousness.'

title: Romans 4:4
text: Now wages are regarded as due to the man who works, not as a favor, but as a debt;

title: Romans 4:5
text: While, as for the man who does not rely upon his obedience, but has faith in him who can pronounce the godless righteous, his faith is regarded by God as righteousness.

title: Romans 4:6
text: In precisely the same way David speaks of the blessing pronounced upon the man who is regarded by God as righteous apart from actions--

title: Romans 4:7
text: 'Blessed are those whose wrong-doings have been forgiven and over whose sins a veil has been drawn!

title: Romans 4:8
text: Blessed the man whom the Lord will never regard as sinful!'

title: Romans 4:9
text: Is this blessing, then, pronounced upon the circumcised only or upon the uncircumcised as well? We say that-'Abraham's faith was regarded by God as righteousness.'

title: Romans 4:10
text: Under what circumstances, then, did this take place? After his circumcision or before it?

title: Romans 4:11
text: Not after, but before. And it was as a sign of this that he received the rite of circumcision-to attest the righteousness due to the faith of an uncircumcised man-in order that he might be the father of all who have faith in God even when uncircumcised, that they also may be regarded by God as righteous;

title: Romans 4:12
text: As well as father of the circumcised-to those who are not only circumcised, but who also follow our father Abraham in that faith which he had while still uncircumcised.

title: Romans 4:13
text: For the promise that he should inherit the world did not come to Abraham or his descendants through Law, but through the righteousness due to faith.

title: Romans 4:14
text: If those who take their stand on Law are to inherit the world, then faith is robbed of its meaning and the promise comes to nothing!

title: Romans 4:15
text: Law entails punishment; but, where no Law exists, no breach of it is possible.

title: Romans 4:16
text: That is why all is made to depend upon faith, that all may be God's gift, and in order that the fulfillment of the promise may be made certain for all Abraham's descendants-not only for those who take their stand on the Law, but also for those who take their stand on the faith of Abraham. (He is the Father of us all;

title: Romans 4:17
text: As Scripture says-'I have made thee the Father of many nations.') And this they do in the sight of that God in whom Abraham had faith, and who gives life to the dead, and speaks of what does not yet exist as if it did.

title: Romans 4:18
text: With no ground for hope, Abraham, sustained by hope, put faith in God; in order that, in fulfillment of the words-'So many shall thy descendants be,' he might become 'the Father of many nations.'

title: Romans 4:19
text: Though he was nearly a hundred years old, yet his faith did not fail him, even when he thought of his own body, then utterly worn out, and remembered that Sarah was past bearing children.

title: Romans 4:20
text: He was not led by want of faith to doubt God's promise.

title: Romans 4:21
text: On the contrary, his faith gave him strength; and he praised God, in the firm conviction that what God has promised he is also able to carry out.

title: Romans 4:22
text: And therefore his faith 'was regarded as righteousness.'

title: Romans 4:23
text: Now these words-'it was regarded as righteousness'-were not written with reference to Abraham only;

title: Romans 4:24
text: But also with reference to us. Our faith, too, will be regarded by God in the same light, if we have faith in him who raised Jesus, our Lord, from the dead;

title: Romans 4:25
text: For Jesus 'was given up to death to atone for our offences,' and was raised to life that we might be pronounced righteous.

title: Romans 5:1
text: Therefore, having been pronounced righteous as the result of faith, let us enjoy peace with God through Jesus Christ, our Lord.

title: Romans 5:2
text: It is through him that, by reason of our faith, we have obtained admission to that place in God's favor in which we not stand. So let us exult in our hope of attaining God's glorious ideal.

title: Romans 5:3
text: And not only that, but let us also exult in our troubles;

title: Romans 5:4
text: For we know that trouble develops endurance, and endurance strength of character, and strength of character hope,

title: Romans 5:5
text: And that 'hope never disappoints.' For the love of God has filled our hearts through the Holy Spirit which was given us;

title: Romans 5:6
text: Seeing that, while we were still powerless, Christ, in God's good time, died on behalf of the godless.

title: Romans 5:7
text: Even for an upright man scarcely any one will die. For a really good man perhaps some one might even dare to die.

title: Romans 5:8
text: But God puts his love for us beyond all doubt by the fact that Christ died on our behalf while we were still sinners.

title: Romans 5:9
text: Much more, then, now that we have been pronounced righteous by virtue of the shedding of his blood, shall we be saved through him from the Wrath of God.

title: Romans 5:10
text: For if, when we were God's enemies, we were reconciled to him through the death of his Son, much more, now that we have become reconciled, shall we be saved by virtue of Christ's Life.

title: Romans 5:11
text: And not only that, but we exult in God, through Jesus Christ, our Lord, through whom we have now obtained this reconciliation.

title: Romans 5:12
text: Therefore, just as sin came into the world through one man, and through sin came death; so, also, death spread to all mankind, because all men had sinned.

title: Romans 5:13
text: Even before the time of the Law there was sin in the world; but sin cannot be charged against a man where no Law exists.

title: Romans 5:14
text: Yet, from Adam to Moses, Death reigned even over those whose sin was not a breach of a law, as Adam's was. And Adam foreshadows the One to come.

title: Romans 5:15
text: But there is a contrast between Adam's Offence and God's gracious Gift. For, if by reason of the offence of the one man the whole race died, far more were the loving-kindness of God, and the gift given in the loving-kindness of the one man, Jesus Christ, lavished upon the whole race.

title: Romans 5:16
text: There is a contrast, too, between the gift and the results of the one man's sin. The judgement, which followed upon the one man's sin, resulted in condemnation, but God's gracious Gift, which followed upon many offences, resulted in a decree of righteousness.

title: Romans 5:17
text: For if, by reason of the offence of the one man, Death reigned through that one man, far more will those, upon whom God's loving- kindness and his gift of righteousness are lavished, find Life, and reign through the one man, Jesus Christ.

title: Romans 5:18
text: Briefly then, just as a single offence resulted for all mankind in condemnation, so, too, a single decree of righteousness resulted for all mankind in that declaration of righteousness which brings Life.

title: Romans 5:19
text: For, as through the disobedience of the one man the whole race was rendered sinful, so, too, through the obedience of the one, the whole race will be rendered righteous.

title: Romans 5:20
text: Law was introduced in order that offences might be multiplied. But, where sins were multiplied, the loving-kindness of God was lavished the more,

title: Romans 5:21
text: In order than, just as Sin had reigned in the realm of Death, so, too, might Loving-kindness reign through righteousness, and result in Immortal Life, through Jesus Christ, our Lord.

title: Romans 6:1
text: What are we to say, then? Are we to continue to sin, in order that God's loving-kindness may be multiplied?

title: Romans 6:2
text: Heaven forbid! We became dead to sin, and how can we go on living in it?

title: Romans 6:3
text: Or can it be that you do not know that all of us, who were baptized into union with Christ Jesus, in our baptism shared his death?

title: Romans 6:4
text: Consequently, through sharing his death in our baptism, we were buried with him; that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by a manifestation of the Father's power, so we also may live a new Life.

title: Romans 6:5
text: If we have become united with him by the act symbolic of his death, surely we shall also become united with him by the act symbolic of his resurrection.

title: Romans 6:6
text: We recognize the truth that our old self was crucified with Christ, in order that the body, the stronghold of Sin, might be rendered powerless, so that we should no longer be slaves to Sin.

title: Romans 6:7
text: For the man who has so died has been pronounced righteous and released from Sin.

title: Romans 6:8
text: And our belief is, that, as we have shared Christ's Death, we shall also share his Life.

title: Romans 6:9
text: We know, indeed, that Christ, having once risen from the dead, will not die again. Death has power over him no longer.

title: Romans 6:10
text: For the death that he died was a death to sin, once and for all. But the Life that he now lives, he lives for God.

title: Romans 6:11
text: So let it be with you-regard yourselves as dead to sin, but as living for God, through union with Christ Jesus.

title: Romans 6:12
text: Therefore do not let Sin reign in your mortal bodies and compel you to obey its cravings.

title: Romans 6:13
text: Do not offer any part of your bodies to Sin, in the cause of unrighteousness, but once for all offer yourselves to God (as those who, though once dead, now have Life), and devote every part of your bodies to the cause of righteousness.

title: Romans 6:14
text: For Sin shall not lord it over you. You are living under the reign, not of Law, but of Love.

title: Romans 6:15
text: What follows, then? Are we to sin because we are living under the reign of Love and not of Law? Heaven forbid!

title: Romans 6:16
text: Surely you know that, when you offer yourselves as servants, to obey any one, you are the servants of the person whom you obey, whether the service be that of Sin which leads to Death, or that of Duty which leads to Righteousness.

title: Romans 6:17
text: God be thanked that, though you were once servants of Sin, yet you learned to give hearty obedience to that form of doctrine under which you were placed.

title: Romans 6:18
text: Set free from the control of Sin, you became servants to Righteousness.

title: Romans 6:19
text: I can but speak as men do because of the weakness of your earthly nature. Once you offered every part of your bodies to the service of impurity, and of wickedness, which leads to further wickedness. Now, in the same way, offer them to the service of Righteousness, which leads to holiness.

title: Romans 6:20
text: While you were still servants of Sin, you were free as regards Righteousness.

title: Romans 6:21
text: But what were the fruits that you reaped from those things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of such things is Death.

title: Romans 6:22
text: But now that you have been set free from the control of Sin, and have become servants to God, the fruit that you reap is an ever-increasing holiness, and the end Immortal Life.

title: Romans 6:23
text: The wages of Sin are Death, but the gift of God is Immortal Life, through union with Christ Jesus, our Lord.

title: Romans 7:1
text: Surely, Brothers, you know (for I am speaking to men who know what Law means) that Law has power over a man only as long as he lives.

title: Romans 7:2
text: For example, by law a married woman is bound to her husband while he is living; but, if her husband dies, she is set free from the law that bound her to him.

title: Romans 7:3
text: If, then, during her husband's lifetime, she unites herself to another man, she will be called an adulteress; but, if her husband dies, the law has no further hold on her, nor, if she unites herself to another man, is she an adulteress.

title: Romans 7:4
text: And so with you, my Brothers; as far as the Law was concerned, you underwent death in the crucified body of the Christ, so that you might be united to another, to him who was raised from the dead, in order that our lives might bear fruit for God.

title: Romans 7:5
text: When we were living merely earthly lives, our sinful passions, aroused by the Law, were active in every part of our bodies, with the result that our lives bore fruit for Death.

title: Romans 7:6
text: But now we are set free from the Law, because we are dead to that which once kept us under restraint; and so we serve under new, spiritual conditions, and not under old, written regulations.

title: Romans 7:7
text: What are we to say, then? That Law and sin are the same thing? Heaven forbid! On the contrary, I should not have learned what sin is, had not it been for Law. If the Law did not say 'Thou shalt not covet,' I should not know what it is to covet.

title: Romans 7:8
text: But sin took advantage of the Commandment to arouse in me every form of covetousness, for where there is no consciousness of Law sin shows no sign of life.

title: Romans 7:9
text: There was a time when I myself, unconscious of Law, was alive; but when the Commandment was brought home to me, sin sprang into life, while I died!

title: Romans 7:10
text: The very Commandment that should have meant Life I found to result in Death!

title: Romans 7:11
text: Sin took advantage of the Commandment to deceive me, and used it to bring about my Death.

title: Romans 7:12
text: And so the Law is holy, and each Commandment is also holy, and just, and good.

title: Romans 7:13
text: Did, then, a thing, which in itself was good, involve Death in my case? Heaven forbid! It was sin that involved Death; so that, by its use of what I regarded as good to bring about my Death, its true nature might appear; and in this way the Commandment showed how intensely sinful sin is.

title: Romans 7:14
text: We know that the Law is spiritual, but I am earthly-sold into slavery to Sin.

title: Romans 7:15
text: I do not understand my own actions. For I am so far from habitually doing what I want to do, that I find myself doing the very thing that I hate.

title: Romans 7:16
text: But when I do what I want not to do, I am admitting that the Law is right.

title: Romans 7:17
text: This being so, the action is no longer my own, but that of Sin which is within me.

title: Romans 7:18
text: I know that there is nothing good in me-I mean in my earthly nature. For, although it is easy for me to want to do right, to act rightly is not easy.

title: Romans 7:19
text: I fail to do the good thing that I want to do, but the bad thing that I want not to do-that I habitually do.

title: Romans 7:20
text: But, when I do the very thing that I want not to do, the action is no longer my own, but that of Sin which is within me.

title: Romans 7:21
text: This, then, is the law that I find-When I want to do right, wrong presents itself!

title: Romans 7:22
text: At heart I delight in the Law of God;

title: Romans 7:23
text: But throughout my body I see a different law, one which is in conflict with the law accepted by my reason, and which endeavors to make me a prisoner to that law of Sin which exists throughout my body.

title: Romans 7:24
text: Miserable man that I am! Who will deliver me from the body that is bringing me to this Death?

title: Romans 7:25
text: Thank God, there is deliverance through Jesus Christ, our Lord! Well then, for myself, with my reason I serve the Law of God, but with my earthly nature the Law of Sin.

title: Romans 8:1
text: There is, therefore, now no condemnation for those who are in union with Christ Jesus;

title: Romans 8:2
text: For through your union with Christ Jesus, the Law of the life- giving Spirit has set you free from the Law of Sin and Death.

title: Romans 8:3
text: What Law could not do, in so far as our earthly nature weakened its action, God did, by sending his own Son, with a nature resembling our sinful nature, to atone for sin. He condemned sin in that earthly nature,

title: Romans 8:4
text: So that the requirements of the Law might be satisfied in us who live now in obedience, not to our earthly nature, but to the Spirit.

title: Romans 8:5
text: They who follow their earthly nature are earthly-minded, while they who follow the Spirit are spiritually minded.

title: Romans 8:6
text: To be earthly-minded means Death, to be spiritually minded means Life and Peace;

title: Romans 8:7
text: Because to be earthly-minded is to be an enemy to God, for such a mind does not submit to the Law of God, nor indeed can it do so.

title: Romans 8:8
text: They who are earthly cannot please God.

title: Romans 8:9
text: You, however, are not earthly but spiritual, since the Spirit of God lives within you. Unless a man has the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ;

title: Romans 8:10
text: But, if Christ is within you, then, though the body is dead as a consequence of sin, the spirit is Life as a consequence of righteousness.

title: Romans 8:11
text: And, if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead lives within you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will give Life even to your mortal bodies, through his Spirit living within you.

title: Romans 8:12
text: So then, Brothers, we owe nothing to our earthly nature, that we should live in obedience to it.

title: Romans 8:13
text: If you live in obedience to your earthly nature, you will inevitably die; but if, by the power of the Spirit, you put an end to the evil habits of the body, you will live.

title: Romans 8:14
text: All who are guided by the Spirit of God are Sons of God.

title: Romans 8:15
text: For you did not receive the spirit of a slave, to fill you once more with fear, but the spirit of a son which leads us to cry 'Abba, Our Father.'

title: Romans 8:16
text: The Spirit himself unites with our spirits in bearing witness to our being God's children,

title: Romans 8:17
text: And if children, then heirs-heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ, since we share Christ's sufferings in order that we may also share his Glory.

title: Romans 8:18
text: I do not count the sufferings of our present life worthy of mention when compared with the Glory that is to be revealed and bestowed upon us.

title: Romans 8:19
text: All Nature awaits with eager expectation the appearing of the Sons of God.

title: Romans 8:20
text: For Nature was made subject to imperfection-not by its own choice, but owing to him who made it so--

title: Romans 8:21
text: Yet not without the hope that some day Nature, also, will be set free from enslavement to decay, and will attain to the freedom which will mark the Glory of the Children of God.

title: Romans 8:22
text: We know, indeed, that all Nature alike has been groaning in the pains of labor to this very hour.

title: Romans 8:23
text: And not Nature only; but we ourselves also, though we have already a first gift of the Spirit-we ourselves are inwardly groaning, while we eagerly await our full adoption as Sons-the redemption of our bodies.

title: Romans 8:24
text: By our hope we were saved. But the thing hoped for is no longer an object of hope when it is before our eyes; for who hopes for what is before his eyes?

title: Romans 8:25
text: But when we hope for what is not before our eyes, then we wait for it with patience.

title: Romans 8:26
text: So, also, the Spirit supports us in our weakness. We do not even know how to pray as we should; but the Spirit himself pleads for us in sighs that can find no utterance.

title: Romans 8:27
text: Yet he who searches all our hearts knows what the Spirit's meaning is, because the pleadings of the Spirit for Christ's People are in accordance with his will.

title: Romans 8:28
text: But we do know that God causes all things to work together for the good of those who love him-those who have received the Call in accordance with his purpose.

title: Romans 8:29
text: For those whom God chose from the first he also destined from the first to be transformed into likeness to his Son, so that his Son might be the eldest among many Brothers.

title: Romans 8:30
text: And those whom God destined for this he also called; and those whom he called he also pronounced righteous; and those whom he pronounced righteous he also brought to Glory.

title: Romans 8:31
text: What are we to say, then, in the light of all this? If God is on our side, who can there be against us?

title: Romans 8:32
text: God did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up on behalf of us all; will he not, then, with him, freely give us all things?

title: Romans 8:33
text: Who will bring a charge against any of God's People? He who pronounces them righteous is God!

title: Romans 8:34
text: Who is there to condemn them? He who died for us is Christ Jesus!-or, rather, it was he who was raised from the dead, and who is now at God's right hand and is even pleading on our behalf!

title: Romans 8:35
text: Who is there to separate us from the love of the Christ? Will trouble, or difficulty, or persecution, or hunger, or nakedness, or danger, or the sword?

title: Romans 8:36
text: Scripture says-'For thy sake we are being killed all the day long, We are regarded as sheep to be slaughtered.'

title: Romans 8:37
text: Yet amidst all these things we more than conquer through him who loved us!

title: Romans 8:38
text: For I am persuaded that neither Death, nor Life, nor Angels, nor Archangels, nor the Present, nor the Future, nor any Powers,

title: Romans 8:39
text: Nor Height, nor Depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God revealed in Christ Jesus, our Lord!

title: Romans 9:1
text: I am speaking the truth as one in union with Christ; it is no lie; and my conscience, enlightened by the Holy Spirit,

title: Romans 9:2
text: Bears me out when I say that there is a great weight of sorrow upon me and that my heart is never free from pain.

title: Romans 9:3
text: I could wish that I were myself accursed and severed from the Christ, for the sake of my Brothers-my own countrymen.

title: Romans 9:4
text: For they are Israelites, and theirs are the adoption as Sons, the visible Presence, the Covenants, the revealed Law, the Temple worship, and the Promises.

title: Romans 9:5
text: They are descended from the Patriarchs; and, as far as his human nature was concerned, from them came the Christ-he who is supreme over all things, God for ever blessed. Amen.

title: Romans 9:6
text: Not that God's Word has failed. For it is not all who are descended from Israel who are true Israelites;

title: Romans 9:7
text: Nor, because they are Abraham's descendants, are they all his Children; but-'It is Isaac's children who will be called thy descendants.'

title: Romans 9:8
text: This means that it is not the children born in the course of nature who are God's Children, but it is the children born in fulfillment of the Promise who are to be regarded as Abraham's descendants.

title: Romans 9:9
text: For these words are the words of a promise-'About this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son.'

title: Romans 9:10
text: Nor is that all. There is also the case of Rebecca, when she was about to bear children to our ancestor Isaac.

title: Romans 9:11
text: For in order that the purpose of God, working through selection, might not fail-a selection depending, not on obedience, but on his Call-Rebecca was told, before her children were born and before they had done anything either right or wrong,

title: Romans 9:12
text: that 'the elder would be a servant to the younger.'

title: Romans 9:13
text: The words of Scripture are-'I loved Jacob, but I hated Esau.'

title: Romans 9:14
text: What are we to say, then? Is God guilty of injustice? Heaven forbid!

title: Romans 9:15
text: For his words to Moses are-'I will take pity on whom I take pity, and be merciful to whom I am merciful.'

title: Romans 9:16
text: So, then, all depends, not on human wishes or human efforts, but on God's mercy.

title: Romans 9:17
text: In Scripture, again, it is said to Pharaoh-'It was for this very purpose that I raised thee to the throne, to show my power by my dealings with thee, and to make my name known throughout the world.'

title: Romans 9:18
text: So, then, where God wills, he takes pity, and where he wills, he hardens the heart.

title: Romans 9:19
text: Perhaps you will say to me-'How can any one still be blamed? For who withstands his purpose?'

title: Romans 9:20
text: I might rather ask 'Who are you who are arguing with God?' Does a thing which a man has molded say to him who has molded it 'Why did you make me like this?'

title: Romans 9:21
text: Has not the potter absolute power over his clay, so that out of the same lump he makes one thing for better, and another for common, use?

title: Romans 9:22
text: And what if God, intending to reveal his displeasure and make his power known, bore most patiently with the objects of his displeasure, though they were fit only to be destroyed,

title: Romans 9:23
text: So as to make known his surpassing glory in dealing with the objects of his mercy, whom he prepared beforehand for glory,

title: Romans 9:24
text: And whom he called-even us-Not only from among the Jews but from among the Gentiles also!

title: Romans 9:25
text: This, indeed, is what he says in the Book of Hosea-'I will call those my People who were not my People, and her my beloved who was not beloved.

title: Romans 9:26
text: And in the very place where it was said to them-"Ye are not my People", they shall be called Sons of the Living God.'

title: Romans 9:27
text: And Isaiah cries aloud over Israel-'Though the Sons of Israel are like the sand of the sea in number, only a remnant of them shall escape!

title: Romans 9:28
text: For the Lord will execute his sentence upon the world, fully and without delay.'

title: Romans 9:29
text: It is as Isaiah foretold-'Had not the Lord of Hosts spared some few of our race to us, we should have become like Sodom and been made to resemble Gomorrah.'

title: Romans 9:30
text: What are we to say, then? Why, that Gentiles, who were not in search of righteousness, secured it-a righteousness which was the result of faith;

title: Romans 9:31
text: While Israel, which was in search of a Law which would ensure righteousness, failed to discover one.

title: Romans 9:32
text: And why? Because they looked to obedience, and not to faith, to secure it. They stumbled over 'the Stumbling-block.'

title: Romans 9:33
text: As Scripture says-'See, I place a Stumbling-block in Zion-- a Rock which shall prove a hindrance; and he who believes in him shall have no cause for shame.'

title: Romans 10:1
text: Brothers, my heart's desire and prayer to God for my People is for their Salvation.

title: Romans 10:2
text: I can testify that they are zealous for the honor of God; but they are not guided by true insight,

title: Romans 10:3
text: For, in their ignorance of the Divine Righteousness, and in their eagerness to set up a righteousness of their own, they refused to accept with submission the Divine Righteousness.

title: Romans 10:4
text: For Christ has brought Law to an end, so that righteousness may be obtained by every one who believes in him.

title: Romans 10:5
text: For Moses writes that, as for the righteousness which results from Law, 'those who practice it will find Life through it.'

title: Romans 10:6
text: But the righteousness which results from faith finds expression in these words--'Do not say to yourself "Who will go up into heaven?"'--which means to bring Christ down--'

title: Romans 10:7
text: Or "Who will go down into the depths below?"'--which means to bring Christ up from the dead.

title: Romans 10:8
text: No, but what does it say? 'The Message of Faith' which we proclaim.

title: Romans 10:9
text: For, if with your lips you acknowledge the truth of the Message that JESUS IS LORD, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you shall be saved.

title: Romans 10:10
text: For with their hearts men believe and so attain to righteousness, while with their lips they make their Profession of Faith and so find Salvation.

title: Romans 10:11
text: As the passage of Scripture says--'No one who believes in him shall have any cause for shame.'

title: Romans 10:12
text: For no distinction is made between the Jew and the Greek, for all have the same Lord, and he is bountiful to all who invoke him.

title: Romans 10:13
text: For 'every one who invokes the Name of the Lord shall be saved.'

title: Romans 10:14
text: But how, it may be asked, are they to invoke one in whom they have not learned to believe? And how are they to believe in one whose words they have not heard? And how are they to hear his words unless some one proclaims him?

title: Romans 10:15
text: And how are men to proclaim him unless they are sent as his messengers? As Scripture says--'How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!'

title: Romans 10:16
text: Still, it may be said, every one did not give heed to the Good News. No, for Isaiah asks--'Lord, who has believed our teaching?'

title: Romans 10:17
text: And so we gather, faith is a result of teaching, and the teaching comes in the Message of Christ.

title: Romans 10:18
text: But I ask 'Is it possible that men have never heard?' No, indeed, for--'Their voices spread through all the earth, and their Message to the very ends of the world.'

title: Romans 10:19
text: But again I ask 'Did not the people of Israel understand? First there is Moses, who says--'I, the Lord, will stir you to rivalry with a nation which is no nation; Against an undiscerning nation I will arouse your anger.'

title: Romans 10:20
text: And Isaiah says boldly--'I was found by those who were not seeking me; I made myself known to those who were not inquiring of me.

title: Romans 10:21
text: But of the people of Israel he says--'All day long I have stretched out my hands to a people who disobey and contradict.'

title: Romans 11:1
text: I ask, then, 'Has God rejected his People?' Heaven forbid! For I myself am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

title: Romans 11:2
text: God has not rejected his People, whom he chose from the first. Have you forgotten the words of Scripture in the story of Elijah- how he appeals to God against Israel?

title: Romans 11:3
text: 'Lord, they have killed thy Prophets, they have pulled down thy altars, and I only am left; and now they are eager to take my life.'

title: Romans 11:4
text: But what was the divine response? 'I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have never bowed the knee to Baal.'

title: Romans 11:5
text: And so in our own time, too, there is to be found a remnant of our nation selected by God in love.

title: Romans 11:6
text: But if in love, then no longer as a result of obedience. Otherwise love would cease to be love.

title: Romans 11:7
text: What follows from this? Why, that Israel as a nation failed to secure what it was seeking, while those whom God selected did secure it.

title: Romans 11:8
text: The rest grew callous; as Scripture says--'God has given them a deadness of mind--eyes that are not to see and ears that are not to hear--and it is so to this very day.'

title: Romans 11:9
text: David, too, says--'May their feasts prove a snare and a trap to them--a hindrance and a retribution;

title: Romans 11:10
text: May their eyes be darkened, so that they cannot see; and do thou always make their backs to bend.'

title: Romans 11:11
text: I ask then--'Was their stumbling to result in their fall?' Heaven forbid! On the contrary, through their falling away Salvation has reached the Gentiles, to stir the rivalry of Israel.

title: Romans 11:12
text: And, if their falling away has enriched the world, and their failure has enriched the Gentiles, how much more will result from their full restoration!

title: Romans 11:13
text: But I am speaking to you who were Gentiles.

title: Romans 11:14
text: Being myself an Apostle to the Gentiles, I exalt my office, in the hope that I may stir my countrymen to rivalry, and so save some of them.

title: Romans 11:15
text: For, if their being cast aside has meant the reconciliation of the world, what will their reception mean, but Life from the dead?

title: Romans 11:16
text: If the first handful of dough in holy, so is the whole mass; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.

title: Romans 11:17
text: Some, however, of the branches were broken off, and you, who were only a wild olive, were grafted in among them, and came to share with them the root which is the source of the richness of the cultivated olive.

title: Romans 11:18
text: Yet do not exult over the other branches. But, if you do exult over them, remember that you do not support the root, but that the root supports you.

title: Romans 11:19
text: But branches, you will say, were broken off, so that I might be grafted in.

title: Romans 11:20
text: True; it was because of their want of faith that they were broken off, and it is because of your faith that you are standing. Do not think too highly of yourself, but beware.

title: Romans 11:21
text: For, if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

title: Romans 11:22
text: See, then, both the goodness and the severity of God--his severity towards those who fell, and his goodness towards you, provided that you continue to confide in that goodness; otherwise you, also, will be cut off.

title: Romans 11:23
text: And they, too, if they do not continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in; for God has it in his power to graft them in again.

title: Romans 11:24
text: If you were cut off from your natural stock--a wild olive-- and were grafted, contrary to the course of nature, upon a good olive, much more will they--the natural branches--be grafted back into their parent tree.

title: Romans 11:25
text: Brothers, for fear that you should think too highly of yourselves, I want you to recognize the truth, hitherto hidden, that the callousness which has come over Israel is only partial, and will continue only till the whole Gentile world has been gathered in.

title: Romans 11:26
text: And then all Israel shall be saved. As Scripture says--'From Zion will come the Deliverer; he will banish ungodliness from Jacob.

title: Romans 11:27
text: And they shall see the fulfillment of my Covenant, when I have taken away their sins.'

title: Romans 11:28
text: From the stand-point of the Good News, the Jews are God's enemies on your account; but from the stand-point of God's selection, they are dear to him on account of the Patriarchs.

title: Romans 11:29
text: For God never regrets his gifts or his Call.

title: Romans 11:30
text: Just as you at one time were disobedient to him, but have now found mercy in the day of their disobedience;

title: Romans 11:31
text: So, too, they have now become disobedient in your day of mercy, in order that they also in their turn may now find mercy.

title: Romans 11:32
text: For God has given all alike over to disobedience, that to all alike he may show mercy.

title: Romans 11:33
text: Oh! the unfathomable wisdom and knowledge of God! How inscrutable are his judgements, how untraceable his ways! Yes--

title: Romans 11:34
text: 'Who has ever comprehended the mind of the Lord? Who has ever become his counselor?

title: Romans 11:35
text: Or who has first given to him, so that he may claim a recompense?'

title: Romans 11:36
text: For all things are from him, through him, and for him. And to him be all glory for ever and ever! Amen.

title: Romans 12:1
text: I entreat you, then, Brothers, by the mercies of God, to offer your bodies as a living and holy sacrifice, acceptable to God, for this is your rational worship.

title: Romans 12:2
text: Do not conform to the fashion of this world; but be transformed by the complete change that has come over your minds, so that you may discern what God's will is--all that is good, acceptable, and perfect.

title: Romans 12:3
text: In fulfillment of the charge with which I have been entrusted, I bid every one of you not to think more highly of himself than he ought to think, but to think till he learns to think soberly--in accordance with the measure of faith that God has allotted to each.

title: Romans 12:4
text: For, just as in the human body there is a union of many parts, and each part has its own function,

title: Romans 12:5
text: So we, by our union in Christ, many though we are, form but one body, and individually we are related one to another as its parts.

title: Romans 12:6
text: Since our gifts differ in accordance with the particular charge entrusted to us, if our gift is to preach, let our preaching correspond to our faith;

title: Romans 12:7
text: If it is to minister to others, let us devote ourselves to our ministry; the teacher to his teaching,

title: Romans 12:8
text: The speaker to his exhortation. Let the man who gives in charity do so with a generous heart; let him who is in authority exercise due diligence; let him who shows kindness do so in a cheerful spirit.

title: Romans 12:9
text: Let your love be sincere. Hate the wrong; cling to the right.

title: Romans 12:10
text: In brotherly love, be affectionate to one another; in showing respect, set an example of deference to one another;

title: Romans 12:11
text: Never flagging in zeal; fervent in spirit; serving the Master;

title: Romans 12:12
text: Rejoicing in your hope; steadfast under persecution; persevering in prayer;

title: Romans 12:13
text: Relieving the wants of Christ's People; devoted to hospitality.

title: Romans 12:14
text: Bless your persecutors--bless and never curse.

title: Romans 12:15
text: Rejoice with those who are rejoicing, and weep with those who are weeping.

title: Romans 12:16
text: Let the same spirit of sympathy animate you all, not a spirit of pride; be glad to associate with the lowly. Do not think too highly of yourselves.

title: Romans 12:17
text: Never return injury for injury. Aim at doing what all men will recognize as honorable.

title: Romans 12:18
text: If it is possible, as far as rests with you, live peaceably with every one.

title: Romans 12:19
text: Never avenge yourselves, dear friends, but make way for the Wrath of God; for Scripture declares--'"It is for me to avenge, I will requite," says the Lord.'

title: Romans 12:20
text: Rather--'If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him to drink. By doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.'

title: Romans 12:21
text: Never be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.

title: Romans 13:1
text: Let every one obey the supreme Authorities. For no Authority exists except by the will of God, and the existing Authorities have been appointed by God.

title: Romans 13:2
text: Therefore he who sets himself against the authorities is resisting God's appointment, and those who resist will bring a judgement upon themselves.

title: Romans 13:3
text: A good action has nothing to fear from Rulers; a bad action has. Do you want to have no reason to fear the Authorities? Then do what is good, and you will win their praise.

title: Romans 13:4
text: For they are God's servants appointed for your good. But, if you do what is wrong, you may well be afraid; for the sword they carry is not without meaning! They are God's servants to inflict his punishments on those who do wrong.

title: Romans 13:5
text: You are bound, therefore, to obey, not only through fear of God's punishments, but also as a matter of conscience.

title: Romans 13:6
text: This, too, is the reason for your paying taxes; for the officials are God's officers, devoting themselves to this special work.

title: Romans 13:7
text: In all cases pay what is due from you--tribute where tribute is due, taxes where taxes are due, respect where respect is due, and honor where honor is due.

title: Romans 13:8
text: Owe nothing to any one except brotherly love; for he who loves his fellow men has satisfied the Law.

title: Romans 13:9
text: The commandments, 'Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not covet,' and whatever other commandment there is, are all summed up in the words--'Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thou dost thyself.'

title: Romans 13:10
text: Love never wrongs a neighbor. Therefore Love fully satisfies the Law.

title: Romans 13:11
text: This I say, because you know the crisis that we have reached, for the time has already come for you to rouse yourselves from sleep; our Salvation is nearer now than when we accepted the Faith.

title: Romans 13:12
text: The night is almost gone; the day is near. Therefore let us have done with the deeds of Darkness, and arm ourselves with the weapons of Light.

title: Romans 13:13
text: Being in the light of Day, let us live becomingly, not in revelry and drunkenness, not in lust and licentiousness, not in quarreling and jealousy.

title: Romans 13:14
text: No! Arm yourselves with the spirit of the Lord Jesus Christ, and spend no thought on your earthly nature, to satisfy its cravings.

title: Romans 14:1
text: As for those whose faith is weak, always receive them as friends, but not for the purpose of passing judgement on their scruples.

title: Romans 14:2
text: One man's faith permits of his eating food of all kinds, while another whose faith is weak eats only vegetable food.

title: Romans 14:3
text: The man who eats meat must not despise the man who abstains from it; nor must the man who abstains from eating meat pass judgement on the one who eats it, for God himself has received him.

title: Romans 14:4
text: Who are you, that you should pass judgement on the servant of another? His standing or falling concerns his own master. And stand he will, for his Master can enable him to stand.

title: Romans 14:5
text: Again, one man considers some days to be more sacred than others, while another considers all days to be alike. Every one ought to be fully convinced in his own mind.

title: Romans 14:6
text: He who observes a day, observes it to the Master's honor. He, again, who eats meat eats it to the Master's honor, for he gives thanks to God; while he who abstains from it abstains from it to the Master's honor, and also gives thanks to God.

title: Romans 14:7
text: There is not one of us whose life concerns himself alone, and not one of us whose death concerns himself alone;

title: Romans 14:8
text: For, if we live, our life is for the Master, and, if we die, our death is for the Master. Whether, then, we live or die we belong to the Master.

title: Romans 14:9
text: The very purpose for which Christ died and came back to life was this--that he might be Lord over both the dead and the living.

title: Romans 14:10
text: I would ask the one man 'Why do you judge your Brother?' And I would ask the other 'Why do you despise your Brother?' For we shall all stand before the Bar of God.

title: Romans 14:11
text: For Scripture says--'"As surely as I live," says the Lord, "every knee shall bend before me; and every tongue shall make acknowledgment to God."'

title: Romans 14:12
text: So, then, each one of us will have to render account of himself to God.

title: Romans 14:13
text: Let us, then, cease to judge one another. Rather let this be your resolve--never to place a stumbling-block or an obstacle in a Brother's way.

title: Romans 14:14
text: Through my union with the Lord Jesus, I know and am persuaded that nothing is 'defiling in itself.' A thing is 'defiling' only to him who holds it to be so.

title: Romans 14:15
text: If, for the sake of what you eat, you wound your Brother's feelings, your life has ceased to be ruled by love. Do not, by what you eat, ruin a man for whom Christ died!

title: Romans 14:16
text: Do not let what is right for you become a matter of reproach.

title: Romans 14:17
text: For the Kingdom of God does not consist of eating and drinking, but of righteousness and peace and gladness through the presence of the Holy Spirit.

title: Romans 14:18
text: He who serves the Christ in this way pleases God, and wins the approval of his fellow men.

title: Romans 14:19
text: Therefore our efforts should be directed towards all that makes for peace and the mutual building up of character.

title: Romans 14:20
text: Do not undo God's work for the sake of what you eat. Though everything is 'clean,' yet, if a man eats so as to put a stumbling- block in the way of others, he does wrong.

title: Romans 14:21
text: The right course is to abstain from meat or wine or, indeed, anything that is a stumbling-block to your Brother.

title: Romans 14:22
text: As for yourself--keep this faith of yours to yourself, as in the presence of God. Happy is he who never has to condemn himself in regard to the very thing which he thinks right!

title: Romans 14:23
text: He, however, who has misgivings stands condemned if he still eats, because his doing so is not the result of faith. And anything not done as the result of faith is a sin.

title: Romans 15:1
text: We, the strong, ought to take on our own shoulders the weaknesses of those who are not strong, and not merely to please ourselves.

title: Romans 15:2
text: Let each of us please his neighbor for his neighbor's good, to help in the building up of his character.

title: Romans 15:3
text: Even the Christ did not please himself! On the contrary, as Scripture says of him--'The reproaches of those who were reproaching thee fell upon me.'

title: Romans 15:4
text: Whatever was written in the Scriptures in days gone by was written for our instruction, so that, through patient endurance, and through the encouragement drawn from the Scriptures, we might hold fast to our hope.

title: Romans 15:5
text: And may God, the giver of this patience and this encouragement, grant you to be united in sympathy in Christ,

title: Romans 15:6
text: So that with one heart and one voice you may praise the God and Father of Jesus Christ, our Lord.

title: Romans 15:7
text: Therefore always receive one another as friends, just as the Christ himself received us, to the glory of God.

title: Romans 15:8
text: For I tell you that Christ, in vindication of God's truthfulness, has become a minister of the Covenant of Circumcision, so that he may fulfil the promises made to our ancestors,

title: Romans 15:9
text: And that the Gentiles also may praise God for his mercy. As Scripture says--'Therefore will I make acknowledgment to thee among the Gentiles and sing in honor of thy Name.'

title: Romans 15:10
text: And again it says--'Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with God's People.'

title: Romans 15:11
text: And yet again--'Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles, and let all Peoples sing his praises.'

title: Romans 15:12
text: Again, Isaiah says--'There shall be a Scion of the house of Jesse, One who is to arise to rule the Gentiles; on him shall the Gentiles rest their hopes.'

title: Romans 15:13
text: May God, who inspires our hope, grant you perfect happiness and peace in your faith, till you are filled with this hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

title: Romans 15:14
text: I am persuaded, my Brothers--yes, I Paul, with regard to you- that you are yourselves full of kindness, furnished with all Christian learning, and well able to give advice to one another.

title: Romans 15:15
text: But in parts of this letter I have expressed myself somewhat boldly--by way of refreshing your memories--

title: Romans 15:16
text: Because of the charge with which God has entrusted me, that I should be a minister of Christ Jesus to go to the Gentiles--that I should act as a priest of God's Good News, so that the offering up of the Gentiles may be an acceptable sacrifice, consecrated by the Holy Spirit.

title: Romans 15:17
text: It is, then, through my union with Christ Jesus that I have a proud confidence in my work for God.

title: Romans 15:18
text: For I will not dare to speak of anything but what Christ has done through me to win the obedience of the Gentiles--

title: Romans 15:19
text: By my words and actions, through the power displayed in signs and marvels, and through the power of the Holy Spirit. And so, starting from Jerusalem and its neighborhood, and going as far as Illyria, I have told in full the Good News of the Christ;

title: Romans 15:20
text: Yet always with the ambition to tell the Good News where Christ's name had not previously been heard, so as to avoid building upon another man's foundations.

title: Romans 15:21
text: But as Scripture says--'They to whom he had never been proclaimed shall see; and they who have never heard shall understand!'

title: Romans 15:22
text: That is why I have so often been prevented from coming to you.

title: Romans 15:23
text: But now there are no further openings for me in these parts, and I have for several years been longing to come to you whenever I may be going to Spain.

title: Romans 15:24
text: For my hope is to visit you on my journey, and then to be sent on my way by you, after I have first partly satisfied myself by seeing something of you.

title: Romans 15:25
text: Just now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem, to take help to Christ's People there.

title: Romans 15:26
text: For Macedonia and Greece have been glad to make a collection for the poor among Christ's People at Jerusalem.

title: Romans 15:27
text: Yes, they were glad to do so; and indeed it is a duty which they owe to them. For the Gentile converts who have shared their spiritual blessings are in duty bound to minister to them in the things of this world.

title: Romans 15:28
text: When I have settled this matter, and have secured to the poor at Jerusalem the enjoyment of these benefits, I shall go, by way of you, to Spain.

title: Romans 15:29
text: And I know that, when I come to you, it will be with a full measure of blessing from Christ.

title: Romans 15:30
text: I beg you, then, Brothers, by Jesus Christ, our Lord, and by the love inspired by the Spirit, to join me in earnest prayer to God on my behalf.

title: Romans 15:31
text: Pray that I may be rescued from those in Judea who reject the Faith, and that the help which I am taking to Jerusalem may prove acceptable to Christ's People;

title: Romans 15:32
text: So that, God willing, I may be able to come to you with a joyful heart, and enjoy some rest among you.

title: Romans 15:33
text: May God, the giver of peace, be with you all. Amen.

title: Romans 16:1
text: I commend to your care our Sister, Phoebe, who helps in the work of the Church at Cenchreae;

title: Romans 16:2
text: And I ask you to give her a Christian welcome--one worthy of Christ's People--and to aid her in any matter in which she may need your assistance. She has proved herself a staunch friend to me and to many others.

title: Romans 16:3
text: Give my greeting to Prisca and Aquila, my fellow-workers in the Cause of Christ Jesus,

title: Romans 16:4
text: Who risked their own lives to save mine. It is not I alone who thank them, but all the Churches among the Gentiles thank them also.

title: Romans 16:5
text: Give my greeting, also, to the Church that meets at their house, as well as to my dear friend Epaenetus, one of the first in Roman Asia to believe in Christ;

title: Romans 16:6
text: To Mary, who worked hard for you;

title: Romans 16:7
text: To Andronicus and Junias, my countrymen and once my fellow- prisoners, who are men of note among the Apostles, and who became Christians before I did;

title: Romans 16:8
text: To my dear Christian friend Ampliatus;

title: Romans 16:9
text: To Urban, our fellow-worker in the Cause of Christ, and to my dear friend Stachys;

title: Romans 16:10
text: To that proved Christian Apelles; to the household of Aristobulus;

title: Romans 16:11
text: To my countryman Herodion; to the Christians in the household of Narcissus;

title: Romans 16:12
text: To Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who have worked hard for the Master; to my dear friend Persis, for she has done much hard work for the Master;

title: Romans 16:13
text: To that eminent Christian, Rufus, and to his mother, who has been a mother to me also;

title: Romans 16:14
text: To Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the Brothers with them;

title: Romans 16:15
text: Also to Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and to all Christ's People who are with them.

title: Romans 16:16
text: Greet one another with a sacred kiss. All the Churches of the Christ send you greetings.

title: Romans 16:17
text: I urge you, Brothers, to be on your guard against people who, by disregarding the teaching which you received, cause divisions and create difficulties; dissociate yourselves from them.

title: Romans 16:18
text: For such persons are not serving Christ, our Master, but are slaves to their own appetites; and, by their smooth words and flattery, they deceive simple-minded people.

title: Romans 16:19
text: Every one has heard of your ready obedience. It is true that I am very happy about you, but I want you to be well versed in all that is good, and innocent of all that is bad.

title: Romans 16:20
text: And God, the giver of peace, will before long crush Satan under your feet. May the blessing of Jesus, our Lord, be with you.

title: Romans 16:21
text: Timothy, my fellow-worker, sends you his greetings, and Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my countrymen, send theirs.

title: Romans 16:22
text: I Tertius, who am writing this letter, send you my Christian greeting.

title: Romans 16:23
text: My host Gaius, who extends his hospitality to the whole Church, sends you his greeting; and Erastus, the City Treasurer, and Quartus, our Brother, add theirs.

title: Romans 16:24
text: (Translation omits this verse)

title: Romans 16:25
text: Now to him who is able to strengthen you, as promised in the Good News entrusted to me and in the proclamation of Jesus Christ, in accordance with the revelation of that hidden purpose, which in past ages was kept secret but now has been revealed

title: Romans 16:26
text: And, in obedience to the command of the Immortal God, made known through the writings of the Prophets to all nations, to secure submission to the Faith--

title: Romans 16:27
text: To him, I say, the wise and only God, be ascribed, through Jesus Christ, all glory for ever and ever. Amen. (r)

title: I Corinthians 1:1
text: To the Church of God in Corinth, to those who have been consecrated by union with Christ Jesus and called to become his People, and also to all, wherever they may be, who invoke the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ-their Master and ours,

title: I Corinthians 1:2
text: From Paul, who has been called to be an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, And from Sosthenes, our Brother.

title: I Corinthians 1:3
text: May God, our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ bless you and give you peace.

title: I Corinthians 1:4
text: I always thank God about you for the blessing bestowed upon you in Christ Jesus.

title: I Corinthians 1:5
text: For through union with him you were enriched in every way-in your power to preach, and in your knowledge of the Truth;

title: I Corinthians 1:6
text: And so became yourselves a confirmation of my testimony to the Christ.

title: I Corinthians 1:7
text: And thus there is no gift in which you are deficient, while waiting for the Appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: I Corinthians 1:8
text: And God himself will strengthen you to the end, so that at the Day of our Lord Jesus Christ you may be found blameless.

title: I Corinthians 1:9
text: God will not fail you, and it is he who called you into communion with his Son, Jesus Christ, our Lord.

title: I Corinthians 1:10
text: But I appeal to you, Brothers, by the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to agree in what you profess, and not to allow divisions to exist among you, but to be united-of one mind and of one opinion.

title: I Corinthians 1:11
text: For I have been informed, my Brothers, by the members of Chloe's household, that party feeling exists among you.

title: I Corinthians 1:12
text: I mean this, that every one of you says either 'I follow Paul,' or 'I Apollos,' or 'I Kephas,' or 'I Christ.'

title: I Corinthians 1:13
text: You have rent the Christ in pieces! Was it Paul who was crucified for you? or were you baptized into the Faith of Paul?

title: I Corinthians 1:14
text: I am thankful that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius,

title: I Corinthians 1:15
text: So that no one can say that you were baptized into my Faith.

title: I Corinthians 1:16
text: I baptized also the household of Stephanas. I do not know that I baptized any one else.

title: I Corinthians 1:17
text: My mission from Christ was not to baptize, but to tell the Good News; not, however, in the language of philosophy, lest the cross of the Christ should be robbed of its meaning.

title: I Corinthians 1:18
text: The Message of the Cross is indeed mere folly to those who are in the path to Ruin, but to us who are in the path of Salvation it is the very power of God.

title: I Corinthians 1:19
text: For Scripture says-'I will bring the philosophy of the philosophers to nought, and the shrewdness of the shrewd I will make of no account.'

title: I Corinthians 1:20
text: Where is the Philosopher? where the Teacher of the Law? where the Disputant of to-day? Has not God shown the world's philosophy to be folly?

title: I Corinthians 1:21
text: For since the world, in God's wisdom, did not by its philosophy learn to know God, God saw fit, by the 'folly' of our proclamation, to save those who believe in Christ!

title: I Corinthians 1:22
text: While Jews ask for miraculous signs, and Greeks study philosophy,

title: I Corinthians 1:23
text: We are proclaiming Christ crucified!-to the Jews an obstacle, to the Gentiles mere folly,

title: I Corinthians 1:24
text: But to those who have received the Call, whether Jews or Greeks, Christ, the Power of God and the Wisdom of God!

title: I Corinthians 1:25
text: For God's 'folly' is wiser than men, and God's 'weakness' is stronger than men.

title: I Corinthians 1:26
text: Look at the facts of your Call, Brothers. There are not many among you who are wise, as men reckon wisdom, not many who are influential, not many who are high-born;

title: I Corinthians 1:27
text: But God chose what the world counts foolish to put its wise men to shame, and God chose what the world counts weak to put its strong things to shame,

title: I Corinthians 1:28
text: And God chose what the world counts poor and insignificant-- things that to it are unreal-to bring its 'realities' to nothing,

title: I Corinthians 1:29
text: So that in his presence no human being should boast.

title: I Corinthians 1:30
text: But you, by your union with Christ Jesus, belong to God; and Christ, by God's will, became not only our Wisdom, but also our Righteousness, Holiness, and Deliverance,

title: I Corinthians 1:31
text: So that-in the words of Scripture-'Let him who boasts make his boast of the Lord!'

title: I Corinthians 2:1
text: For my own part, Brothers, when I came to you, it was with no display of eloquence or philosophy that I came to tell the hidden purpose of God;

title: I Corinthians 2:2
text: For I had determined that, while with you, I would know nothing but Jesus Christ-and him crucified!

title: I Corinthians 2:3
text: Indeed, when I came among you, I was weak, and full of fears, and in great anxiety.

title: I Corinthians 2:4
text: My Message and my Proclamation were not delivered in the persuasive language of philosophy, but were accompanied by the manifestation of spiritual power,

title: I Corinthians 2:5
text: So that your faith should be based, not on the philosophy of man, but on the power of God.

title: I Corinthians 2:6
text: Yet there is a philosophy that we teach to those whose faith is matured, but it is not the philosophy of to-day, nor that of the leaders of to-day-men whose downfall is at hand.

title: I Corinthians 2:7
text: No, it is a divine philosophy that we teach, one concerned with the hidden purpose of God-that long-hidden philosophy which God, before time began, destined for our glory.

title: I Corinthians 2:8
text: This philosophy is not known to any of the leaders of to-day; for, had they known it, they would not have crucified our glorified Lord.

title: I Corinthians 2:9
text: It is what Scripture speaks of as-'What eye never saw, nor ear ever heard, what never entered the mind of man-even all that God has prepared for those who love him.'

title: I Corinthians 2:10
text: Yet to us God revealed it through his Spirit; for the Spirit fathoms all things, even the inmost depths of God's being.

title: I Corinthians 2:11
text: For what man is there who knows what a man is, except the man's own spirit within him? So, also, no one comprehends what God is, except the Spirit of God.

title: I Corinthians 2:12
text: And as for us, it is not the Spirit of the World that we have received, but the Spirit that comes from God, that we may realize the blessings given to us by him.

title: I Corinthians 2:13
text: And we speak of these gifts, not in language taught by human philosophy, but in language taught by the Spirit, explaining spiritual things in spiritual words.

title: I Corinthians 2:14
text: The merely intellectual man rejects the teaching of the Spirit of God; for to him it is mere folly; he cannot grasp it, because it is to be understood only by spiritual insight.

title: I Corinthians 2:15
text: But the man with spiritual insight is able to understand everything, although he himself is understood by no one.

title: I Corinthians 2:16
text: For 'who has so comprehended the mind of the Lord as to be able to instruct him?' We, however, have the very mind of Christ.

title: I Corinthians 3:1
text: But I, Brothers, could not speak to you as men with spiritual insight, but only as worldly-minded-mere infants in the Faith of Christ.

title: I Corinthians 3:2
text: I fed you with milk, not with solid food, for you were not then able to take it. No, and even now you are not able; you are still worldly.

title: I Corinthians 3:3
text: While there exist among you jealousy and party feeling, is it not true that you are worldly, and are acting merely as other men do?

title: I Corinthians 3:4
text: When one says 'I follow Paul,' and another 'I follow Apollos,' are not you like other men?

title: I Corinthians 3:5
text: What, I ask, is Apollos? or what is Paul? Servants through whom you were led to accept the Faith; and that only as the Lord helped each of you.

title: I Corinthians 3:6
text: I planted, and Apollos watered, but it was God who caused the growth.

title: I Corinthians 3:7
text: Therefore neither the man who plants, nor the man who waters, is of any account, but only God who causes the growth.

title: I Corinthians 3:8
text: In this the man who plants and the man who waters are one; yet each will receive his own reward in proportion to his own labor.

title: I Corinthians 3:9
text: For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's harvest field, God's building.

title: I Corinthians 3:10
text: In fulfillment of the charge which God had entrusted to me, I laid the foundation like a skillful master-builder; but another man is now building upon it. Let every one take care how he builds;

title: I Corinthians 3:11
text: For no man can lay any other foundation than the one already laid-Jesus Christ.

title: I Corinthians 3:12
text: Whatever is used by those who build upon this foundation, whether gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, or straw,

title: I Corinthians 3:13
text: The quality of each man's work will become known, for the Day will make it plain; because that Day is to be ushered in with fire, and the fire itself will test the quality of every man's work.

title: I Corinthians 3:14
text: If any man's work, which he has built upon that foundation, still remains, he will gain a reward.

title: I Corinthians 3:15
text: If any man's work is burnt up, he will suffer loss; though he himself will escape, but only as one who has passed through fire.

title: I Corinthians 3:16
text: Do not you know that you are God's Temple, and that God's Spirit has his home in you?

title: I Corinthians 3:17
text: If any one destroys the Temple of God, God will destroy him; for the Temple of God is sacred, and so also are you.

title: I Corinthians 3:18
text: Let no one deceive himself. If any one among you imagines that, as regards this world, he is a wise man, let him become a 'fool,' that he may become wise.

title: I Corinthians 3:19
text: For in God's sight this world's wisdom is folly. Scripture tells of-'One who catches the wise in their own craftiness,'

title: I Corinthians 3:20
text: And it says again-'The Lord sees how fruitless are the deliberations of the wise.'

title: I Corinthians 3:21
text: Therefore let no one boast about men; for all things are yours--

title: I Corinthians 3:22
text: Whether Paul, or Apollos, or Kephas, or the world, or life, or death, or the present, or the future-all things are yours!

title: I Corinthians 3:23
text: But you are Christ's and Christ is God's.

title: I Corinthians 4:1
text: Let men look upon us as Christ's servants, and as stewards of the hidden truths of God.

title: I Corinthians 4:2
text: Now what we look for in stewards is that they should be trustworthy.

title: I Corinthians 4:3
text: But it weighs very little with me that I am judged by you or by any human tribunal. No, I do not even judge myself;

title: I Corinthians 4:4
text: For, though I am conscious of nothing against myself, that does not prove me innocent. It is the Lord who is my judge.

title: I Corinthians 4:5
text: Therefore do not pass judgement before the time, but wait till the Lord comes. He will throw light upon what is now dark and obscure, and will reveal the motives in men's minds; and then every one will receive due praise from God.

title: I Corinthians 4:6
text: All this, Brothers, I have, for your sakes, applied to Apollos and myself, so that, from our example, you may learn to observe the precept-'Keep to what is written,' that none of you may speak boastfully of one teacher to the disparagement of another.

title: I Corinthians 4:7
text: For who makes any one of you superior to others? And what have you that was not given you? But if you received it as a gift, why do you boast as if you had not?

title: I Corinthians 4:8
text: Are you all so soon satisfied? Are you so soon rich? Have you begun to reign without us? Would indeed that you had, so that we also might reign with you!

title: I Corinthians 4:9
text: For, as it seems to me, God has exhibited us, the Apostles, last of all, as men doomed to death. We are made a spectacle to the universe, both to angels and to men!

title: I Corinthians 4:10
text: We, for Christ's sake, are 'fools,' but you, by your union with Christ, are men of discernment. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are despised.

title: I Corinthians 4:11
text: To this very hour we go hungry, thirsty, and naked; we are beaten; we are homeless;

title: I Corinthians 4:12
text: We work hard, toiling with our own hands. We meet abuse with blessings, we meet persecution with endurance,

title: I Corinthians 4:13
text: We meet slander with gentle appeals. We have been treated as the scum of the earth, the vilest of the vile, to this very hour.

title: I Corinthians 4:14
text: It is with no wish to shame you that I am writing like this; but to warn you as my own dear children.

title: I Corinthians 4:15
text: Though you may have thousands of instructors in the Faith of Christ, yet you have not many fathers. It was I who, through union with Christ Jesus, became your father by means of the Good News.

title: I Corinthians 4:16
text: Therefore I entreat you-Follow my example.

title: I Corinthians 4:17
text: This is my reason for sending Timothy to you. He is my own dear faithful child in the Master's service, and he will remind you of my methods of teaching the Faith of Christ Jesus-methods which I follow everywhere in every Church.

title: I Corinthians 4:18
text: Some, I hear, are puffed up with pride, thinking that I am not coming to you.

title: I Corinthians 4:19
text: But come to you I will, and that soon, if it please the Lord; and then I shall find out, not what words these men use who are so puffed up, but what power they possess;

title: I Corinthians 4:20
text: For the Kingdom of God is based, not on words, but on power.

title: I Corinthians 4:21
text: What do you wish? Am I to come to you with a rod, or in a loving and gentle spirit?

title: I Corinthians 5:1
text: There is a wide-spread report respecting a case of immorality among you, and that, too, of a kind that does not occur even among the Gentiles-a man, I hear, is living with his father's wife!

title: I Corinthians 5:2
text: Instead of grieving over it and taking steps for the expulsion of the man who has done this thing, is it possible that you are still puffed up?

title: I Corinthians 5:3
text: For I myself, though absent in body, have been present with you in spirit, and in the name of our Lord Jesus I have already passed judgement, just as if I had been present, upon the man who has acted in this way.

title: I Corinthians 5:4
text: I have decided-having been present in spirit at your meetings, when the power of the Lord Jesus was with us-

title: I Corinthians 5:5
text: To deliver such a man as this over to Satan, that what is sensual in him may be destroyed, so that his spirit may be saved at the Day of the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 5:6
text: Your boasting is unseemly. Do not you know that even a little leaven leavens all the dough?

title: I Corinthians 5:7
text: Get rid entirely of the old leaven, so that you may be like new dough-free from leaven, as in truth you are. For our Passover Lamb is already sacrificed-Christ himself;

title: I Corinthians 5:8
text: Therefore let us keep our festival, not with the leaven of former days, nor with the leaven of vice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

title: I Corinthians 5:9
text: I told you, in my letter, not to associate with immoral people- -

title: I Corinthians 5:10
text: Not, of course, meaning men of the world who are in immoral, or who are covetous and grasping, or who worship idols; for then you would have to leave the world altogether.

title: I Corinthians 5:11
text: But, as things are, I say that you are not to associate with any one who, although a Brother in name, is immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or abusive, or a drunkard, or grasping-no, not even to sit at table with such people.

title: I Corinthians 5:12
text: What have I to do with judging those outside the Church? Is it not for you to judge those who are within the Church,

title: I Corinthians 5:13
text: While God judges those who are outside? 'Put away the wicked man from among you.'

title: I Corinthians 6:1
text: Can it be that, when one of you has a dispute with another, he dares to have his case tried before the heathen, instead of before Christ's People?

title: I Corinthians 6:2
text: Do not you know that Christ's People will try the world? And if the world is to be tried by you, are you unfit to try the most trivial cases?

title: I Corinthians 6:3
text: Do not you know that we are to try angels-to say nothing of the affairs of this life?

title: I Corinthians 6:4
text: Why, then, if you have cases relating to the affairs of this life, do you set to try them men who carry no weight with the Church? To your shame I ask it.

title: I Corinthians 6:5
text: Can it be that there is not one man among you wise enough to decide between two of his Brothers?

title: I Corinthians 6:6
text: Must Brother go to law with Brother, and that, too, before unbelievers?

title: I Corinthians 6:7
text: To begin with, it is undoubtedly a loss to you to have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather let yourselves be wronged? Why not rather let yourselves be cheated?

title: I Corinthians 6:8
text: Instead of this, you wrong and cheat others yourselves-yes, even your Brothers!

title: I Corinthians 6:9
text: Do not you know that wrong-doers will have no share in God's Kingdom? Do not be deceived. No one who is immoral, or an idolater, or an adulterer, or licentious, or a sodomite,

title: I Corinthians 6:10
text: Or a thief, or covetous, or a drunkard, or abusive, or grasping, will have any share in God's Kingdom.

title: I Corinthians 6:11
text: Such some of you used to be; but you washed yourselves clean. You became Christ's People! you were pronounced righteous through the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and through the Spirit of our God!

title: I Corinthians 6:12
text: Everything is allowable for me! Yes, but everything is not profitable. Everything is allowable for me! Yes, but for my part, I will not let myself be enslaved by anything.

title: I Corinthians 6:13
text: Food exists for the stomach, and the stomach for food; but God will put an end to both the one and the other. The body, however, exists, not for immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body;

title: I Corinthians 6:14
text: And, as God has raised the Lord, so he will raise up us also by the exercise of his power.

title: I Corinthians 6:15
text: Do not you know that your bodies are Christ's members? Am I, then, to take the members that belong to the Christ and make them the members of a prostitute? Heaven forbid!

title: I Corinthians 6:16
text: Or do not you know that a man who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body (for 'the two,' it is said, 'will become one');

title: I Corinthians 6:17
text: While a man who is united with the Lord is one with him in spirit?

title: I Corinthians 6:18
text: Shun all immorality. Every other sin that men commit is something outside the body; but an immoral man sins against his own body.

title: I Corinthians 6:19
text: Again, do not you know that your body is a shrine of the Holy Spirit that is within you-the Spirit which you have from God?

title: I Corinthians 6:20
text: Moreover, you are not your own masters; you were bought, and the price was paid. Therefore, honor God in your bodies.

title: I Corinthians 7:1
text: With reference to the subjects about which you wrote to me: It would be well for a man to remain single.

title: I Corinthians 7:2
text: But, owing to the prevalence of immorality, I advise every man to have his own wife, and every woman her husband.

title: I Corinthians 7:3
text: A husband should give his wife her due, and a wife her husband.

title: I Corinthians 7:4
text: It is not the wife, but the husband, who exercises power over her body; and so, too, it is not the husband, but the wife, who exercises power over his body.

title: I Corinthians 7:5
text: Do not deprive each other of what is due-unless it is only for a time and by mutual consent, so that your minds may be free for prayer till you again live as man and wife-lest Satan should take advantage of your want of self-control and tempt you.

title: I Corinthians 7:6
text: I say this, however, as a concession, not as a command.

title: I Corinthians 7:7
text: I should wish every one to be just what I am myself. But every one has his own gift from God-one in one way, and one in another.

title: I Corinthians 7:8
text: My advice, then, to those who are not married, and to widows, is this: It would be well for them to remain as I am myself.

title: I Corinthians 7:9
text: But, if they cannot control themselves, let them marry, for it is better to marry than to be consumed with passion.

title: I Corinthians 7:10
text: To those who are married my direction is-yet it is not mine, but the Master's-that a woman is not to leave her husband

title: I Corinthians 7:11
text: (If she has done so, let her remain as she is, or else be reconciled to her husband) and also that a man is not to divorce his wife.

title: I Corinthians 7:12
text: To all others I say-I, not the Master-If a Brother is married to a woman, who is an unbeliever but willing to live with him, he should not divorce her;

title: I Corinthians 7:13
text: And a woman who is married to a man, who is an unbeliever but willing to live with her, should not divorce her husband.

title: I Corinthians 7:14
text: For, through his wife, the husband who is an unbeliever has become associated with Christ's People; and the wife who is an unbeliever has become associated with Christ's People through our Brother whom she has married. Otherwise your children would be 'defiled,' but, as it is, they belong to Christ's People.

title: I Corinthians 7:15
text: However, if the unbeliever wishes to be separated, let him be so. Under such circumstances neither the Brother nor the Sister is bound; God has called you to live in peace.

title: I Corinthians 7:16
text: How can you tell, wife, whether you may not save your husband? and how can you tell, husband, whether you may not save your wife?

title: I Corinthians 7:17
text: In any case, a man should continue to live in the condition which the Lord has allotted to him, and in which he was when God called him. This is the rule that I lay down in every Church.

title: I Corinthians 7:18
text: Was a man already circumcised when he was called? Then he should not efface his circumcision. Has a man been called when uncircumcised? Then he should not be circumcised.

title: I Corinthians 7:19
text: Circumcision is nothing; the want of it is nothing; but to keep the commands of God is everything.

title: I Corinthians 7:20
text: Let every one remain in that condition of life in which he was when the Call came to him.

title: I Corinthians 7:21
text: Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let that trouble you. No, even if you are able to gain your freedom, still do your best.

title: I Corinthians 7:22
text: For the man who was a slave when he was called to the master's service is the Master's freed-man; so, too, the man who was free when called is Christ's slave.

title: I Corinthians 7:23
text: You were bought, and the price was paid. Do not let yourselves become slaves to men.

title: I Corinthians 7:24
text: Brothers, let every one remain in the condition in which he was when he was called, in close communion with God.

title: I Corinthians 7:25
text: With regard to unmarried women, I have no command from the Master to give you, but I tell you my opinion, and it is that of a man whom the Master in his mercy has made worthy to be trusted.

title: I Corinthians 7:26
text: I think, then, that, in view of the time of suffering that has now come upon us, what I have already said is best-that a man should remain as he is.

title: I Corinthians 7:27
text: Are you married to a wife? Then do not seek to be separated. Are you separated from a wife? Then do not seek for a wife.

title: I Corinthians 7:28
text: still, if you should marry, that is not wrong; nor, if a young woman marries, is that wrong. But those who marry will have much trouble to bear, and my wish is to spare you.

title: I Corinthians 7:29
