text: What I mean, Brothers, is this-The time is short. Meanwhile, let those who have wives live as if they had none,

title: I Corinthians 7:30
text: Those who are weeping as if not weeping, those who are rejoicing as if not rejoicing, those who buy as if not possessing,

title: I Corinthians 7:31
text: And those who use the good things of the world as using them sparingly; for this world as we see it is passing away.

title: I Corinthians 7:32
text: I want you to be free from anxiety. The unmarried man is anxious about the Master's Cause, desiring to please him;

title: I Corinthians 7:33
text: While the married man is anxious about worldly matters, desiring to please his wife;

title: I Corinthians 7:34
text: And so his interests are divided. Again, the unmarried woman, whether she is old or young, is anxious about the Master's Cause, striving to be pure both in body and in spirit, while the married woman is anxious about worldly matters, desiring to please her husband.

title: I Corinthians 7:35
text: I say this for your own benefit, not with any intention of putting a halter round your necks, but in order to secure for the Master seemly and constant devotion, free from all distraction.

title: I Corinthians 7:36
text: If, however, a father thinks that he is not acting fairly by his unmarried daughter, when she is past her youth, and if under these circumstances her marriage ought to take place, let him act as he thinks right. He is doing nothing wrong-let the marriage take place.

title: I Corinthians 7:37
text: On the other hand, a father, who has definitely made up his mind, and is under no compulsion, but is free to carry out his own wishes, and who has come to the decision, in his own mind, to keep his unmarried daughter at home will be doing right.

title: I Corinthians 7:38
text: In short, the one who consents to his daughter's marriage is doing right, and yet the other will be doing better.

title: I Corinthians 7:39
text: A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives; but, if the husband should pass to his rest, the widow is free to marry any one she wishes, provided he is a believer.

title: I Corinthians 7:40
text: Yet she will be happier if she remains as she is-in my opinion, for I think that I also have the Spirit of God.

title: I Corinthians 8:1
text: With reference to food that has been offered in sacrifice to idols-We are aware that all of us have knowledge! Knowledge breeds conceit, while love builds up character.

title: I Corinthians 8:2
text: If a man thinks that he knows anything, he has not yet reached that knowledge which he ought to have reached.

title: I Corinthians 8:3
text: On the other hand, if a man loves God, he is known by God.

title: I Corinthians 8:4
text: With reference, then, to eating food that has been offered to idols-we are aware that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God but one.

title: I Corinthians 8:5
text: Even supposing that there are so-called 'gods' either in Heaven or on earth-and there are many such 'gods' and 'lords'-

title: I Corinthians 8:6
text: Yet for us there is only one God, the Father, from whom all things come (and for him we live), and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things come (and through him we live).

title: I Corinthians 8:7
text: Still, it is not every one that has this knowledge. Some people, because of their association with idols, continued down to the present time, eat the food as food offered to an idol; and their consciences, while still weak, are dulled.

title: I Corinthians 8:8
text: What we eat, however, will not bring us nearer to God. We lose nothing by not eating this food, and we gain nothing by eating it.

title: I Corinthians 8:9
text: But take care that this right of yours does not become in any way a stumbling-block to the weak.

title: I Corinthians 8:10
text: For if some one should see you who possess this knowledge, feasting in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, if he is a weak man, become so hardened that he, too, will eat food offered to idols?

title: I Corinthians 8:11
text: And so, through this knowledge of yours, the weak man is ruined-your Brother for whose sake Christ died!

title: I Corinthians 8:12
text: In this way, by sinning against your Brothers and injuring their consciences, while still weak, you sin against Christ.

title: I Corinthians 8:13
text: Therefore, if what I eat makes my Brother fall, rather than make my Brother fall, I will never eat meat again.

title: I Corinthians 9:1
text: Am I not free? Am I not an Apostle? Have I not seen our Lord Jesus? Are not you yourselves my work achieved in union with the Lord?

title: I Corinthians 9:2
text: If I am not an Apostle to others, yet at least I am to you; for you are the seal that stamps me as an Apostle in union with the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 9:3
text: The defense that I make to my critics is this:

title: I Corinthians 9:4
text: Have not we a right to food and drink?

title: I Corinthians 9:5
text: Have not we a right to take a wife with us, if she is a Christian, as the other Apostles and the Master's brothers and Kephas all do?

title: I Corinthians 9:6
text: Or is it only Barnabas and I who have no right to give up working for our bread?

title: I Corinthians 9:7
text: Does any one ever serve as a soldier at his own expense? Does any one plant a vineyard and not eat its produce? Or does any one look after a herd and not drink the milk?

title: I Corinthians 9:8
text: Am I, in all this, speaking only from the human standpoint? Does not the Law also say the same?

title: I Corinthians 9:9
text: For in the Law of Moses it is said-'Thou shalt not muzzle a bullock while it is treading out the grain.' Is it the bullocks that God is thinking of?

title: I Corinthians 9:10
text: Or is not is said entirely for our sakes? Surely it was written for our sakes, for the ploughman ought not to plough, nor the thrasher to thrash, without expecting a share of the grain.

title: I Corinthians 9:11
text: Since we, then, sowed spiritual seed for you, is it too much that we should reap from you an earthly harvest?

title: I Corinthians 9:12
text: If others share in this right over you, do not we even more? Still we did not avail ourselves of this right. No, we endure anything rather than impede the progress of the Good News of the Christ.

title: I Corinthians 9:13
text: Do not you know that those who do the work of the Temple live on what comes from the Temple, and that those who serve at the altar share the offerings with the altar?

title: I Corinthians 9:14
text: So, too, the Master has appointed that those who tell the Good News should get their living from the Good News.

title: I Corinthians 9:15
text: I, however, have not availed myself of any of these rights. I am not saying this to secure such an arrangement for myself; indeed, I would far rather die-Nobody shall make my boast a vain one!

title: I Corinthians 9:16
text: If I tell the Good News, I have nothing to boast of, for I can but do so. Woe is me if I do not tell it!

title: I Corinthians 9:17
text: If I do this work willingly, I have a reward; but, if unwillingly, I have been charged to perform a duty.

title: I Corinthians 9:18
text: What is my reward, then? To present the Good News free of all cost, and so make but a sparing use of the rights which it gives me.

title: I Corinthians 9:19
text: Although I was entirely free, yet, to win as many converts as possible, I made myself everyone's slave.

title: I Corinthians 9:20
text: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win Jews. To those who are subject to Law I became like a man subject to Law-though I was not myself subject to Law-to win those who are subject to Law.

title: I Corinthians 9:21
text: To those who have no Law I became like a man who has no Law- -not that I am free from God's Law; no, for I am under Christ's Law-to win those who have no law.

title: I Corinthians 9:22
text: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all men, so as at all costs to save some.

title: I Corinthians 9:23
text: And I do everything for the sake of the Good News, that with them I may share in its blessings.

title: I Corinthians 9:24
text: Do not you know that on a race-course, though all run, yet only one wins the prize? Run in such a way that you may win.

title: I Corinthians 9:25
text: Every athlete exercises self-restraint in everything; they, indeed, for a crown that fades, we for one that is unfading.

title: I Corinthians 9:26
text: I, therefore, run with no uncertain aim. I box-not like a man hitting the air.

title: I Corinthians 9:27
text: No, I bruise my body and make it my slave, lest I, who have called others to the contest, should myself be rejected.

title: I Corinthians 10:1
text: I want you to bear in mind, Brothers, that all our ancestors were beneath the cloud, and all passed through the sea;

title: I Corinthians 10:2
text: That in the cloud and in the sea they all underwent baptism as followers of Moses;

title: I Corinthians 10:3
text: And that they all ate the same supernatural food,

title: I Corinthians 10:4
text: and all drank the same supernatural water, for they used to drink from a supernatural rock which followed them, and that rock was the Christ.

title: I Corinthians 10:5
text: Yet with most of them God was displeased; for they were 'struck down in the desert.'

title: I Corinthians 10:6
text: Now these things happened as warnings to us, to teach us not to long for evil things as our forefathers longed.

title: I Corinthians 10:7
text: Do not become idolaters, as some of them became. Scripture says-'The people sat down to eat and drink, and stood up to dance.'

title: I Corinthians 10:8
text: Nor let us act immorally, as some of them acted, with the result that twenty-three thousand of them fell dead in a single day.

title: I Corinthians 10:9
text: Nor let us try the patience of the Lord too far, as some of them tried it, with the result that they 'were, one after another, destroyed by the snakes.'

title: I Corinthians 10:10
text: And do not murmur, as some of them murmured, and so 'were destroyed by the Angel of Death.'

title: I Corinthians 10:11
text: These things happened to them by way of warning, and were recorded to serve as a caution to us, in whose days the close of the ages has come.

title: I Corinthians 10:12
text: Therefore let the man who thinks that he stands take care that he does not fall.

title: I Corinthians 10:13
text: No temptation has come upon you that is not common to all mankind. God will not fail you, and he will not allow you to be tempted beyond your strength; but, when he sends the temptation, he will also provide the way of escape, so that you may have strength to endure.

title: I Corinthians 10:14
text: Therefore, my dear friends, shun the worship of idols.

title: I Corinthians 10:15
text: I speak to you as man of discernment; form your own judgement about what I am saying.

title: I Corinthians 10:16
text: In the Cup of Blessing which we bless, is not there a sharing in the blood of the Christ? And in the Bread which we break, is not there a sharing in the Body of the Christ?

title: I Corinthians 10:17
text: The Bread is one, and we, though many, are one body; for we all partake of that one Bread.

title: I Corinthians 10:18
text: Look at the people of Israel. Do not those who eat the sacrifices share with the altar?

title: I Corinthians 10:19
text: What do I mean? you ask. Than an offering made to an idol, or the idol itself, is anything?

title: I Corinthians 10:20
text: No; what I say is that the sacrifices offered by the Gentiles 'are offered to demons and to a Being who is no God,' and I do not want you to share with demons.

title: I Corinthians 10:21
text: You cannot drink both the Cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot partake at the Table of the Lord and at the table of demons.

title: I Corinthians 10:22
text: Or 'are we to rouse the jealousy of the Lord'? Are we stronger than he?

title: I Corinthians 10:23
text: Everything is allowable! Yes, but everything is not profitable. Everything is allowable! Yes, but everything does not build up character.

title: I Corinthians 10:24
text: A man must not study his own interests, but the interests of others.

title: I Corinthians 10:25
text: Eat anything that is sold in the market, without making inquiries to satisfy your scruples;

title: I Corinthians 10:26
text: For 'the earth, with all that is in it, belongs to the Lord.'

title: I Corinthians 10:27
text: If an unbeliever invites you to his house and you consent to go, eat anything that is put before you, without making inquiries to satisfy your scruples.

title: I Corinthians 10:28
text: But, if any one should say to you 'This has been offered in sacrifice to an idol,' then, for the sake of the speaker and his scruples, do not eat it.

title: I Corinthians 10:29
text: I do not say 'your' scruples, but 'his.' For why should the freedom that I claim be condemned by the scruples of another?

title: I Corinthians 10:30
text: If, for my part, I take the food thankfully, why should I be abused for eating that for which I give thanks?

title: I Corinthians 10:31
text: Whether, then, you eat or drink or whatever you do, do everything to the honor of God.

title: I Corinthians 10:32
text: Do not cause offence either to Jews or Greeks or to the Church of God;

title: I Corinthians 10:33
text: For I, also, try to please everybody in everything, not seeking my own advantage, but that of men in general, that they may be saved.

title: I Corinthians 11:1
text: Imitate me, as I myself imitate Christ.

title: I Corinthians 11:2
text: I praise you, indeed, because you never forget me, and are keeping my injunctions in mind, exactly as I laid them upon you.

title: I Corinthians 11:3
text: But I am anxious that you should understand that the Christ is the Head of every man, that man is the Head of woman, and that God is the Head of the Christ.

title: I Corinthians 11:4
text: Any man who keeps his head covered, when praying or preaching in public, dishonors him who is his Head;

title: I Corinthians 11:5
text: While any woman, who prays or preaches in public bare-headed, dishonors him who is her Head; for that is to make herself like one of the shameless women who shave their heads.

title: I Corinthians 11:6
text: Indeed, if a woman does not keep her head covered, she may as well cut her hair short. But, since to cut her hair short, or shave it off, marks her as one of the shameless women, let her keep her head covered.

title: I Corinthians 11:7
text: A man ought not to have his head covered, for he has been from the beginning 'the likeness of God' and the reflection of his glory, but woman is the reflection of man's glory.

title: I Corinthians 11:8
text: For it was not man who was taken from woman, but woman who was taken from man.

title: I Corinthians 11:9
text: Besides, man was not created for the sake of woman, but woman for the sake of man.

title: I Corinthians 11:10
text: And, therefore, a woman ought to wear on her head a symbol of her subjection, because of the presence of the angels.

title: I Corinthians 11:11
text: Still, when in union with the Lord, woman is not independent of man, or man of woman;

title: I Corinthians 11:12
text: For just as woman came from man, so man comes by means of woman; and all things come from God.

title: I Corinthians 11:13
text: Judge for yourselves. Is it fitting that a woman should pray to God in public with her head uncovered?

title: I Corinthians 11:14
text: Does not nature herself teach us that, while for a man to wear his hair long is degrading to him,

title: I Corinthians 11:15
text: A woman's long hair is her glory? Her hair has been given her to serve as a covering.

title: I Corinthians 11:16
text: If, however, any one still thinks it right to contest the point-well, we have no such custom, nor have the Churches of God.

title: I Corinthians 11:17
text: In giving directions on the next subject, I cannot praise you; because your meetings do more harm than good.

title: I Corinthians 11:18
text: To begin with, I hear you and, to some extent, I believe it.

title: I Corinthians 11:19
text: Indeed, there must be actual parties among you, for so only will the men of real worth become known.

title: I Corinthians 11:20
text: When you meet together, as I understand, it is not possible to eat the Lord's Supper;

title: I Corinthians 11:21
text: For, as you eat, each of you tries to secure his own supper first, with the result that one has too little to eat, and another has too much to drink!

title: I Corinthians 11:22
text: Have you no houses in which you can eat and drink? Or are you trying to show your contempt for the Church of God, and to humiliate the poor? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this matter I cannot praise you.

title: I Corinthians 11:23
text: For I myself received from the Lord the account which I have in turn given to you-how the Lord Jesus, on the very night of his betrayal, took some bread,

title: I Corinthians 11:24
text: And, after saying the thanksgiving, broke it and said "This is my own body given on your behalf. Do this in memory of me."

title: I Corinthians 11:25
text: And in the same way with the cup, after supper, saying "This cup is the new Covenant made by my blood. Do this, whenever you drink it, in memory of me."

title: I Corinthians 11:26
text: For whenever you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death-till he comes.

title: I Corinthians 11:27
text: Therefore, whoever eats the bread, or drinks the Lord's cup, in an irreverent spirit, will have to answer for an offence against the Lord's body and blood.

title: I Corinthians 11:28
text: Let each man look into his own heart, and only then eat of the bread and drink from the cup.

title: I Corinthians 11:29
text: For the man who eats and drinks brings a judgement upon himself by his eating and drinking, when he does not discern the body.

title: I Corinthians 11:30
text: That is why so many among you are weak and ill, and why some are sleeping.

title: I Corinthians 11:31
text: But, if we judged ourselves rightly, we should not be judged.

title: I Corinthians 11:32
text: Yet, in being judged by the Lord, we are undergoing discipline, so that we may not have judgement passed upon us with the rest of the world.

title: I Corinthians 11:33
text: Therefore, my Brothers, when you meet together to eat the Supper, wait for one another.

title: I Corinthians 11:34
text: If a man is hungry, let him eat at home, so that your meetings may not bring a judgement upon you. The other details I will settle when I come.

title: I Corinthians 12:1
text: In the next place, Brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant about spiritual gifts.

title: I Corinthians 12:2
text: You know that there was a time when you were Gentiles, going astray after idols that could not speak, just as you happened to be led.

title: I Corinthians 12:3
text: Therefore I tell you plainly that no one who speaks under the influence of the Spirit of God says 'JESUS IS ACCURSED,' and that no one can say 'JESUS IS LORD,' except under the influence of the Holy Spirit.

title: I Corinthians 12:4
text: Gifts differ, but the Spirit is the same;

title: I Corinthians 12:5
text: Ways of serving differ, yet the Master is the same;

title: I Corinthians 12:6
text: Results differ, yet the God who brings about every result is in every case the same.

title: I Corinthians 12:7
text: To each man there is given spiritual illumination for the general good.

title: I Corinthians 12:8
text: To one is given the power to speak with wisdom through the Spirit; to another the power to speak with knowledge, due to the same Spirit;

title: I Corinthians 12:9
text: To another faith by the same Spirit; to another power to cure diseases by the one Spirit; to another supernatural powers;

title: I Corinthians 12:10
text: To another the gift of preaching; to another the gift of distinguishing between true and false inspiration; to another varieties of the gift of 'tongues'; to another the power to interpret 'tongues.'

title: I Corinthians 12:11
text: All these result from one and the same Spirit, who distributes his gifts to each individually as he wills.

title: I Corinthians 12:12
text: For just as the human body is one whole, and yet has many parts, and all its parts, many though they are, form but one body, so it is with the Christ;

title: I Corinthians 12:13
text: For it was by one Spirit that we were all baptized to form one Body, whether Jews or Greeks, slaves or free men, and were all imbued with one Spirit.

title: I Corinthians 12:14
text: The human body, I repeat, consists not of one part, but of many.

title: I Corinthians 12:15
text: If the foot says 'Since I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,' it does not on that account cease to belong to the body.

title: I Corinthians 12:16
text: Or if the ear says 'Since I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,' it does not on that account cease to belong to the body.

title: I Corinthians 12:17
text: If all the body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If it were all hearing, where would the sense of smell be?

title: I Corinthians 12:18
text: But in fact God has placed each individual part just where he thought fit in the body.

title: I Corinthians 12:19
text: If, however, they all made up only one part, where would the body be?

title: I Corinthians 12:20
text: But in fact, although it has many parts, there is only one body.

title: I Corinthians 12:21
text: The eye cannot say to the hand 'I do not need you,' nor, again, the head to the feet 'I do not need you.'

title: I Corinthians 12:22
text: No! Those parts of the body that seem naturally the weaker are indispensable;

title: I Corinthians 12:23
text: And those parts which we deem less honorable we surround with special honor; and our ungraceful parts receive a special grace which our graceful parts do not require.

title: I Corinthians 12:24
text: Yes, God has so constructed the body--by giving a special honor to the part that lacks it-

title: I Corinthians 12:25
text: As to secure that there should be no disunion in the body, but that the parts should show the same care for one another.

title: I Corinthians 12:26
text: If one part suffers, all the others suffer with it, and if one part has honor done it, all the others share its joy.

title: I Corinthians 12:27
text: Together you are the Body of Christ, and individually its parts.

title: I Corinthians 12:28
text: In the Church God has appointed, first, Apostles, secondly Preachers, thirdly Teachers; then he has given supernatural powers, then power to cure diseases, aptness for helping others, capacity to govern, varieties of the gift of 'tongues.'

title: I Corinthians 12:29
text: Can every one be an Apostle? can every one be a Preacher? can every one be a Teacher? can every one have supernatural powers?

title: I Corinthians 12:30
text: Can every one have power to cure diseases? can every one speak in 'tongues'? can every one interpret them?

title: I Corinthians 12:31
text: Strive for the greater gifts. Yet I can still show you a way beyond all comparison the best.

title: I Corinthians 13:1
text: Though I speak in the 'tongues' of men, or even of angels, yet have not Love, I have become mere echoing brass, or a clanging cymbal!

title: I Corinthians 13:2
text: Even though I have the gift of preaching, and fathom all hidden truths and all the depths of knowledge; even though I have such faith as might move mountains, yet have not Love, I am nothing!

title: I Corinthians 13:3
text: Even though I dole my substance to the poor, even though I sacrifice my body, that I may boast, yet have not Love, it avails me nothing!

title: I Corinthians 13:4
text: Love is long-suffering, and kind; Love is never envious, never boastful, never conceited, never behaves unbecomingly;

title: I Corinthians 13:5
text: Love is never self-seeking, never provoked, never reckons up her wrongs;

title: I Corinthians 13:6
text: Love never rejoices at evil, but rejoices in the triumph of Truth;

title: I Corinthians 13:7
text: Love bears with all things, every trustful, ever hopeful, ever patient.

title: I Corinthians 13:8
text: Love never fails. But, whether it be the gift of preaching, it will be done with; whether it be the gift of 'tongues,' it will cease; whether it be knowledge, it, too, will be done with.

title: I Corinthians 13:9
text: For our knowledge is incomplete, and our preaching is incomplete,

title: I Corinthians 13:10
text: But, when the Perfect has come, that which is incomplete will be done with.

title: I Corinthians 13:11
text: When I was a child, I talked as a child, I felt as a child, I reasoned as a child; now that I am a man, I have done with childish ways.

title: I Corinthians 13:12
text: As yet we see, in a mirror, dimly, but then-face to face! As yet my knowledge is incomplete, but then I shall know in full, as I have been fully known.

title: I Corinthians 13:13
text: Meanwhile Faith, Hope, and Love endure-these three, but the greatest of these is Love.

title: I Corinthians 14:1
text: Seek this Love earnestly, and strive for spiritual gifts, above all for the gift of preaching.

title: I Corinthians 14:2
text: He who, when speaking, uses the gift of 'tongues' is speaking, not to men, but to God, for no one understands him; yet in spirit he is speaking of hidden truths.

title: I Corinthians 14:3
text: But he who preaches is speaking to his fellow men words that will build up faith, and give them comfort and encouragement.

title: I Corinthians 14:4
text: He who, when speaking, uses the gift of 'tongues' builds up his own faith, while he who preaches builds up the faith of the Church.

title: I Corinthians 14:5
text: Now I want you all to speak in 'tongues,' but much more I wish that you should preach. A Preacher is of more account than he who speaks in 'tongues,' unless he interprets his words, so that the faith of the Church may be built up.

title: I Corinthians 14:6
text: This being so, Brothers, what good shall I do you, if I come to you and speak in 'tongues,' unless my words convey some revelation, or knowledge, or take the form of preaching or teaching?

title: I Corinthians 14:7
text: Even with inanimate things, such as a flute or a harp, though they produce sounds, yet unless the notes are quite distinct, how can the tune played on the flute or the harp be recognized?

title: I Corinthians 14:8
text: If the bugle sounds a doubtful call, who will prepare for battle?

title: I Corinthians 14:9
text: And so with you; unless, in using the gift of 'tongues,' you utter intelligible words, how can what you say be understood? You will be speaking to the winds!

title: I Corinthians 14:10
text: There is, for instance, a certain number of different languages in the world, and not one of them fails to convey meaning.

title: I Corinthians 14:11
text: If, however, I do not happen to know the language, I shall be a foreigner to those who speak it, and they will be foreigners to me.

title: I Corinthians 14:12
text: And so with you; since your are striving for spiritual gifts, be eager to excel in such as will build up the faith of the Church.

title: I Corinthians 14:13
text: Therefore let him who, when speaking, uses the gift of 'tongues' pray for ability to interpret them.

title: I Corinthians 14:14
text: If, when praying, I use the gift of 'tongues,' my spirit indeed prays, but my mind is a blank.

title: I Corinthians 14:15
text: What, then, is my conclusion? Simply this-I will pray with my spirit, but with my mind as well; I will sing with my spirit, but with my mind as well.

title: I Corinthians 14:16
text: If you bless God with your spirit only, how can the man in the congregation who is without your gift say 'Amen' to your thanksgiving? He does not know what you are saying!

title: I Corinthians 14:17
text: Your thanksgiving may be excellent, but the other is not helped by it.

title: I Corinthians 14:18
text: Thank God, I use the gift of 'tongues' more than any of you.

title: I Corinthians 14:19
text: But at a meeting of the Church I would rather speak five words with my mind, and so teach others, than ten thousand words when using the gift of 'tongues.'

title: I Corinthians 14:20
text: Brothers, do not show yourselves children in understanding. In wickedness be infants, but in understanding show yourselves men.

title: I Corinthians 14:21
text: It is said in the Law-'In strange tongues and by the lips of strangers will I speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to me, says the Lord.'

title: I Corinthians 14:22
text: Therefore the gift of the 'tongues' is intended as a sign, not for those who believe in Christ, but for those who do not, while the gift of preaching is intended as a sign, not for those who do not believe in Christ, but for those who do.

title: I Corinthians 14:23
text: So, when the whole Church meets, if all present use the gift of 'tongues,' and some men who are without the gift, or who are unbelievers, come in, will not they say that you are mad?

title: I Corinthians 14:24
text: While, if all those present use the gift of preaching, and an unbeliever, or a man without the gift, comes in, he is convinced of his sinfulness by them all, he is called to account by them all;

title: I Corinthians 14:25
text: The secrets of his heart are revealed, and then, throwing himself on his face, he will worship God, and declare 'God is indeed among you!'

title: I Corinthians 14:26
text: What do I suggest, then, Brothers? Whenever you meet for worship, each of you comes, either with a hymn, or a lesson, or a revelation, or the gift of 'tongues,' or the interpretation of them; let everything be directed to the building up of faith.

title: I Corinthians 14:27
text: If any of you use the gift of 'tongues,' not more than two, or at the most three, should do so-each speaking in his turn-and some one should interpret them.

title: I Corinthians 14:28
text: If there is no one able to interpret what is said, they should remain silent at the meeting of the Church, and speak to themselves and to God.

title: I Corinthians 14:29
text: Of preachers two or three should speak, and the rest should weigh well what is said.

title: I Corinthians 14:30
text: But, if some revelation is made to another person as he sits there, the first speaker should stop.

title: I Corinthians 14:31
text: For you can all preach in turn, so that all may learn some lesson and all receive encouragement.

title: I Corinthians 14:32
text: (The spirit that moves the preachers is within the preachers' control;

title: I Corinthians 14:33
text: For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace.) This custom prevails in all the Churches of Christ's People.

title: I Corinthians 14:34
text: At the meetings of the Church married women should remain silent, for they are not allowed to speak in public; they should take a subordinate place, as the Law itself directs.

title: I Corinthians 14:35
text: If they want information on any point, they should ask their husbands about it at home; for it is unbecoming for a married woman to speak at a meeting of the Church.

title: I Corinthians 14:36
text: What! did God's Message to the world originate with you? or did it find its way to none but you?

title: I Corinthians 14:37
text: If any one thinks that he has the gift of preaching or any other spiritual gift, let him recognize that what I am now saying to you is a command from the Lord.

title: I Corinthians 14:38
text: Any one who ignores it may be ignored.

title: I Corinthians 14:39
text: Therefore, my Brothers, strive for the gift of preaching, and yet do not forbid speaking in 'tongues.'

title: I Corinthians 14:40
text: Let everything be done in a proper and orderly manner.

title: I Corinthians 15:1
text: Next, Brothers, I would remind you of the Good News which I told you, and which you received-the Good News on which you have taken your stand,

title: I Corinthians 15:2
text: And by means of which you are being saved. I would remind you of the very words that I used in telling it to you, since you are still holding fast to it, and since it was not in vain that you became believers in Christ.

title: I Corinthians 15:3
text: For at the very beginning of my teaching I gave you the account which I had myself received-that Christ died for our sins (as the Scriptures had foretold),

title: I Corinthians 15:4
text: That he was buried, that on the third day he was raised (as the Scriptures had foretold),

title: I Corinthians 15:5
text: And that he appeared to Kephas, and then to the Twelve.

title: I Corinthians 15:6
text: After that, he appeared to more than five hundred of our Brothers at one time, most of whom are still alive, though some have gone to their rest.

title: I Corinthians 15:7
text: After that, he appeared to James, and then to all the Apostles.

title: I Corinthians 15:8
text: Last of all, he appeared even to me, who am, as it were, the abortion.

title: I Corinthians 15:9
text: For I am the meanest of the Apostles, I who am unworthy of the name of 'Apostle,' because I persecuted the Church of God.

title: I Corinthians 15:10
text: But it is through the love of God that I am what I am, and the love that he showed me has not been wasted. No, I have toiled harder than any of them, and yet it was not I, but the love of God working with me.

title: I Corinthians 15:11
text: Whether, then, it was I or whether it was they, this we proclaim, and this you believed.

title: I Corinthians 15:12
text: Now, if it is proclaimed of Christ that he has been raised from the dead, how is it that some of you say that there is no such thing as a resurrection of the dead?

title: I Corinthians 15:13
text: But, if there is no such thing as a resurrection of the dead, then even Christ has not been raised;

title: I Corinthians 15:14
text: And, if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is without meaning, and our faith without meaning also!

title: I Corinthians 15:15
text: Yes, and we are being proved to have borne false testimony about God; for we testified of God that he raised the Christ, whom he did not raise, if, indeed, the dead do not rise!

title: I Corinthians 15:16
text: For, if the dead do not rise, then even Christ himself has not been raised,

title: I Corinthians 15:17
text: And, if Christ has not been raised, your faith is folly-your sins are on you still!

title: I Corinthians 15:18
text: Yes, and they, who have passed to their rest in union with Christ, perished!

title: I Corinthians 15:19
text: If all that we have done has been to place our hope in Christ for this life, then we of all men are the most to be pitied.

title: I Corinthians 15:20
text: But, in truth, Christ has been raised from the dead, the first-fruits of those who are at rest.

title: I Corinthians 15:21
text: For, since through a man there is death, so, too, through a man there is a resurrection of the dead.

title: I Corinthians 15:22
text: For, as through union with Adam all men die, so through union with the Christ will all be made to live.

title: I Corinthians 15:23
text: But each in his proper order-Christ the first-fruits; afterwards, at his Coming, those who belong to the Christ.

title: I Corinthians 15:24
text: Then will come the end-when he surrenders the Kingdom to his God and Father, having overthrown all other rule and all other authority and power.

title: I Corinthians 15:25
text: For he must reign until God 'has put all his enemies under his feet.'

title: I Corinthians 15:26
text: The last enemy to be overthrown is death;

title: I Corinthians 15:27
text: For God has placed all things under Christ's feet. (But, when it is said that all things have been placed under Christ, it is plain that God is excepted who placed everything under him.)

title: I Corinthians 15:28
text: And, when everything has been placed under him, the Son will place himself under God who placed everything under him, that God may be all in all!

title: I Corinthians 15:29
text: Again, what good will they be doing who are baptized on behalf of the dead? If it is true that the dead do not rise, why are people baptized on their behalf?

title: I Corinthians 15:30
text: Why, too, do we risk our lives every hour?

title: I Corinthians 15:31
text: Daily I face death-I swear it, Brothers, by the pride in you that I feel through my union with Christ Jesus, our Lord.

title: I Corinthians 15:32
text: If with only human hopes I had fought in the arena at Ephesus, what should I have gained by it? If the dead do not rise, then-'Let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we shall die'!

title: I Corinthians 15:33
text: Do not be deceived. 'Good character is marred by evil company.'

title: I Corinthians 15:34
text: Awake to a righteous life, and cease to sin. There are some who have no true knowledge of God. I speak in this way to shame you.

title: I Corinthians 15:35
text: Some one, however, may ask 'How do the dead rise? and in what body will they come?'

title: I Corinthians 15:36
text: You foolish man! The seed you yourself sow does not come to life, unless it dies!

title: I Corinthians 15:37
text: And when you sow, you sow not the body that will be, but a mere grain-perhaps of wheat, or something else.

title: I Corinthians 15:38
text: God gives it the body that he pleases-to each seed its special body.

title: I Corinthians 15:39
text: All forms of life are not the same; there is one for men, another for beasts, another for birds, and another for fishes.

title: I Corinthians 15:40
text: There are heavenly bodies, and earthly bodies; but the beauty of the heavenly bodies is not the beauty of the earthly.

title: I Corinthians 15:41
text: There is a beauty of the sun, and a beauty of the moon, and a beauty of the stars; for even star differs from star in beauty.

title: I Corinthians 15:42
text: It is the same with the resurrection of the dead. Sown a mortal body, it rises immortal; sown disfigured, it rises beautiful;

title: I Corinthians 15:43
text: Sown weak, it rises strong; sown a human body, it rises a spiritual body.

title: I Corinthians 15:44
text: As surely as there is a human body, there is also a spiritual body.

title: I Corinthians 15:45
text: That is what is meant by the words-'Adam, the first man, became a human being'; the last Adam became a Life-giving spirit.

title: I Corinthians 15:46
text: That which comes first is not the spiritual, but the human; afterwards comes the spiritual;

title: I Corinthians 15:47
text: The first man was from the dust of the earth; the second man from Heaven.

title: I Corinthians 15:48
text: Those who are of the dust are like him who came from the dust; and those who are of Heaven are like him who came from Heaven.

title: I Corinthians 15:49
text: And as we have borne the likeness of him who came from the dust, so let us bear the likeness of him who came from Heaven.

title: I Corinthians 15:50
text: This I say, Brothers-Flesh and blood can have no share in the Kingdom of God, nor can the perishable share the imperishable.

title: I Corinthians 15:51
text: Listen, I will tell you God's hidden purpose! We shall not all have passed to our rest, but we shall all be transformed-in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye,

title: I Corinthians 15:52
text: At the last trumpet-call; for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise immortal, and we, also, shall be transformed.

title: I Corinthians 15:53
text: For this perishable body of ours must put on an imperishable form, and this dying body a deathless form.

title: I Corinthians 15:54
text: And, when this dying body has put on its deathless form, then indeed will the words of Scripture come true-

title: I Corinthians 15:55
text: 'Death has been swallowed up in victory! Where, O Death, is thy victory? Where, O Death, is thy sting?'

title: I Corinthians 15:56
text: It is sin that gives death its sting, and it is the Law that gives sin its power.

title: I Corinthians 15:57
text: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory, through Jesus Christ, our Lord.

title: I Corinthians 15:58
text: Therefore, my dear Brothers, stand firm, unshaken, always diligent in the Lord's work, for you know that, in union with him, your toil is not in vain.

title: I Corinthians 16:1
text: With reference to the Collection for Christ's People, I want you to follow the instructions that I gave to the Churches in Galatia.

title: I Corinthians 16:2
text: On the first day of every week each of you should put by what he can afford, so that no collections need be made after I have come.

title: I Corinthians 16:3
text: On my arrival, I will send any persons, whom you may authorize by letter, to carry your gift to Jerusalem;

title: I Corinthians 16:4
text: And, if it appears to be worth while for me to go also, they shall go with me.

title: I Corinthians 16:5
text: I will come to you as soon as I have been through Macedonia- -for I am going through Macedonia-

title: I Corinthians 16:6
text: And I shall probably make some stay with you or, perhaps, remain for the winter, so that you may yourselves send me on my way, wherever I may be going.

title: I Corinthians 16:7
text: I do not propose to pay you a visit in passing now, for I hope to stay with you for some time, if the Lord permits.

title: I Corinthians 16:8
text: I intend, however, staying at Ephesus till the Festival at the close of the Harvest;

title: I Corinthians 16:9
text: For a great opening for active work has presented itself, and there are many opponents.

title: I Corinthians 16:10
text: If Timothy comes, take care that he has no cause for feeling anxious while he is with you. He is doing the Master's work no less than I am.

title: I Corinthians 16:11
text: No one, therefore, should slight him. See him safely on his way to me, for I am expecting him with some of our Brothers.

title: I Corinthians 16:12
text: As for our Brother Apollos, I have often urged him to go to you with the others. He has, however, been very unwilling to do so as yet; but he will go as soon as he finds a good opportunity.

title: I Corinthians 16:13
text: Be watchful; stand firm in your faith; show yourselves men; be strong.

title: I Corinthians 16:14
text: Let everything you do be done in a loving spirit.

title: I Corinthians 16:15
text: I have another request to make of you, Brothers. You remember Stephanas and his household, and that they were the first-fruits gathered in from Greece, and set themselves to serve Christ's People.

title: I Corinthians 16:16
text: I want you, on your part, to show deference to such men as these, as well as to every fellow laborer and earnest worker.

title: I Corinthians 16:17
text: I am glad Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus have come, for they have made up for your absence;

title: I Corinthians 16:18
text: They have cheered my heart, and your hearts also. Recognize the worth of such men as these.

title: I Corinthians 16:19
text: The Churches in Roman Asia send you their greetings. Aquila and Prisca and the Church that meets at their house send you many Christian greetings.

title: I Corinthians 16:20
text: All our brothers send you greetings. Greet one another with a sacred kiss.

title: I Corinthians 16:21
text: I, Paul, add this greeting in my own handwriting.

title: I Corinthians 16:22
text: Accursed be any one who has no love for the Lord. THE LORD IS COMING.

title: I Corinthians 16:23
text: May the blessing of the Lord Jesus be with you.

title: I Corinthians 16:24
text: My love to all of you who are in union with Christ Jesus.

title: II Corinthians 1:1
text: To the Church of God in Corinth, and to all Christ's People throughout Greece, from Paul, an Apostle of Christ Jesus, by the will of God, and from Timothy, a Brother.

title: II Corinthians 1:2
text: May God, our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ bless you and give you peace.

title: II Corinthians 1:3
text: Blessed is the God and Father of Jesus Christ our Lord, the all-merciful Father, the God ever ready to console,

title: II Corinthians 1:4
text: Who consoles us in all our troubles, so that we may be able to console those who are in any trouble with the consolation that we ourselves receive from him.

title: II Corinthians 1:5
text: It is true that we have our full share of the sufferings of the Christ, but through the Christ we have also our full share of consolation.

title: II Corinthians 1:6
text: If we meet with trouble, it is for the sake of your consolation and salvation; and, if we find consolation, it is for the sake of the consolation that you will experience when you are called to endure the very sufferings that we ourselves are enduring;

title: II Corinthians 1:7
text: And our hope for you remains unshaken. We know that, as you are sharing our sufferings, you will also share our consolation.

title: II Corinthians 1:8
text: We want you, Brothers, to know that, in the troubles which befell us in Roman Asia, we were burdened altogether beyond our strength, so much so that we even despaired of life.

title: II Corinthians 1:9
text: Indeed, we had the presentiment that we must die, so that we might rely, not on ourselves, but on God who raises the dead.

title: II Corinthians 1:10
text: And from so imminent a death God delivered us, and will deliver us again; for in him we have placed our hopes of future deliverance, while you, also, help us by your prayers.

title: II Corinthians 1:11
text: And then many lips will give thanks on our behalf for the blessing granted us in answer to many prayers.

title: II Corinthians 1:12
text: Indeed, our main ground for satisfaction is this--Our conscience tells us that our conduct in the world, and still more in our relations with you, was marked by a purity of motive and a sincerity that were inspired by God, and was based, not on worldly policy, but on the help of God.

title: II Corinthians 1:13
text: We never write anything to you other than what you will acknowledge to the very end--

title: II Corinthians 1:14
text: And, indeed, you have already partly acknowledged it about us--that you have a right to be proud of us, as we shall be proud of you, on the Day of our Lord Jesus.

title: II Corinthians 1:15
text: With this conviction in my mind, I planned to come to see you first, so that your pleasure might be doubled--

title: II Corinthians 1:16
text: To visit you both on my way to Macedonia, and to come to you again on my return from Macedonia, and then to get you to send me on my way into Judea.

title: II Corinthians 1:17
text: As this was my plan, where, pray, did I show any fickleness of purpose? Or do you think that my plans are formed on mere impulse, so that in the same breath I say 'Yes' and 'No'?

title: II Corinthians 1:18
text: As God is true, the Message that we brought you does not waver between 'Yes' and 'No'!

title: II Corinthians 1:19
text: The Son of God, Christ Jesus, whom we--Silas, Timothy, and I- -proclaimed among you, never wavered between 'Yes' and 'No.' With him it has always been 'Yes.'

title: II Corinthians 1:20
text: For, many as were the promises of God, in Christ is the 'Yes' that fulfils them. Therefore, through Christ again, let the 'Amen' rise, through us, to the glory of God.

title: II Corinthians 1:21
text: God who brings us, with you, into close union with Christ, and who consecrated us,

title: II Corinthians 1:22
text: Also set his seal upon us, and gave us his Spirit in our hearts as a pledge of future blessings.

title: II Corinthians 1:23
text: But, as my life shall answer for it, I call God to witness that it was to spare you that I deferred my visit to Corinth.

title: II Corinthians 1:24
text: I do not mean that we are to dictate to you with regard to your faith; on the contrary, we work with you for your true happiness; indeed, it is through your faith that you are standing firm.

title: II Corinthians 2:1
text: For my own sake, as well, I decided not to pay you another painful visit.

title: II Corinthians 2:2
text: If it is I who cause you pain, why, who is there to cheer me, except the very person whom I am paining?

title: II Corinthians 2:3
text: So I wrote as I did, for fear that, if I had come, I should have been pained by those who ought to have made me glad; for I felt sure that it was true of you all that my joy was in every case yours also.

title: II Corinthians 2:4
text: I wrote to you in sore trouble and distress of heart and with many tears, not to give you pain, but to let you see how intense a love I have for you.

title: II Corinthians 2:5
text: Now whoever has caused the pain has not so much pained me, as he has, to some extent--not to be too severe--pained every one of you.

title: II Corinthians 2:6
text: The man to whom I refer has been sufficiently punished by the penalty inflicted by the majority of you;

title: II Corinthians 2:7
text: So that now you must take the opposite course, and forgive and encourage him, or else he may be overwhelmed by the intensity of his pain.

title: II Corinthians 2:8
text: So I entreat you to assure him of your love.

title: II Corinthians 2:9
text: I had this further object, also, in what I wrote--to ascertain whether you might be relied upon to be obedient in everything.

title: II Corinthians 2:10
text: When you forgive a man anything, I forgive him, too. Indeed, for my part, whatever I have forgiven (if I have had to forgive anything), I have forgiven for your sakes, in the presence of Christ,

title: II Corinthians 2:11
text: So as to prevent Satan from taking advantage of us; for we are not ignorant of his devices.

title: II Corinthians 2:12
text: When I went to the district round Troas to tell the Good News of the Christ, even though there was an opening for serving the Master,

title: II Corinthians 2:13
text: I could get no peace of mind because I failed to find Titus, my Brother; so I took leave of the people there, and went on to Macedonia.

title: II Corinthians 2:14
text: All thanks to God, who, through our union with the Christ, leads us in one continual triumph, and uses us to spread the sweet odor of the knowledge of him in every place.

title: II Corinthians 2:15
text: For we are the fragrance of Christ ascending to God--both among those who are in the path of Salvation and among those who are in the path to Ruin.

title: II Corinthians 2:16
text: To the latter we are an odor which arises from death and tells of Death; to the former an odor which arises from life and tells of Life. But who is equal to such a task?

title: II Corinthians 2:17
text: Unlike many people, we are not in the habit of making profit out of God's Message; but in all sincerity, and bearing God's commission, we speak before him in union with Christ.

title: II Corinthians 3:1
text: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or are we like some who need letters of commendation to you, or from you?

title: II Corinthians 3:2
text: You yourselves are our letter--a letter written on our hearts, and one which everybody can read and understand.

title: II Corinthians 3:3
text: All can see that you are a letter from Christ delivered by us, a letter written, not with ink, but with the Spirit of the Living God, not on 'tablets of stone,' but on 'tablets of human hearts.'

title: II Corinthians 3:4
text: This, then, is the confidence in regard to God that we have gained through the Christ.

title: II Corinthians 3:5
text: I do not mean that we are fit to form any judgement by ourselves, as if on our own authority;

title: II Corinthians 3:6
text: Our fitness comes from God, who himself made us fit to be ministers of a New Covenant, of which the substance is, not a written Law, but a Spirit. For the written Law means Death, but the Spirit gives Life.

title: II Corinthians 3:7
text: If the system of religion which involved Death, embodied in a written Law and engraved on stones, began amid such glory, that the Israelites were unable to gaze at the face of Moses on account of its glory, though it was but a passing glory,

title: II Corinthians 3:8
text: Will not the religion that confers the Spirit have still greater glory?

title: II Corinthians 3:9
text: For, if there was a glory in the religion that involved condemnation, far greater is the glory of the religion that confers righteousness!

title: II Corinthians 3:10
text: Indeed, that which then had glory has lost its glory, because of the glory which surpasses it.

title: II Corinthians 3:11
text: And, if that which was to pass away was attended with glory, far more will that which is to endure be surrounded with glory!

title: II Corinthians 3:12
text: With such a hope as this, we speak with all plainness;

title: II Corinthians 3:13
text: Unlike Moses, who covered his face with a veil, to prevent the Israelites from gazing at the disappearance of what was passing away.

title: II Corinthians 3:14
text: But their minds were slow to learn. Indeed, to this very day, at the public reading of the Old Covenant, the same veil remains unlifted; only for those who are in union with Christ does it pass away.

title: II Corinthians 3:15
text: But, even to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies on their hearts.

title: II Corinthians 3:16
text: 'Yet, whenever a man turns to the Lord, the veil is removed.'

title: II Corinthians 3:17
text: And the 'Lord' is the Spirit, and, where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

title: II Corinthians 3:18
text: And all of us, with faces from which the veil is lifted, seeing, as if reflected in a mirror, the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into his likeness, from glory to glory, as it is given by the Lord, the Spirit.

title: II Corinthians 4:1
text: Therefore, since it is by God's mercy that we are engaged in this ministry, we do not lose heart.

title: II Corinthians 4:2
text: No, we have renounced the secrecy prompted by shame, refusing to adopt crafty ways, or to tamper with God's Message, and commending ourselves to every man's conscience, in the sight of God, by our exhibition of the Truth.

title: II Corinthians 4:3
text: And, even if the Good News that we bring is veiled, it is veiled only in the case of those who are on the path to Ruin--

title: II Corinthians 4:4
text: Men whose minds have been blinded by the God of this Age, unbelievers as they are, so that the light from the Good News of the glory of the Christ, who is the very incarnation of God, should not shine for them.

title: II Corinthians 4:5
text: (For it is not ourselves that we proclaim, but Christ Jesus, as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake.)

title: II Corinthians 4:6
text: Indeed, the same God who said 'Out of darkness light shall shine,' has shone in upon our hearts, so that we should bring out into the light the knowledge of the glory of God, seen in the face of Christ.

title: II Corinthians 4:7
text: This treasure we have in these earthen vessels, that its all- prevailing power may be seen to come from God, and not to be our own.

title: II Corinthians 4:8
text: Though hard pressed on every side, we are never hemmed in; through perplexed, never driven to despair;

title: II Corinthians 4:9
text: Though pursued, never abandoned; though struck down, never killed!

title: II Corinthians 4:10
text: We always bear on our bodies the marks of the death that Jesus died, so that the Life also of Jesus may be exhibited in our bodies.

title: II Corinthians 4:11
text: Indeed, we who still live are continually being given over to death for Jesus' sake, so that the Life also of Jesus may be exhibited in our mortal nature.

title: II Corinthians 4:12
text: And so, while death is at work within us, Life is at work within you.

title: II Corinthians 4:13
text: But, in the same spirit of faith as that expressed in the words--'I believed, and therefore I spoke,' we, also believe, and therefore speak.

title: II Corinthians 4:14
text: For we know that he who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with him, and will bring us, with you, into his presence.

title: II Corinthians 4:15
text: For all this is for your sakes, that the loving-kindness of God, spreading from heart to heart, may cause yet more hearts to overflow with thanksgiving, to his glory.

title: II Corinthians 4:16
text: Therefore, as I said, we do not lose heart. No, even though outwardly we are wasting away, yet inwardly we are being renewed day by day.

title: II Corinthians 4:17
text: The light burden of our momentary trouble is preparing for us, in measure transcending thought, a weight of imperishable glory;

title: II Corinthians 4:18
text: We, all the while, gazing not on what is seen, but on what is unseen; for what is seen is transient, but what is unseen is imperishable.

title: II Corinthians 5:1
text: For we know that if our tent--that earthly body which is now our home--is taken down, we have a house of God's building, a home not made by hands, imperishable, in Heaven.

title: II Corinthians 5:2
text: Even while in our present body we sigh, longing to put over it our heavenly dwelling,

title: II Corinthians 5:3
text: Sure that, when we have put it on, we shall never be found discarnate.

title: II Corinthians 5:4
text: For we who are in this 'tent' sigh under our burden, unwilling to take it off, yet wishing to put our heavenly body over it, so that all that is mortal may be absorbed in Life.

title: II Corinthians 5:5
text: And he who has prepared us for this change is God, who has also given us his Spirit as a pledge.

title: II Corinthians 5:6
text: Therefore we are always confident, knowing that, while our home is in the body, we are absent from our home with the Lord.

title: II Corinthians 5:7
text: For we guide our lives by faith, and not by what we see.

title: II Corinthians 5:8
text: And in this confidence we would gladly leave our home in the body, and make our home with the Lord.

title: II Corinthians 5:9
text: Therefore, whether in our home or absent from our home, our one ambition is to please him.

title: II Corinthians 5:10
text: For at the Bar of the Christ we must all appear in our true characters, that each may reap the results of the life which he has lived in the body, in accordance with his actions--whether good or worthless.

title: II Corinthians 5:11
text: Therefore, because we know the fear inspired by the Lord, it is true that we are trying to win men, but our motives are plain to God; and I hope that in your inmost hearts they are plain to you also.

title: II Corinthians 5:12
text: We are not "commending ourselves" again to you, but rather are giving you cause for pride in us, so that you may have an answer ready for those who pride themselves on appearances and not on character.

title: II Corinthians 5:13
text: For, if we were "beside ourselves," it was in God's service! If we are not in our senses, it is in yours!

title: II Corinthians 5:14
text: It is the love of the Christ which compels us, when we reflect that, as one died for all, therefore all died;

title: II Corinthians 5:15
text: And that he died for all, so that the living should no longer live for themselves, but for him who died and rose for them.

title: II Corinthians 5:16
text: For ourselves, then, from this time forward, we refuse to regard any one from the world's standpoint. Even if we once thought of Christ from the standpoint of the world, yet now we do so no longer.

title: II Corinthians 5:17
text: Therefore, if any one is in union with Christ, he is a new being! His old life has passed away; a new life has begun!

title: II Corinthians 5:18
text: But all this is the work of God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ, and gave us the Ministry of Reconciliation--

title: II Corinthians 5:19
text: To proclaim that God, in Christ, was reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning men's offenses against them, and that he had entrusted us with the Message of this reconciliation.

title: II Corinthians 5:20
text: It is, then, on Christ's behalf that we are acting as ambassadors, God, as it were, appealing to you through us. We implore you on Christ's behalf--Be reconciled to God.

title: II Corinthians 5:21
text: Him who never knew sin God made to be Sin, on our behalf; so that we, through union with him, might become the Righteousness of God.

title: II Corinthians 6:1
text: Therefore, as God's fellow-workers, we also appeal to you not to receive his loving-kindness in vain.

title: II Corinthians 6:2
text: For he says--'At the time for acceptance I listened to thee, And on the day of deliverance I helped thee.' Now is the time for acceptance! Now is the day of deliverance!

title: II Corinthians 6:3
text: Never do we put an obstacle in any one's way, that no fault may be found with our ministry.

title: II Corinthians 6:4
text: No, we are trying to commend ourselves under all circumstances, as God's ministers should--in many an hour of endurance, in troubles, in hardships, in difficulties,

title: II Corinthians 6:5
text: In floggings, in imprisonments, in riots, in toils, in sleepless nights, in fastings;

title: II Corinthians 6:6
text: By purity, by knowledge, by patience, by kindliness, by holiness of spirit, by unfeigned love;

title: II Corinthians 6:7
text: By the Message of Truth, and by the power of God; by the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;

title: II Corinthians 6:8
text: Amid honor and disrepute, amid slander and praise; regarded as deceivers, yet proved to be true;

title: II Corinthians 6:9
text: As unknown, yet well-known; as at death's door, yet, see, we are living; as chastised, yet not killed;

title: II Corinthians 6:10
text: As saddened, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet enriching many; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things!

title: II Corinthians 6:11
text: We have been speaking freely to you, men of Corinth; we have opened our heart;

title: II Corinthians 6:12
text: There is room there for you, yet there is not room, in your love, for us.

title: II Corinthians 6:13
text: Can you not in return--I appeal to you as I should to children--open your hearts to us?

title: II Corinthians 6:14
text: Do not enter into inconsistent relations with those who reject the Faith. For what partnership can there be between righteousness and lawlessness? or what has light to do with darkness?

title: II Corinthians 6:15
text: What harmony can there be between Christ and Belial? or what can those who accept the Faith have in common with those who reject it?

title: II Corinthians 6:16
text: What agreement can thee be between a temple of God and idols? And we are a temple of the Living God. That is what God meant when he said--'I will dwell among them, and walk among them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

title: II Corinthians 6:17
text: Therefore "Come out from among the nations, and separate yourselves from them," says the Lord, "and touch nothing impure; And I will welcome you;

title: II Corinthians 6:18
text: And I will be a father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters," says the Lord, the Ruler of all.'

title: II Corinthians 7:1
text: With these promises, dear friends, let us purify ourselves from everything that pollutes either body or spirit, and, in deepest reverence for God, aim at perfect holiness.

title: II Corinthians 7:2
text: Make room for us in your hearts. In no instance have we ever wronged, or harmed, or taken advantage of, any one.

title: II Corinthians 7:3
text: I am not saying this to condemn you. Indeed, I have already said that you are in our very heart, to live and die together.

title: II Corinthians 7:4
text: I have the utmost confidence in you; I am always boasting about you. I am full of encouragement and, in spite of all our troubles, my heart is overflowing with happiness.

title: II Corinthians 7:5
text: Ever since we reached Macedonia, we have had no rest in body or mind; on every side there have been troubles--conflicts without, anxieties within.

title: II Corinthians 7:6
text: But God, who encourages the downcast, has encouraged us by the arrival of Titus.

title: II Corinthians 7:7
text: And it is not only by his arrival that we are encouraged, but also by the encouragement which he received from you; for he tells us of your strong affection, your penitence, and your zeal on my behalf--so that I am happier still.

title: II Corinthians 7:8
text: For, though I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Even if I were inclined to regret it--for I see that my letter did cause you sorrow though only for a time--

title: II Corinthians 7:9
text: I am glad now; not because of the sorrow it caused you, but because your sorrow brought you to repentance. For it was God's will that you should feel sorrow, in order that you should not suffer loss in any way at our hands.

title: II Corinthians 7:10
text: For, when sorrow is in accordance with God's will, it results in a repentance leading to Salvation, and which will never be regretted. The sure result of the sorrow that the world knows is Death.

title: II Corinthians 7:11
text: For see what results that other sorrow--sorrow in accordance with God's will--has had in your case. What earnestness it produced! what explanations! what strong feeling! what alarm! what longing! what eagerness! what readiness to punish! You have proved yourselves altogether free from guilt in that matter.

title: II Corinthians 7:12
text: So, then, even though I did write to you, it was not for the sake of the wrong-doer, or of the man who was wronged, but to make you conscious, in the sight of God, of your own earnest care for us. And it is this that has encouraged us.

title: II Corinthians 7:13
text: In addition to the encouragement that this gave us, we were made far happier still by the happiness of Titus for his heart has been cheered by you all.

title: II Corinthians 7:14
text: Although I have been boasting a little to him about you, you did not put me to shame; but, just as every thing we had said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus about you has also proved to be the truth.

title: II Corinthians 7:15
text: And his affection for you is all the greater, as he remembers the deference that you all showed him, and recalls how you received him with anxious care.

title: II Corinthians 7:16
text: I am glad that I can feel perfect confidence in you.

title: II Corinthians 8:1
text: We would remind you, Brothers, of the love that God has shown to the Churches in Macedonia--

title: II Corinthians 8:2
text: How, tired though they were by many a trouble, their overflowing happiness, and even their deep poverty, resulted in a flood of generosity.

title: II Corinthians 8:3
text: I can bear witness that to the full extent of their power, and even beyond their power, spontaneously,

title: II Corinthians 8:4
text: And with many an appeal to us for permission, they showed their love, and contributed their share towards the fund for their fellow-Christians.

title: II Corinthians 8:5
text: And that, not only in the way we had expected; but first they gave themselves to the Lord, and to us also, in accordance with God's will.

title: II Corinthians 8:6
text: And this led us to urge upon Titus that, as he had started the work for you, he should also see to the completion of this expression of your love.

title: II Corinthians 8:7
text: And, remembering how you excel in everything--in faith, in teaching, in knowledge, in unfailing earnestness, and in the affection that we have awakened in you--I ask you to excel also in this expression of your love.

title: II Corinthians 8:8
text: I am not laying a command upon you, but I am making use of the earnestness shown by others to test the genuineness of your affection.

title: II Corinthians 8:9
text: For you do not forget the loving-kindness of our Lord Jesus Christ--how that for your sakes, although he was rich, he became poor, so that you also might become rich through his poverty.

title: II Corinthians 8:10
text: I am only making suggestions on this matter; for this is the best course for you, since you were a year before others, not only in taking action, but also in showing your readiness to do so.

title: II Corinthians 8:11
text: And now I want you to complete the work, so that its completion may correspond with your willing readiness--in proportion, of course, to your means.

title: II Corinthians 8:12
text: For, where there is willingness, a man's gift is valued by its comparison with what he has, and not with what he has not.

title: II Corinthians 8:13
text: For our object is not to give relief to others and bring distress on you, but, by equalizing matters, to secure that,

title: II Corinthians 8:14
text: On the present occasion, what you can spare may supply their need, so that at another time what they can spare may supply your need, and thus matters may be equalized.

title: II Corinthians 8:15
text: As Scripture says--'The man who had much had nothing over, and the man who had little did not lack!'

title: II Corinthians 8:16
text: I thank God for inspiring Titus with the same keen interest in your welfare that I have;

title: II Corinthians 8:17
text: For Titus has responded to my appeals and, in his great earnestness, is starting to go to you of his own accord.

title: II Corinthians 8:18
text: We are sending with him the Brother whose fame in the service of the Good News has spread through all the Churches;

title: II Corinthians 8:19
text: And not only that, but he has been elected by the Churches to accompany us on our journey, in Keynesian with this expression of your love, which we are personally administering to the honor of the Lord, and to show our deep interest.

title: II Corinthians 8:20
text: What we are specially guarding against is that any fault should be found with us in regard to our administration of this charitable fund;

title: II Corinthians 8:21
text: For we are trying to make arrangements which shall be right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men.

title: II Corinthians 8:22
text: We are also sending with them another of our Brothers, whose earnestness we have many a time proved in many ways, and whom we now find made even more earnest by his great confidence in you.

title: II Corinthians 8:23
text: If I must say anything about Titus, he is my intimate companion, and he shares my work for you; if it is our Brothers, they are delegates of the Churches, an honor to Christ.

title: II Corinthians 8:24
text: Show them, therefore--so that the Churches may see it-- the proof of your affection, and the ground for our boasting to them about you.

title: II Corinthians 9:1
text: With reference, indeed, to the Fund for your fellow-Christians, it is quite superfluous for me to say anything to you.

title: II Corinthians 9:2
text: I know, of course, your willingness to help, and I am always boasting of it to the Macedonians. I tell them that you in Greece have been ready for a year past; and it was really your zeal that stimulated most of them.

title: II Corinthians 9:3
text: So my reason for sending our Brothers is to prevent what we said about you from proving, in this particular matter, an empty boast, and to enable you to be as well prepared as I have been saying that you are.

title: II Corinthians 9:4
text: Otherwise, if any Macedonians were to come with me, and find you unprepared, we--to say nothing of you--should feel ashamed of our present confidence.

title: II Corinthians 9:5
text: Therefore I think it necessary to urge the Brothers to go to you in advance, and to complete the arrangements for the gift, which you have already promised, so that it may be ready, as a gift, before I come, and not look as if it were being given under pressure.

title: II Corinthians 9:6
text: Remember the saying--'Scanty sowing, scanty harvest; plentiful sowing, plentiful harvest.'

title: II Corinthians 9:7
text: Let every one give as he has determined before hand, not grudgingly or under compulsion; for God loves 'a cheerful giver.'

title: II Corinthians 9:8
text: God has power to shower all kinds of blessings upon you, so that, having, under all circumstances and on all occasions, all that you can need, you may be able to shower all kinds of benefits upon others.

title: II Corinthians 9:9
text: (As Scripture says--'He scattered broadcast, he gave to the poor; His righteousness continues for ever.'

title: II Corinthians 9:10
text: And he who supplies 'seed to the sower, and bread for eating,' will supply you with seed, and cause it to increase, and will multiply 'the fruits of your righteousness').

title: II Corinthians 9:11
text: Rich in all things yourselves, you will be able to show liberality to all, which, with our help, will cause thanksgiving to be offered to God.

title: II Corinthians 9:12
text: For the rendering of a public service such as this, not only relieves the needs of your fellow-Christians, but also results in the offering to God of many a thanksgiving.

title: II Corinthians 9:13
text: Through the evidence afforded by the service thus rendered, you cause men to praise God for your fidelity to your profession of faith in the Good News of the Christ, as well as for the liberality of your contributions for them and for all others.

title: II Corinthians 9:14
text: And they also, in their prayers for you, express their longing to see you, because of the surpassing love of God displayed toward you.

title: II Corinthians 9:15
text: All thanks to God for his inestimable gift!

title: II Corinthians 10:1
text: Now, I, Paul, make a personal appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of the Christ--I who, "in your presence, am humble in my bearing towards you, but, when absent, am bold in my language to you"--

title: II Corinthians 10:2
text: I implore you not to drive me to "show my boldness," when I do come, by the confident tone which I expect to have to adopt towards some of you, who are expecting to find us influenced in our conduct by earthly motives.

title: II Corinthians 10:3
text: For, though we live an earthly life, we do not wage an earthly war.

title: II Corinthians 10:4
text: The weapons for our warfare are not earthly, but, under God, are powerful enough to pull down strongholds.

title: II Corinthians 10:5
text: We are engaged in confuting arguments and pulling down every barrier raised against the knowledge of God. We are taking captive every hostile thought, to bring it into submission to the Christ,

title: II Corinthians 10:6
text: And are fully prepared to punish every act of rebellion, when once your submission is complete.

title: II Corinthians 10:7
text: You look at the outward appearance of things! Let any one, who is confident that he belongs to Christ, reflect, for himself, again upon the fact--that we belong to Christ no less than he does.

title: II Corinthians 10:8
text: Even if I boast extravagantly about our authority--which the Lord gave us for building up your faith and not for overthrowing it--still I have no reason to be ashamed.

title: II Corinthians 10:9
text: I say this, that it may not seem as if I were trying to overawe you by my letters.

title: II Corinthians 10:10
text: For people say "His letters are impressive and vigorous, but his personal appearance is insignificant and his speaking contemptible."

title: II Corinthians 10:11
text: Let such a man be assured of this--that our words in our letters show us to be, when absent, just what our deeds will show us to be, when present.

title: II Corinthians 10:12
text: We have not indeed the audacity to class or compare ourselves with some of those who indulge in self-commendation! But, when such persons measure themselves by themselves, and compare themselves with themselves, they show a want of wisdom.

title: II Corinthians 10:13
text: We, however, will not give way to unlimited boasting, but will confine ourselves to the limits of the sphere to which God limited us, when he permitted us to come as far as Corinth.

title: II Corinthians 10:14
text: For it is not the case, as it would be if we were not in the habit of coming to you, that we are exceeding our bounds! Why, we were the very first to reach you with the Good News of the Christ!

title: II Corinthians 10:15
text: Our boasting, therefore, is not unlimited, nor does it extend to the labors of others; but our hope is that, as your faith grows, our influence among you may be very greatly increased-- though still confined to our sphere--

title: II Corinthians 10:16
text: So that we shall be able to tell the Good News in the districts beyond you, without trespassing on the sphere assigned to others, or boasting of what has been already done.

title: II Corinthians 10:17
text: 'Let him who boasts make his boast of the Lord.'

title: II Corinthians 10:18
text: For it is not the man who commends himself that stands the test, but the man who is commended by the Lord.

title: II Corinthians 11:1
text: I could wish that you would tolerate a little folly in me! But indeed you do tolerate me.

title: II Corinthians 11:2
text: I am jealous over you with the jealousy of God. For I betrothed you to one husband, that I might present you to the Christ a pure bride.

title: II Corinthians 11:3
text: Yet I fear that it may turn out that, just as the Serpent by his craftiness deceived Eve, so your minds may have lost the loyalty and purity due from you to the Christ.

title: II Corinthians 11:4
text: For, if some new-comer is proclaiming a Jesus other than him whom we proclaimed, or if you are receiving a Spirit different from the Spirit which you received, or a Good News different from that which you welcomed, then you are marvelously tolerant!

title: II Corinthians 11:5
text: I do not regard myself as in any way inferior to the most eminent Apostles!

title: II Corinthians 11:6
text: Though I am no trained orator, yet I am not without knowledge; indeed we made this perfectly clear to you in every way.

title: II Corinthians 11:7
text: Perhaps you say that I did wrong in humbling myself that you might be exalted--I mean because I told you God's Good News without payment.

title: II Corinthians 11:8
text: I robbed other churches by taking pay from them, so that I might serve you!

title: II Corinthians 11:9
text: And, when I was with you in need, I did not become a burden to any of you; for our Brothers, on coming from Macedonia, supplied my needs. I kept myself, and will keep myself from being an expense to you in any way.

title: II Corinthians 11:10
text: As surely as I know anything of the Truth of Christ, this boast, as far as I am concerned, shall not be stopped in any part of Greece.

title: II Corinthians 11:11
text: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows that I do!

title: II Corinthians 11:12
text: What I am doing now I shall continue to do, that I may cut away the ground from under those who are wishing for some ground for attacking me, so that as regards the thing of which they boast they may appear in their true characters, just as we do.

title: II Corinthians 11:13
text: Men of this stamp are false apostles, treacherous workers, disguising themselves as Apostles of Christ!

title: II Corinthians 11:14
text: And no wonder; for even Satan disguises himself as an angel of Light.

title: II Corinthians 11:15
text: It is not surprising, therefore, if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of Righteousness. But their end will be in accordance with their actions.

title: II Corinthians 11:16
text: I say again--Let no one think me a fool! Yet, if you do, at least welcome me as you would a fool, that I, too may indulge in a little boasting.

title: II Corinthians 11:17
