text: He rid himself of all the Powers of Evil, and held them up to open contempt, when he celebrated his triumph over them on the cross!

title: Colossians 2:16
text: Do not, then, allow any one to take you to task on questions of eating or drinking, or in the matter of annual or monthly or weekly festivals.

title: Colossians 2:17
text: These things are only the shadow of what is to come; the substance is in the Christ.

title: Colossians 2:18
text: Do not let any one defraud you of the reality by affecting delight in so-called 'humility' and angel-worship. Such a man busies himself with his visions, and without reason is rendered conceited by his merely human intellect.

title: Colossians 2:19
text: He fails to maintain union with the Head, to whom it is due that the whole body, nourished and knit together by the contact and Keynesian of every part, grows with a divine growth.

title: Colossians 2:20
text: Since, with Christ, you became dead to the puerile teaching of this world, why do you submit, as though your life were still that of the world,

title: Colossians 2:21
text: To such ordinances as 'Do not handle, or taste, or touch'?

title: Colossians 2:22
text: For all the things referred to in them cease to exist when used. You are following mere human directions and instructions.

title: Colossians 2:23
text: Such prohibitions appear reasonable where there is a desire for self-imposed service, and so-called 'humility,' and harsh treatment of the body, but are of no real value against the indulgence of our earthly nature.

title: Colossians 3:1
text: Since, therefore, you were raised to Life with the Christ, seek for the things that are above; for it is there that the Christ is 'seated at the right hand of God.'

title: Colossians 3:2
text: Fix your thoughts upon the things that are above, not upon those that are on earth.

title: Colossians 3:3
text: For you died, and your Life now lies hidden, with the Christ, in God.

title: Colossians 3:4
text: When the Christ, who is our Life, appears, then you also will appear with him in glory.

title: Colossians 3:5
text: Therefore destroy all that is earthly in you--immorality, uncleanness, passions, evil desires, and that greed which is idolatry.

title: Colossians 3:6
text: These are the things on account of which the Wrath of God comes,

title: Colossians 3:7
text: And to which you, like others, once devoted your lives, when you lived for them.

title: Colossians 3:8
text: You, however, must now lay aside all such things--anger, passion, malice, slander, abuse.

title: Colossians 3:9
text: Never lie to one another. Get rid of your old self and its habits,

title: Colossians 3:10
text: And clothe yourselves with that new self, which, as it gains in knowledge, is being constantly renewed 'in resemblance to him who made it.'

title: Colossians 3:11
text: In that new life there is no distinction between Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, freeman; but Christ is all!--and in all!

title: Colossians 3:12
text: Therefore, as God's People, consecrated and dear to him, clothe yourselves with tenderness of heart, kindliness, humility, gentleness, forbearance;

title: Colossians 3:13
text: Bearing with one another, and, when there is any ground for complaint, forgiving one another freely. As the Master freely forgave you, so you must forgive one another.

title: Colossians 3:14
text: Over all these virtues put on love; for that is the girdle which makes all complete.

title: Colossians 3:15
text: Let the Peace that the Christ gives decide all doubts within your hearts; for you also were called to the enjoyment of peace as members of one Body. And show yourselves thankful.

title: Colossians 3:16
text: Let the Message of the Christ dwell in your minds in all its wealth, bringing all wisdom with it. Teach and admonish one another with psalms, and hymns, and sacred songs, full of the loving- kindness of God, lifting your hearts in song to him.

title: Colossians 3:17
text: And, whatever you say or do, do everything in the Name of the Lord Jesus; and through him offer thanksgiving to God the father.

title: Colossians 3:18
text: Wives, submit to your husbands, as befits those who belong to the Lord.

title: Colossians 3:19
text: Husbands, love your wives, and never treat them harshly.

title: Colossians 3:20
text: Children, always obey your parents; for that is pleasant to see in those who belong to the Lord.

title: Colossians 3:21
text: Fathers, never irritate your children, lest they should become disheartened.

title: Colossians 3:22
text: Slaves, always obey your earthly masters, not only when their eyes are on you, as if you had but to please men, but giving them ungrudging service, in your reverence for the Master.

title: Colossians 3:23
text: Whatever you do, do it with all your heart, as if working for the Master and not for men,

title: Colossians 3:24
text: Since you know that it is from the Master that you will receive the inheritance which will be your recompense. You are serving Christ, the Master.

title: Colossians 3:25
text: Those who do wrong will reap the wrong they have done; and there will be no partiality.

title: Colossians 4:1
text: Masters, do what is right and fair by your slaves, for you know that you also have a Master--in Heaven.

title: Colossians 4:2
text: Devote yourselves to prayer. Give your whole mind to it, and also offer thanksgiving;

title: Colossians 4:3
text: And at the same time pray for us, that God may give us an opening for our Message, so that we may speak of the truths hidden in the Christ--the truths for which I am in chains!

title: Colossians 4:4
text: Then I shall make them known, as I ought to do.

title: Colossians 4:5
text: Show tact in your behavior to the outside world, making the most of every opportunity.

title: Colossians 4:6
text: Let your conversation always be kindly, and seasoned, as it were, with salt; that you may know in each case what answer you ought to give.

title: Colossians 4:7
text: Our dear Brother, Tychicus, will tell you all about me. He is a faithful minister, and a fellow-servant in the Master's cause.

title: Colossians 4:8
text: I send him to you expressly that you may learn our circumstances, and that he may give you encouragement.

title: Colossians 4:9
text: With him will be Onesimus, our dear faithful Brother, who is one of yourselves. They will tell you all that is going on here.

title: Colossians 4:10
text: My fellow-prisoner, Aristarchus, sends you his greeting, and Barnabas's cousin, Mark, sends his. (You have received directions about him. If he comes to you, make him welcome.)

title: Colossians 4:11
text: Joshua, who is called Justus, also sends his greeting. These are the only converts from Judaism who have worked with me for the kingdom of God; I have found them a great comfort.

title: Colossians 4:12
text: Epaphras, who is one of yourselves, sends you his greeting. He is a servant of Christ Jesus, and is always most earnest in your behalf in his prayers, praying that you may stand firm, with a matured faith and with a sure conviction of all that is in accordance with God's will.

title: Colossians 4:13
text: I can bear testimony to the deep interest he takes in you, as well as in the Brethren at Laodicea and at Hierapolis.

title: Colossians 4:14
text: Luke, our dear doctor, sends you his greeting, and Demas sends his.

title: Colossians 4:15
text: Give my greeting to the Brethren at Laodicea, and to Nymphe, and to the Church that meets at her house.

title: Colossians 4:16
text: And when this letter has been read to you, see that it is also read before the Church at Laodicea, and that you yourselves read the letter which will be forwarded from there.

title: Colossians 4:17
text: Give this message to Archippus--'Take care to discharge to the best of your ability the office to which you were appointed in the Master's Cause.'

title: Colossians 4:18
text: I, Paul, add this greeting in my own handwriting. Remember these chains of mine. God's blessing be with you.

title: I Thessalonians 1:1
text: To the Thessalonian Church in union with God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, from Paul, Silas, and Timothy. May God bless you and give you peace.

title: I Thessalonians 1:2
text: We always mention you in our prayers and thank God for you all;

title: I Thessalonians 1:3
text: Recalling continually before our God and Father the efforts that have resulted from your faith, the toil prompted by your love, and the patient endurance sustained by your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: I Thessalonians 1:4
text: Brothers, whom God loves, we know that he has chosen you,

title: I Thessalonians 1:5
text: Because the Good News that we brought came home to you, not merely as so many words, but with a power and a fulness of conviction due to the Holy Spirit. For you know the life that we lived among you for your good.

title: I Thessalonians 1:6
text: And you yourselves began to follow, not only our example, but the Master's also; and, in spite of much suffering, you welcomed the Message with a joy inspired by the Holy Spirit,

title: I Thessalonians 1:7
text: And so became a pattern to all who believed in Christ throughout Macedonia and Greece.

title: I Thessalonians 1:8
text: For it was from you that the Lord's Message resounded throughout Macedonia and Greece; and, more than that, your faith in God has become known far and wide; so that there is no need for us to say another word.

title: I Thessalonians 1:9
text: Indeed, in speaking about us, the people themselves tell of the reception you gave us, and how, turning to God from your idols, you became servants of the true and living God,

title: I Thessalonians 1:10
text: And are now awaiting the return from Heaven of his Son whom he raised from the dead--Jesus, our deliverer from the Coming Wrath.

title: I Thessalonians 2:1
text: Yes, Brothers, you yourselves know that your reception of us was not without result.

title: I Thessalonians 2:2
text: For, although we had experienced suffering and ill-treatment, as you know, at Philippi, we had the courage, by the help of our God, to tell you God's Good News in spite of great opposition.

title: I Thessalonians 2:3
text: Our appeal to you was not based on a delusion, nor was it made from unworthy motives, or with any intention of misleading you.

title: I Thessalonians 2:4
text: But, having been found worthy by God to be entrusted with the Good News, therefore we tell it; with a view to please, not men, but God who proves our hearts.

title: I Thessalonians 2:5
text: Never at any time, as you know, did we use the language of flattery, or make false professions in order to hide selfish aims. God will bear witness to that.

title: I Thessalonians 2:6
text: Nor did we seek to win honour from men, whether from you or from others, although, as Apostles of Christ, we might have burdened you with our support.

title: I Thessalonians 2:7
text: But we lived among you with the simplicity of a child; we were like a woman nursing her own children.

title: I Thessalonians 2:8
text: In our strong affection for you, that seemed to us the best way of sharing with you, not only God's Good news, but our very lives as well--so dear had you become to us.

title: I Thessalonians 2:9
text: You will not have forgotten, Brothers, our labor and toil. Night and day we used to work at our trades, so as not be a burden to any of you, while we proclaimed to you God's Good News.

title: I Thessalonians 2:10
text: You will bear witness, and God also, that our relations with you who believed in Christ were pure, and upright, and beyond reproach.

title: I Thessalonians 2:11
text: Indeed, you know that, like a father with his own children, we used to encourage and comfort every one of you, and solemnly plead with you;

title: I Thessalonians 2:12
text: So that you should make your daily lives worthy of God who is calling you into the glory of his Kingdom.

title: I Thessalonians 2:13
text: This, too, is a reason why we, on our part, are continually thanking God--because, in receiving the teaching that you had from us, you accepted it, not as the teaching of man, but as what it really is--the teaching of God, which is even now doing its work within you who believe in Christ.

title: I Thessalonians 2:14
text: For you, Brothers, began to follow the example of the Churches of God in Judea which are in union with Jesus Christ; you, in your turn, suffering at the hands of your fellow-citizens, in the same way as those Churches did at the hands of the Jews--

title: I Thessalonians 2:15
text: The men who killed both the Lord Jesus and the Prophets, and persecuted us also. They do not try to please God, and they are enemies to all mankind,

title: I Thessalonians 2:16
text: For they would prevent us from speaking to the Gentiles with a view to their Salvation, and thus are always 'filling up the measure of their iniquity.' But the Wrath of God has come upon them to the full!

title: I Thessalonians 2:17
text: As for ourselves, Brothers, our having been bereaved of you even for a short time--though in body only, and not in spirit--made us all the more eager to see your faces again; and the longing to do so was strong upon us.

title: I Thessalonians 2:18
text: That was why we made up our minds to go and see you--at least I, Paul, did, more than once--but Satan put difficulties in our way.

title: I Thessalonians 2:19
text: For what hope or joy will be ours, or what crown shall we have to boast of, in the presence of our Lord Jesus, at his Coming, if it be not you?

title: I Thessalonians 2:20
text: You are our pride and our delight!

title: I Thessalonians 3:1
text: And so, as we could bear it no longer, we made up our minds to remain behind alone at Athens,

title: I Thessalonians 3:2
text: And sent Timothy, our Brother and God's minister of the Good News of the Christ, to strengthen you, and to encourage you in your faith,

title: I Thessalonians 3:3
text: So that none of you should be shaken by the troubles through which you are passing. You yourselves know that we are destined to meet with such things.

title: I Thessalonians 3:4
text: For, even while we were with you, we warned you beforehand that we were certain to encounter trouble. And so it proved, as you know.

title: I Thessalonians 3:5
text: Therefore, since I could no longer endure the uncertainty, I sent to make inquiries about your faith, fearing that the Tempter had tempted you, and that our toil might prove to have been in vain.

title: I Thessalonians 3:6
text: But, when Timothy recently returned to us from you with good news of your faith and love, and told us how kindly you think of us--always longing, he said, to see us, just as we are longing to see you--

title: I Thessalonians 3:7
text: On hearing his, we felt encouraged about you, Brothers, in the midst of all our difficulties and troubles, by your faith.

title: I Thessalonians 3:8
text: For it is new life to us to know that you are holding fast to the Lord.

title: I Thessalonians 3:9
text: How can we thank God enough for all the happiness that you are giving us in the sight of our God?

title: I Thessalonians 3:10
text: Night and day we pray most earnestly that we may see you face to face, and make good any deficiency in your faith.

title: I Thessalonians 3:11
text: May our God and Father himself, and Jesus, our Lord, make the way plain for us to come to you.

title: I Thessalonians 3:12
text: And for you, may the Lord fill you to overflowing with love for one another and for every one, just as we are filled with love for you;

title: I Thessalonians 3:13
text: And so make your hearts strong, and your lives pure beyond reproach, in the sight of our God and Father, at the Coming of our Lord Jesus, with all his Holy Ones.

title: I Thessalonians 4:1
text: Further, Brothers, we beg and exhort you in the name of our Lord Jesus to carry out more fully than ever--as indeed you are already doing--all that you have heard from us as to what your daily life must be, if it is to please God.

title: I Thessalonians 4:2
text: For you have not forgotten the directions that we gave you on the authority of our Lord Jesus.

title: I Thessalonians 4:3
text: For this is God's purpose--that you should be pure; abstaining from all immorality;

title: I Thessalonians 4:4
text: Each of you recognizing the duty of taking one woman for his wife, purely and honorably,

title: I Thessalonians 4:5
text: And not for the mere gratification of his passions, like the Gentiles who know nothing of God;

title: I Thessalonians 4:6
text: None of you over-reaching or taking advantage of his Brother in such matters. 'The Lord takes vengeance' upon all who do such things, as we have already warned you and solemnly declared.

title: I Thessalonians 4:7
text: For God's Call to us does not permit of an impure life, but demands purity.

title: I Thessalonians 4:8
text: Therefore he who disregards this warning disregards, not man, but God who gives you his Holy Spirit.

title: I Thessalonians 4:9
text: As to love for the Brethren there is no need to write to you; for you have yourselves been taught by God to love one another;

title: I Thessalonians 4:10
text: And indeed you do act in this spirit towards all the Brethren throughout Macedonia. Yet, Brothers, we urge you to still further efforts.

title: I Thessalonians 4:11
text: Make it your ambition to live quietly, and to attend to your own business, and to work with your hands, as we directed you;

title: I Thessalonians 4:12
text: So that your conduct may win respect from those outside the Church, and that you may not want for anything.

title: I Thessalonians 4:13
text: We do not wish you to remain in ignorance, Brothers, with regard to those who have passed to their rest, that your grief may not be like that of others, who have no hope.

title: I Thessalonians 4:14
text: For, as we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also we believe that God will bring, with Jesus, those who through him have passed to their rest.

title: I Thessalonians 4:15
text: This we tell you on the authority of the Lord--that those of us who are still living at the Coming of the Lord will not anticipate those who have passed to their rest.

title: I Thessalonians 4:16
text: For, with a loud summons, with the shout of an archangel, and with the trumpet-call of God, the Lord himself will come down from Heaven.

title: I Thessalonians 4:17
text: Then those who died in union with Christ shall rise first; and afterwards we who are still living shall be caught up in the clouds, with them, to meet the Lord in the air; and so we shall be for ever with the Lord.

title: I Thessalonians 4:18
text: Therefore, comfort one another with what I have told you.

title: I Thessalonians 5:1
text: But as to the times and the moments, there is no need, Brothers, for any one to write to you.

title: I Thessalonians 5:2
text: You yourselves know well that the Day of the Lord will come just as a thief comes in the night.

title: I Thessalonians 5:3
text: When people are saying 'All is quiet and safe,' it is then that, like birth-pains upon a woman with child, Ruin comes suddenly upon them, and there will be no escape!

title: I Thessalonians 5:4
text: You, however, Brothers, are not in darkness, that the daylight should take you by surprise as if you were thieves.

title: I Thessalonians 5:5
text: For you all are 'Sons of Light' and 'Sons of the Day.' We have nothing to do with night, or darkness.

title: I Thessalonians 5:6
text: Therefore let us not sleep as others do. No, let us be watchful and self-controlled.

title: I Thessalonians 5:7
text: It is at night that men sleep, and at night that drunkards get drunk.

title: I Thessalonians 5:8
text: But let us, who belong to the Day, control ourselves, and put on faith and love as a breast plate, and the hope of Salvation as a helmet.

title: I Thessalonians 5:9
text: For God destined us, not for Wrath, but to win Salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, who died for us,

title: I Thessalonians 5:10
text: That, whether we are still watching or have fallen asleep, we may live with him.

title: I Thessalonians 5:11
text: Therefore encourage one another, and try to build up one another's characters, as indeed you are doing.

title: I Thessalonians 5:12
text: We beg you, Brothers, to value those who toil among you, and are your leaders in the Lord's service, and give you counsel.

title: I Thessalonians 5:13
text: Hold them in the very greatest esteem and affection for the sake of their work. Live at peace with one another.

title: I Thessalonians 5:14
text: We entreat you also, Brothers--warn the disorderly, comfort the faint-hearted, give a helping hand to the weak, and be patient with every one.

title: I Thessalonians 5:15
text: Take care that none of you ever pays back wrong for wrong, but always follow the kindest course with one another and with every one.

title: I Thessalonians 5:16
text: Always be joyful;

title: I Thessalonians 5:17
text: Never cease to pray;

title: I Thessalonians 5:18
text: Under all circumstances give thanks to God. For this is his will for you as made known in Christ Jesus.

title: I Thessalonians 5:19
text: Do not quench the Spirit;

title: I Thessalonians 5:20
text: Do not make light of preaching.

title: I Thessalonians 5:21
text: Bring everything to the test; cling to what is good;

title: I Thessalonians 5:22
text: Shun every form of evil.

title: I Thessalonians 5:23
text: May God himself, the giver of peace, make you altogether holy; and may your spirits, souls, and bodies be kept altogether faultless until the Coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: I Thessalonians 5:24
text: He who calls you will not fail you; he will complete his work.

title: I Thessalonians 5:25
text: Brothers, pray for us.

title: I Thessalonians 5:26
text: Greet all the Brothers with a sacred kiss.

title: I Thessalonians 5:27
text: I adjure you in the Lord's name to have this letter read to all the Brethren.

title: I Thessalonians 5:28
text: May the blessing of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

title: II Thessalonians 1:1
text: To the Thessalonian Church in union with God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, From Paul, Silas, and Timothy.

title: II Thessalonians 1:2
text: May God, the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ bless you and give you peace.

title: II Thessalonians 1:3
text: Brothers, it is our duty always to thank God about you, as is but right, considering the wonderful growth of your faith, and because, without exception, your love for one another is continually increasing.

title: II Thessalonians 1:4
text: So much is this the case that we ourselves speak with pride, before the Churches of God, of the patience and faith which you have shown, in spite of all the persecutions and troubles that you are enduring.

title: II Thessalonians 1:5
text: These persecutions will vindicate the justice of God's judgement, and will result in your being reckoned worthy of God's Kingdom, for the sake of which you are now afflicted;

title: II Thessalonians 1:6
text: Since God deems it just to inflict suffering upon those who are now inflicting suffering upon you,

title: II Thessalonians 1:7
text: And to give relief to you who are suffering, as well as to us, at the Appearing of the Lord Jesus from Heaven with his mighty angels, 'in flaming fire.'

title: II Thessalonians 1:8
text: Then he will 'inflict punishment upon those who refuse to know God, and upon those who turn a deaf ear' to the Good News of Jesus, our Lord.

title: II Thessalonians 1:9
text: These men will pay the penalty of unutterable Ruin--banished 'from the presence of the Lord and from the glorious manifestation of his might,

title: II Thessalonians 1:10
text: When he comes to be honour ed in his People,' and to be revered in all who have learned to believe in him (for you also believed our testimony)--as he will be on 'That Day.'

title: II Thessalonians 1:11
text: With this in view, our constant prayer for you is that our God may count you worthy of the Call that you have received, and by his power make perfect your delight in all goodness and the efforts that have resulted from your faith.

title: II Thessalonians 1:12
text: Then, in the loving-kindness of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ, will the name of Jesus, our Lord, be honour ed in you, and you in him.

title: II Thessalonians 2:1
text: As to the Coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and our being gathered to meet him, we beg you, Brothers,

title: II Thessalonians 2:2
text: Not lightly to let your minds become unsettled, nor yet to be disturbed by any revelation, or by any message, or by any letter, purporting to come from us, to the effect that the Day of the Lord is come.

title: II Thessalonians 2:3
text: Do not let any one deceive you, whatever he may do. For it will not come until after the Great Apostasy, and the appearing of that Incarnation of Wickedness, that the Lost soul,

title: II Thessalonians 2:4
text: Who so opposes himself to every one that is spoken of as a God or as an object of worship, and so exalts himself above them, that he seats himself in the Temple of God, and displays himself as God!

title: II Thessalonians 2:5
text: Do not you remember how, when I was with you, I used to speak to you of all this?

title: II Thessalonians 2:6
text: And you know now what the restraining influence is which prevents his appearing before his appointed time.

title: II Thessalonians 2:7
text: Wickedness, indeed, is already at work in secret; but only until he who at present restrains it is removed out of the way.

title: II Thessalonians 2:8
text: Then will 'Wickedness Incarnate' appear, but the Lord Jesus will destroy him with the breath of his lips, and annihilate him by the splendor of his Coming.

title: II Thessalonians 2:9
text: For at the Coming of the Lord there will be great activity on the part of Satan, in the form of all kinds of deceptive miracles, signs, and marvels, as well as of wicked attempts to delude--

title: II Thessalonians 2:10
text: to the ruin of those who are on the path to destruction, because they have never received and loved the Truth to their own Salvation.

title: II Thessalonians 2:11
text: That is why God places them under the influence of a delusion, to cause them to believe a lie;

title: II Thessalonians 2:12
text: So that sentence may be passed on all those who refuse to believe the Truth, but delight in wickedness.

title: II Thessalonians 2:13
text: But, Brothers, whom the Lord loves, it is our duty always to thank God about you, for, from the first, God chose you for Salvation through the purifying influence of the Spirit, and your belief in the Truth.

title: II Thessalonians 2:14
text: To this you were called by the Good News which we brought you, to attain to the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: II Thessalonians 2:15
text: Stand firm then, Brothers, and hold fast to the truths that we taught you, whether by word or by letter.

title: II Thessalonians 2:16
text: And may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and, in his loving-kindness, gave us unfailing consolation and good ground for hope,

title: II Thessalonians 2:17
text: Console your hearts, and strengthen you to do and to say all that is right.

title: II Thessalonians 3:1
text: In conclusion, Brothers, pray for us--pray that the Lord's Message may spread rapidly, and be received everywhere with honour, as it was among you;

title: II Thessalonians 3:2
text: And that we may be preserved from wrong-headed and wicked men- -for it is not every one who believes in Christ.

title: II Thessalonians 3:3
text: But the Lord will not fail you; he will give you strength, and guard you from Evil.

title: II Thessalonians 3:4
text: Yes, and the confidence that our union with the Lord enables us to place in you leads us to believe that you are doing, and will do, what we direct you.

title: II Thessalonians 3:5
text: May the Lord bring you to the love of God, and to the patience of the Christ.

title: II Thessalonians 3:6
text: We urge you, Brothers, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, to avoid any Brother who is living an ill-ordered life, which is not in agreement with the teaching that you received from us.

title: II Thessalonians 3:7
text: For you know well that you ought to follow our example. When we were with you, our life was not ill-ordered,

title: II Thessalonians 3:8
text: Nor did we eat any one's bread without paying for it. Night and day, laboring and toiling, we used to work at our trades, so as not to be a burden upon any of you.

title: II Thessalonians 3:9
text: This was not because we had not a right to receive support, but our object was to give you a pattern for you to copy.

title: II Thessalonians 3:10
text: Indeed, when we were with you, what we urged upon you was-- 'If a man does not choose to work, then he shall not eat.'

title: II Thessalonians 3:11
text: We hear that there are among you people who are living ill- ordered lives, and who, instead of attending to their own business, are mere busy-bodies.

title: II Thessalonians 3:12
text: All such people we urge, and entreat, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, to attend quietly to their business, and earn their own living.

title: II Thessalonians 3:13
text: You, Brothers, must not grow weary of doing what is right.

title: II Thessalonians 3:14
text: If any one disregards what we have said in this letter, mark that man and avoid his company, that he may feel ashamed.

title: II Thessalonians 3:15
text: Yet do not think of him as an enemy, but caution him as you would a Brother.

title: II Thessalonians 3:16
text: May the Lord, from whom all peace comes, himself give you his peace at all times and in all ways. May he be with you all.

title: II Thessalonians 3:17
text: I, Paul, add this greeting in my own handwriting. It is my signature to every letter. This is how I write.

title: II Thessalonians 3:18
text: May the blessing of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.

title: I Timothy 1:1
text: From Paul, an Apostle of Christ Jesus by the appointment of God, our Savior, and Christ Jesus, our Hope.

title: I Timothy 1:2
text: To Timothy, my true Child in the Faith: May God, the Father, and Christ Jesus, our Lord, bless you, and be merciful to you, and give you peace.

title: I Timothy 1:3
text: I beg you, as I did when I was on my way into Macedonia, to remain at Ephesus; that you may instruct certain people there not to teach new and strange doctrines,

title: I Timothy 1:4
text: nor to devote their attention to legends and interminable genealogies, which tend to give rise to argument rather than to further that divine plan which is revealed in the Faith.

title: I Timothy 1:5
text: The object of all instruction is to call forth that love which comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and a sincere faith.

title: I Timothy 1:6
text: And it is because they have not aimed at these things that the attention of certain people has been diverted to unprofitable subjects.

title: I Timothy 1:7
text: They want to be Teachers of the Law, and yet do not understand either the words they use, or the subjects on which they speak so confidently.

title: I Timothy 1:8
text: We know, of course, that the Law is excellent, when used legitimately,

title: I Timothy 1:9
text: by one who recognizes that laws were not made for good men, but for the lawless and disorderly, for irreligious and wicked people, for those who are irreverent and profane, for those who ill-treat their fathers or mothers, for murderers,

title: I Timothy 1:10
text: for the immoral, for people guilty of sodomy, for slave-dealers, for liars, for perjurers, and for whatever else is opposed to sound Christian teaching--

title: I Timothy 1:11
text: as is taught in the glorious Good News of the ever-blessed God, with which I was entrusted.

title: I Timothy 1:12
text: I am thankful to Christ Jesus, our Lord, who has been my strength, for showing that he thought me worthy of trust by appointing me to his ministry,

title: I Timothy 1:13
text: though I once used to blaspheme, and to persecute, and to insult. Yet mercy was shown me, because I acted in ignorance, while still an unbeliever;

title: I Timothy 1:14
text: and the loving-kindness of our Lord was boundless, and filled me with that faith and love which come from union with Christ Jesus.

title: I Timothy 1:15
text: How true the saying is, and worthy of the fullest acceptance, that 'Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners'! And there is no greater sinner than I!

title: I Timothy 1:16
text: Yet mercy was shown me for the express purpose that Christ Jesus might exhibit in my case, beyond all others, his exhaustless patience, as an example for those who were afterwards to believe on him and attain Immortal Life.

title: I Timothy 1:17
text: To the Immortal King, ever-living, invisible, the one God, be ascribed honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

title: I Timothy 1:18
text: This, then, is the charge that I lay upon you, Timothy, my Child, in accordance with what was predicted of you--Fight the good fight in the spirit of those predictions,

title: I Timothy 1:19
text: with faith, and with a clear conscience; and it is because they have thrust this aside, that, as regards the Faith, some have wrecked their lives.

title: I Timothy 1:20
text: Hymenaeus and Alexander are instances--the men whom I delivered over to Satan, that they might be taught not to blaspheme.

title: I Timothy 2:1
text: First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings should be offered for every one,

title: I Timothy 2:2
text: especially for kings and all who are in high positions, in order that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in a deeply religious and reverent spirit.

title: I Timothy 2:3
text: This will be good and acceptable in the eyes of God, our Savior,

title: I Timothy 2:4
text: whose will is that every one should be saved, and attain to a full knowledge of the Truth.

title: I Timothy 2:5
text: There is but one God, and one mediator between God and men--the man, Christ Jesus,

title: I Timothy 2:6
text: who gave himself as a ransom on behalf of all men. This must be our testimony, as opportunities present themselves;

title: I Timothy 2:7
text: and it was for this that I was myself appointed a Herald and an Apostle (I am telling the simple truth and no lie)--a Teacher of the Gentiles in the Faith and Truth.

title: I Timothy 2:8
text: My desire, then, is that it should be the custom everywhere for the men to lead the prayers, with hands reverently uplifted, avoiding heated controversy.

title: I Timothy 2:9
text: I also desire that women should adorn themselves with appropriate dress, worn quietly and modestly, and not with wreaths or gold ornaments for the hair, or pearls, or costly clothing,

title: I Timothy 2:10
text: but--as is proper for women who profess to be religious--with good actions.

title: I Timothy 2:11
text: A woman should listen silently to her teachers, and show them all deference.

title: I Timothy 2:12
text: I do not consent to a woman's becoming a teacher, or exercising authority over a man; she ought to be silent.

title: I Timothy 2:13
text: Adam was formed first, not Eve.

title: I Timothy 2:14
text: And it was not Adam who was deceived; it was the woman who was entirely deceived and fell into sin.

title: I Timothy 2:15
text: But women will find their salvation in motherhood, if they never abandon faith, love, or holiness, and behave with modesty.

title: I Timothy 3:1
text: How true is that saying! When a man aspires to be a Presiding-Officer in the Church, he is ambitious for a noble task.

title: I Timothy 3:2
text: The Presiding-Officer should be a man of blameless character; a faithful husband; living a temperate, discreet, and well-ordered life; hospitable, and a skillful teacher,

title: I Timothy 3:3
text: not addicted to drink or brawling, but of a forbearing and peaceable disposition, and not a lover of money;

title: I Timothy 3:4
text: he should be a man who rules his own household well, and whose children are kept under control and are well-behaved.

title: I Timothy 3:5
text: If a man does not know how to rule his own household, how can he take charge of the Church of God?

title: I Timothy 3:6
text: The Presiding-Officer should not be a recent convert, that he may not be blinded by pride and fall under the same condemnation as the Devil.

title: I Timothy 3:7
text: He should also be well spoken of by outsiders, that he may not incur censure and so fall into the snares of the Devil.

title: I Timothy 3:8
text: So, too, Assistant-Officers should be serious and straightforward men, not given to taking much drink or to questionable money-making,

title: I Timothy 3:9
text: but men who hold the deep truths of the Faith and have a clear conscience.

title: I Timothy 3:10
text: They should be tested first, and only appointed to their Office if no objection is raised against them.

title: I Timothy 3:11
text: It should be the same with the women. They should be serious, not gossips, sober, and trustworthy in all respects.

title: I Timothy 3:12
text: Assistant-Officers should be faithful husbands, and men who rule their children and their households well.

title: I Timothy 3:13
text: Those who have filled that post with honour gain for themselves an honorable position, as well as great confidence through the faith that they place in Christ Jesus.

title: I Timothy 3:14
text: I am writing this to you, though I hope that I shall come to see you before long;

title: I Timothy 3:15
text: but in case I should be delayed, I want you to know what your conduct ought to be in the Household of God, which is the Church of the Living God--the pillar and stay of the Truth.

title: I Timothy 3:16
text: Yes, and confessedly wonderful are the deep truths of our religion; for-- 'He was revealed in our nature, pronounced righteous in spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the Gentiles, believed on in the world, taken up into glory.'

title: I Timothy 4:1
text: But the Spirit distinctly says that in later times there will be some who will fall away from the Faith, and devote their attention to misleading spirits, and to the teaching of demons,

title: I Timothy 4:2
text: who will make use of the hypocrisy of lying teachers. These men's consciences are seared,

title: I Timothy 4:3
text: and they discourage marriage and enjoin abstinence from certain kinds of food; though God created these foods to be enjoyed thankfully by those who hold the Faith and have attained a full knowledge of the Truth.

title: I Timothy 4:4
text: Everything created by God is good, and there in nothing that need be rejected--provided only that it is received thankfully;

title: I Timothy 4:5
text: for it is consecrated by God's blessing and by prayer.

title: I Timothy 4:6
text: Put all this before the Brethren, and you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, sustained by the precepts of the Faith and of that Good Teaching by which you have guided your life.

title: I Timothy 4:7
text: As for profane legends and old wives' tales, leave them alone. Train yourself to lead a religious life;

title: I Timothy 4:8
text: for while the training of the body is of service in some respects, religion is of service in all, carrying with it, as it does, a promise of Life both here and hereafter.

title: I Timothy 4:9
text: How true that saying is and worthy of the fullest acceptance!

title: I Timothy 4:10
text: With that aim we toil and struggle, for we have set our hopes on the Living God, who is the Savior of all men, and especially of those who hold the Faith.

title: I Timothy 4:11
text: Dwell upon these things in your teaching.

title: I Timothy 4:12
text: Do not let any one look down on you because you are young, but, by your conversation, your conduct, your love, your faith, and your purity, be an example to those who hold the Faith.

title: I Timothy 4:13
text: Till I come, apply yourself to public reading, preaching, and teaching.

title: I Timothy 4:14
text: Do not neglect the divine gift within you, which was given you, amid many a prediction, when the hands of the Officers of the Church were laid on your head.

title: I Timothy 4:15
text: Practice these things, devote yourself to them, so that your progress may be plain to every one.

title: I Timothy 4:16
text: Look to yourself as well as to your teaching. Persevere in this, for your doing so will mean Salvation for yourself as well as for your hearers.

title: I Timothy 5:1
text: Do not reprimand an older man, but plead with him as if he were your father. Treat the young men as brothers,

title: I Timothy 5:2
text: the older women as mothers, and the younger women as sisters--with all purity.

title: I Timothy 5:3
text: Show consideration for widows--I mean those who are really widowed.

title: I Timothy 5:4
text: but, if a widow has children or grand-children, let them learn to show proper regard for the members of their own family first, and to make some return to their parents; for that is pleasing in God's sight.

title: I Timothy 5:5
text: As for the woman who is really widowed and left quite alone, her hopes are fixed on God, and she devotes herself to prayers and supplications night and day.

title: I Timothy 5:6
text: But the life of a widow who is devoted to pleasure is a living death.

title: I Timothy 5:7
text: Those are the points on which you should dwell, that there may be no call for your censure.

title: I Timothy 5:8
text: Any one who fails to provide for his own relations, and especially for those under his own roof, has disowned the Faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.

title: I Timothy 5:9
text: A widow, when her name is added to the list, should not be less than sixty years old; she should have been a faithful wife,

title: I Timothy 5:10
text: and be well spoken of for her kind actions. She should have brought up children, have shown hospitality to strangers, have washed the feet of her fellow Christians, have relieved those who were in distress, and devoted herself to every kind of good action.

title: I Timothy 5:11
text: But you should exclude the younger widows from the list; for, when they grow restive under the yoke of the Christ, they want to marry,

title: I Timothy 5:12
text: and so they bring condemnation upon themselves for having broken their previous promise.

title: I Timothy 5:13
text: And not only that, but they learn to be idle as they go about from house to house. Nor are they merely idle, but they also become gossips and busy-bodies, and talk of what they ought not.

title: I Timothy 5:14
text: Therefore I advise young widows to marry, bear children, and attend to their homes, and so avoid giving the enemy an opportunity for scandal.

title: I Timothy 5:15
text: There are some who have already left us, to follow Satan.

title: I Timothy 5:16
text: Any Christian woman, who has relations who are widows, ought to relieve them and not allow them to become a burden to the Church, so that the Church may relieve those widows who are really widowed.

title: I Timothy 5:17
text: Those Officers of the Church who fill their office well should be held deserving of especial consideration, particularly those whose work lies in preaching and teaching.

title: I Timothy 5:18
text: The words of Scripture are-- 'Thou shalt not muzzle the ox while it is treading out the grain.' and again-- 'The worker is worth his wages.'

title: I Timothy 5:19
text: Do not receive a charge against an Officer of the Church, unless it is supported by two or three witnesses;

title: I Timothy 5:20
text: but rebuke offenders publicly, so that others may take warning.

title: I Timothy 5:21
text: I charge you solemnly, before God and Christ Jesus and the Chosen Angels, to carry out these directions, unswayed by prejudice, never acting with partiality.

title: I Timothy 5:22
text: Never ordain any one hastily, and take no part in the wrong-doing of others. Keep your life pure.

title: I Timothy 5:23
text: Do not continue to drink water only, but take a little wine on account of the weakness of your stomach, and your frequent ailments.

title: I Timothy 5:24
text: There are some men whose sins are conspicuous and lead on to judgement, while there are others whose sins dog their steps.

title: I Timothy 5:25
text: In the same way noble deeds become conspicuous, and those which are otherwise cannot be concealed.

title: I Timothy 6:1
text: All who are in the position of slaves should regard their masters as deserving of the greatest respect, so that the Name of God, and our Teaching, may not be maligned.

title: I Timothy 6:2
text: Those who have Christian masters should not think less of them because they are their Brothers, but on the contrary they should serve them all the better, because those who are to benefit by their good work are dear to them as their fellow Christians. Those are the things to insist upon in your teaching.

title: I Timothy 6:3
text: Any one who teaches otherwise, and refuses his assent to sound instruction--the instruction of our Lord Jesus Christ--and to the teaching of religion,

title: I Timothy 6:4
text: is puffed up with conceit, not really knowing anything, but having a morbid craving for discussions and arguments. Such things only give rise to envy, quarreling, recriminations, base suspicions,

title: I Timothy 6:5
text: and incessant wrangling on the part of these corrupt-minded people who have lost all hold on the Truth, and who think of religion only as a source of gain.

title: I Timothy 6:6
text: And a great source of gain religion is, when it brings contentment with it!

title: I Timothy 6:7
text: For we brought nothing into the world, because we cannot even carry anything out of it.

title: I Timothy 6:8
text: So, with food and shelter, we will be content.

title: I Timothy 6:9
text: Those who want to be rich fall into the snares of temptation, and become the prey of many foolish and harmful ambitions, which plunge people into Destruction and Ruin.

title: I Timothy 6:10
text: Love of money is a source of all kinds of evil; and in their eagerness to be rich some have wandered away from the Faith, and have been pierced to the heart by many a regret.

title: I Timothy 6:11
text: But do you, Servant of God, avoid all this. Aim at righteousness, piety, faith, love, endurance, gentleness.

title: I Timothy 6:12
text: Run the great race of the Faith, and win the Immortal Life. It was for this that you received the Call, and, in the presence of many witnesses, made the great profession of Faith.

title: I Timothy 6:13
text: I urge you, as in the sight of God, the source of all life, and of Christ Jesus who before Pontius Pilate made the great profession of Faith--

title: I Timothy 6:14
text: I urge you to keep his Command free from stain or reproach, until the Appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

title: I Timothy 6:15
text: This will be brought about in his own time by the one ever-blessed Potentate, the King of all kings and Lord of all lords,

title: I Timothy 6:16
text: who alone is possessed of immortality and dwells in unapproachable light, whom no man has ever seen or ever can see--to whom be ascribed honour and power for ever. Amen.

title: I Timothy 6:17
text: Urge upon those who are wealthy in this life not to pride themselves, or fix their hopes, on so uncertain a thing as wealth, but on God, who gives us a wealth of enjoyment on every side.

title: I Timothy 6:18
text: Urge upon them to show kindness, to exhibit a wealth of good actions, to be open-handed and generous,

title: I Timothy 6:19
text: storing up for themselves what in the future will prove to be a good foundation, that they may gain the only true Life.

title: I Timothy 6:20
text: Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Avoid the profane prattle and contradictions of what some miscall 'theology,'

title: I Timothy 6:21
text: for there are those who, while asserting their proficiency in it, have yet, as regards the Faith, gone altogether astray. God bless you all.

title: II Timothy 1:1
text: -2 To Timothy, my dear Child, from Paul who, by the will of God, is an Apostle of Christ Jesus, charged to proclaim the Life that comes from union with Christ Jesus. May God , the Father, and Christ Jesus, our Lord, bless you, and be merciful to you, and give you peace.

title: II Timothy 1:3
text: I am thankful to God, whom I serve, as my ancestors did, with a clear conscience, when I remember you, as I never fail to do, in my prayers--night and day alike,

title: II Timothy 1:4
text: as I think of your tears, longing to see you, that my happiness may be completed,

title: II Timothy 1:5
text: now that I have been reminded of the sincere faith that you have shown. That faith was seen first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and is now, I am convinced, in you also.

title: II Timothy 1:6
text: And that is my reason for reminding you to stir into flame that gift of God, which is yours through your ordination at my hands.

title: II Timothy 1:7
text: For the Spirit which God gave us was not a spirit of cowardice, but a spirit of power, love, and self-control.

title: II Timothy 1:8
text: Do not, therefore, be ashamed of the testimony which we have to bear to our Lord, nor yet of me who am a prisoner for him; but join with me in suffering for the Good News, as far as God enables you.

title: II Timothy 1:9
text: It was God who saved us, and from him we received our solemn Call--not as a reward for anything that we had done, but in fulfilment of his own loving purpose. For that love was extended to us, through Christ Jesus, before time began,

title: II Timothy 1:10
text: and has now been made apparent through the Appearing of our Saviour, Christ Jesus; who has made an end of Death, and has brought Life and Immortality to light by that Good News,

title: II Timothy 1:11
text: of which I was myself appointed a Herald and Apostle, and Teacher.

title: II Timothy 1:12
text: That is why I am undergoing these sufferings; yet I feel no shame, for I know in whom I have put my faith, and am convinced that he is able to guard what I have entrusted to him until 'That Day.'

title: II Timothy 1:13
text: Keep before you, as an example of sound teaching, all that you learnt from me as you listened with that faith and love which come from union with Christ Jesus.

title: II Timothy 1:14
text: Guard by the help of the Holy Spirit, who is within us, the glorious trust that has been committed to you.

title: II Timothy 1:15
text: You know, of course, that all our friends in Roman Asia turned their backs on me, and among them Phygellus and Hermogenes.

title: II Timothy 1:16
text: May the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus; for he often cheered me and was not ashamed of my chains.

title: II Timothy 1:17
text: On the contrary, when he arrived in Rome, he sought eagerly for me till he found me.

title: II Timothy 1:18
text: The Lord grant that he may find mercy at the hands of the Lord on 'That Day.' The many services that he rendered at Ephesus you have the best means of knowing.

title: II Timothy 2:1
text: Do you, then, my Child, find strength in the help which comes from the union with Christ Jesus;

title: II Timothy 2:2
text: and what you learnt from me, in the presence of many listeners, entrust to reliable men, who will be able in their turn to teach others.

title: II Timothy 2:3
text: Share hardships with me, as a true soldier of Christ Jesus.

title: II Timothy 2:4
text: A soldier on active service, to please his superior officer, always avoids entangling himself in the affairs of ordinary life.

title: II Timothy 2:5
text: No athlete is ever awarded the wreath of victory unless he has kept the rules.

title: II Timothy 2:6
text: The labourer who does the work should be the first to receive a share of the fruits of the earth.

title: II Timothy 2:7
text: Reflect upon what I say; the Lord will always help you to understand.

title: II Timothy 2:8
text: Keep before your mind Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, a descendant of David, as told in the Good News entrusted to me;

title: II Timothy 2:9
text: in the service of which I am suffering hardships, even to being put in fetters as a criminal. But the Message of God is not fettered;

title: II Timothy 2:10
text: and that is why I submit to anything for the sake of God's People, that they also may obtain the Salvation which comes from union with Christ Jesus, and imperishable glory.

title: II Timothy 2:11
text: How true this saying is-- 'If we have shared his death, we shall also share his life.

title: II Timothy 2:12
text: If we continue to endure, we shall also share his throne. If we should ever disown him, he, too, will disown us.

title: II Timothy 2:13
text: If we lose our trust, he is still to be trusted, for he cannot be false to himself!'

title: II Timothy 2:14
text: Remind people of all this; urge them solemnly, as in the sight of God, to avoid controversy, a useless thing and the ruin of those who listen to it.

title: II Timothy 2:15
text: Do your utmost to show yourself true to God, a workman with no reason to be ashamed, accurate in delivering the Message of the Truth.

title: II Timothy 2:16
text: Avoid profane prattle. Those who indulge in it only get deeper into irreligious ways,

title: II Timothy 2:17
text: and their teaching will spread like a cancer. Hymenaeus and Philetus are instances of this.

title: II Timothy 2:18
text: They have gone completely astray as regards the Truth; they say that a resurrection has already taken place, and so upset some people's faith.

title: II Timothy 2:19
text: Yet God's firm foundation still stands unmoved, and it bears this inscription-- 'THE LORD KNOWS THOSE WHO ARE HIS'; and this-- 'LET ALL THOSE WHO USE THE NAME OF THE LORD TURN AWAY FROM WICKEDNESS.'

title: II Timothy 2:20
text: Now in a large house there are not only things of gold and silver, but also others of wood and earthenware, some for better and some for common use.

title: II Timothy 2:21
text: If, then, a man has escaped from the pollution of such errors as I have mentioned, he will be like a thing kept for better use, set apart, serviceable to its owner, ready for any good purpose.

title: II Timothy 2:22
text: Flee from the passions of youth, but pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, in the company of those who, with a pure heart, invoke the Lord.

title: II Timothy 2:23
text: Shun foolish and ignorant discussions, for you know that they only breed quarrels;

title: II Timothy 2:24
text: and a Servant of the Lord should never quarrel. He ought, on the contrary, to be courteous to every one, a skillful teacher, and forbearing.

title: II Timothy 2:25
text: He should instruct his opponents in a gentle spirit; for, possibly, God may give them a repentance that will lead to a fuller knowledge of Truth,

title: II Timothy 2:26
text: and they may yet come to a sober mind, and escape from the snares of the Devil, when captured by the Lord's Servant to do the will of God.

title: II Timothy 3:1
text: Be sure of this, that in the last days difficult times will come.

title: II Timothy 3:2
text: Men will be selfish, mercenary, boastful, haughty, and blasphemous; disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, impure,

title: II Timothy 3:3
text: incapable of affection, merciless, slanderous, wanting in self-control, brutal, careless of the right,

title: II Timothy 3:4
text: treacherous, reckless, and puffed up with pride; they will love pleasure more than they love God;

title: II Timothy 3:5
text: and while they retain the outward form of religion, they will not allow it to influence them. Turn your back on such men as these.

title: II Timothy 3:6
text: For among them are to be found those who creep into homes and captivate weak women--women who, loaded with sins, and slaves to all kinds of passions,

title: II Timothy 3:7
text: are always learning, and yet never able to attain to a real knowledge of the Truth.

title: II Timothy 3:8
text: Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so do these people, in their turn, oppose the Truth. Their minds are corrupted, and, as regards the Faith, they are utterly worthless.

title: II Timothy 3:9
text: They will not, however, make further progress; for their wicked folly will be plain to every one, just as that of Jannes and Jambres was.

title: II Timothy 3:10
text: But you, Timothy, were a close observer of my teaching, my conduct, my purposes, my faith, my forbearance, my love, and my patient endurance,

title: II Timothy 3:11
text: as well as of my persecutions, and of the sufferings which I met with at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. You know what persecutions I underwent; and yet the Lord brought me safe out of all!

title: II Timothy 3:12
text: Yes, and all who aim at living a religious life in union with Christ Jesus will have to suffer persecution;

title: II Timothy 3:13
text: but wicked people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving others and deceived themselves.

title: II Timothy 3:14
text: You, however, must stand by what you learnt and accepted as true. You know who they were from whom you learnt it;

title: II Timothy 3:15
text: and that, from your childhood, you have known the Sacred Writings, which can give you the wisdom that, through belief in Christ Jesus, leads to Salvation.

title: II Timothy 3:16
text: Everything that is written under divine inspiration is helpful for teaching, for refuting error, for giving guidance, and for training others in righteousness;

title: II Timothy 3:17
text: so that the Servant of God may be perfect himself, and perfectly equipped for every good action.

title: II Timothy 4:1
text: I solemnly charge you, in the sight of God and of Christ Jesus, who will one day judge the living and the dead--I charge you by his Appearing and by his Kingdom:--

title: II Timothy 4:2
text: Proclaim the Message, be ready in season and out of season, convince, rebuke, encourage, never failing to instruct with forbearance.

title: II Timothy 4:3
text: For a time will come when people will not tolerate sound teaching. They will follow their own wishes, and, in their itching for novelty, procure themselves a crowd of teachers.

title: II Timothy 4:4
text: They will turn a deaf ear to the Truth, and give their attention to legends instead.

title: II Timothy 4:5
text: But you, Timothy, must always be temperate. Face hardships; do the work of a Missionary; discharge all the duties of your Office.

title: II Timothy 4:6
text: As for me, my life blood is already being poured out; the time of my departure is close at hand.

title: II Timothy 4:7
text: I have run the great Race; I have finished the Course; I have kept the Faith.

title: II Timothy 4:8
text: And now the crown of righteousness awaits me, which the Lord, the just Judge, will give me on 'That Day'--and not only to me, but to all who have loved his Appearing.

title: II Timothy 4:9
text: Do your utmost to come to me soon;

title: II Timothy 4:10
text: for Demas, in his love for the world, has deserted me. He has gone to Thessalonica, Crescens to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.

title: II Timothy 4:11
text: There is no one but Luke with me. Pick up Mark on your way, and bring him with you, for he is useful to me in my work.

title: II Timothy 4:12
text: I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.

title: II Timothy 4:13
text: Bring with you, when you come, the cloak which I left at Troas with Carpus, and the books, especially the parchments.

title: II Timothy 4:14
text: Alexander, the coppersmith, showed much ill-feeling towards me. 'The Lord will give him what his actions deserve.'

title: II Timothy 4:15
text: Do you also, be on your guard against him, for he is strongly opposed to our teaching.

title: II Timothy 4:16
text: At my first trial no one stood by me. They all deserted me. May it never be counted against them!

title: II Timothy 4:17
text: But the Lord came to my help and strengthened me, in order that, through me, the proclamation should be made so widely that all the Gentiles should hear it; and I was rescued 'out of the Lion's mouth.'

title: II Timothy 4:18
text: The Lord will rescue me from all evil, and bring me safe into his Heavenly Kingdom. All glory to him for ever and ever! Amen.

title: II Timothy 4:19
text: Give my greeting to Prisca and Aquila, and to the household of Onesiphorus.

title: II Timothy 4:20
text: Erastus remained at Corinth, and I left Thophimus ill at Miletus.

title: II Timothy 4:21
text: Do your utmost to come before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus and Claudia send you their greetings, and so do all our Brothers.

title: II Timothy 4:22
text: May the Lord be with your soul. God bless you all.

title: Titus 1:1
text: From Paul, a servant of God, and an Apostle of Jesus Christ, charged to strengthen the faith of God's Chosen People, and their knowledge of that Truth which makes for godliness, .

title: Titus 1:2
text: and is based on the hope of Immortal Life, which God, who never lies, promised before the ages began,

title: Titus 1:3
text: and has revealed at his own time in his Message, with the proclamation of which I was entrusted by the command of God our Savior.

title: Titus 1:4
text: To Titus, my true Child in our one Faith: May God, the Father, and Christ Jesus, our Savior, bless you and give you peace.

title: Titus 1:5
text: My reason for leaving you in Crete was that you might put in order what had been left unsettled, and appoint Officers of the Church in the various towns, as I myself directed you.

title: Titus 1:6
text: They are to be men of irreproachable character, who are faithful husbands, whose children are Christians and have never been charged with dissolute conduct or have been unruly.

title: Titus 1:7
text: For a Presiding-Officer, as God's steward, ought to be a man of irreproachable character; not self-willed or quick-tempered, nor addicted to drink or to brawling or to questionable money-making.

title: Titus 1:8
text: On the contrary, he should be hospitable, eager for the right discreet, upright, a man of holy life and capable of self-restraint,

title: Titus 1:9
text: who holds doctrine that can be relied on as being in accordance with the accepted Teaching; so that he may be able to encourage others by sound teaching, as well as to refute our opponents.

title: Titus 1:10
text: There are, indeed, many unruly persons--great talkers who deceive themselves, principally converts from Judaism,

title: Titus 1:11
text: whose mouths ought to be stopped; for they upset whole households by teaching what they ought not to teach, merely to make questionable gains.

title: Titus 1:12
text: It was a Cretan--one of their own teachers--who said: 'Cretans are always liars, base brutes, and gluttonous idlers'; and his statement is true.

title: Titus 1:13
text: Therefore rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the Faith,

title: Titus 1:14
text: and may pay no attention to Jewish legends, or to the directions of those who turn their backs upon the Truth.

title: Titus 1:15
text: Everything is pure to the pure-minded, but to those whose minds are polluted and who are unbelievers nothing is pure. Their minds and consciences are alike polluted.

title: Titus 1:16
text: They profess to know God, but by their actions they disown him. They are degraded and self-willed; and, as far as anything good is concerned, they are utterly worthless.

title: Titus 2:1
text: Do you, however, speak of such subjects as properly have a place in sound Christian teaching.

title: Titus 2:2
text: Teach that the older men should be temperate, serious, and discreet; strong in faith, love, and endurance.

title: Titus 2:3
text: So, too, that the older women should be reverent in their demeanor, and that they should avoid scandal, and beware of becoming slaves to drink;

title: Titus 2:4
text: that they should teach what is right, so as to train the younger women to love their husbands and children,

title: Titus 2:5
text: and to be discreet, pure-minded, domesticated, good women, ready to submit to their husbands, in order that God's Message may not be maligned.

title: Titus 2:6
text: And so again with the younger men--impress upon them the need of discretion.

title: Titus 2:7
text: Above all, set an example of doing good. Show sincerity in your teaching, and a serious spirit;

title: Titus 2:8
text: let the instruction that you give be sound and above reproach, so that the enemy may be ashamed when he fails to find anything bad to say about us.

title: Titus 2:9
text: Urge slaves to be submissive to their owners in all circumstances, and to try their best to please them.

title: Titus 2:10
text: Teach them not to contradict or to pilfer, but to show such praiseworthy fidelity in everything, as to recommend the teaching about God our Savior by all that they do.

title: Titus 2:11
text: For the loving-kindness of God has been revealed, bringing Salvation for all;

title: Titus 2:12
text: leading us to renounce irreligious ways and worldly ambitions, and to live discreet, upright, and religious lives here in this present world,

title: Titus 2:13
text: while we are awaiting our Blessed Hope--the Appearing in glory of our great God and Savior, Christ Jesus.

title: Titus 2:14
text: For he gave himself on our behalf, to deliver us from all wickedness, and to purify for himself a People who should be peculiarly his own and eager to do good.

title: Titus 2:15
text: Speak of all this, and encourage and rebuke with all authority. Do not let any one despise you.

title: Titus 3:1
text: Remind your hearers to respect and obey the Powers that be, to be ready for every kind of good work, to speak ill of no one, to avoid quarreling,

title: Titus 3:2
text: to be forbearing, and under all circumstances to show a gentle spirit in dealing with others, whoever they may be.

title: Titus 3:3
text: There was, you remember, a time when we ourselves were foolish, disobedient, misled, slaves to all kinds of passions and vices, living in a spirit of malice and envy, detested ourselves and hating one another.

title: Titus 3:4
text: But, when the kindness of God our Savior and his love for man were revealed, he saved us,

title: Titus 3:5
text: not as the result of any righteous actions that we had done, but in fulfillment of his merciful purposes. He saved us by that Washing which was a New Birth to us, and by the renewing power of the Holy Spirit,

title: Titus 3:6
text: which he poured out upon us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior;

title: Titus 3:7
text: that, having been pronounced righteous through his loving-kindness, we might enter on our inheritance with the hope of Immortal Life.

title: Titus 3:8
text: How true that saying is! And it is on these subjects that I desire you to lay especial stress, so that those who have learned to trust in God may be careful to devote themselves to doing good. Such subjects are excellent in themselves, and of real use to mankind.

title: Titus 3:9
text: But have nothing to do with foolish discussions, or with genealogies, or with controversy, or disputes about the Law. They are useless and futile.

title: Titus 3:10
text: If a man is causing divisions among you, after warning him once or twice, have nothing more to say to him.

title: Titus 3:11
text: You may be sure that such a man has forsaken the Truth and is in the wrong; he stands self-condemned.

title: Titus 3:12
text: As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, join me as quickly as possible at Nicopolis, for I have arranged to spend the winter there.

title: Titus 3:13
text: Do your best to help Zenas, the Teacher of the Law, and Apollos, on their way, and see that they want for nothing.

title: Titus 3:14
text: Let all our People learn to devote themselves to doing good, so as to meet the most pressing needs, and that their lives may not be unfruitful.

title: Titus 3:15
text: All who are with me here send you their greeting. Give my greeting to our friends in the Faith. God bless you all.

title: Philemon 1:1
text: From Paul, now a prisoner for Christ Jesus, and from Timothy, a Brother.

title: Philemon 1:2
text: To our dear friend and fellow-worker Philemon, to our sister Apphia, to our fellow-soldier Archippus; and to the Church that meets at Philemon's house;

title: Philemon 1:3
text: May God, our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ bless you and give you peace.

title: Philemon 1:4
text: I always mention you in my prayers and thank God for you,

title: Philemon 1:5
text: Because I hear of the love and the faith which you show, not only to the Lord Jesus, but also to all his People;

title: Philemon 1:6
text: And I pray that your participation in the Faith may result in action, as you come to a fuller realization of everything that is good and Christlike in us.

title: Philemon 1:7
text: I have indeed found great joy and encouragement in your love, knowing, as I do, how the hearts of Christ's People have been cheered, brother, by you.

title: Philemon 1:8
text: And so, though my union with Christ enables me, with all confidence, to dictate the course that you should adopt,

title: Philemon 1:9
text: Yet the claims of love make me prefer to plead with you--yes, even me, Paul, though I am an ambassador for Christ Jesus and, now a prisoner for him as well.

title: Philemon 1:10
text: I plead with you for this Child of mine, Onesimus, to whom, in my parson, I have become a Father.

title: Philemon 1:11
text: Once he was of little service to you, but now he has become of great service, not only to you, but to me as well;

title: Philemon 1:12
text: And I am sending him back to you with this letter--though it is like tearing out of my very heart.

title: Philemon 1:13
text: For my own sake I should like to keep him with me, so that, while I am in prison for the Good News, he might attend to my wants on your behalf.

title: Philemon 1:14
text: But I do not wish to do anything without your consent, because I want your generosity to be voluntary and not, as it were, compulsory.

title: Philemon 1:15
text: It may be that he was separated from you for an hour, for this very reason, that you might have him back for ever,

title: Philemon 1:16
text: No longer as a slave, but as something better--a dearly loved Brother, especially dear to me, and how much more so to you, not only as your fellow man, but as your fellow Christian!

title: Philemon 1:17
text: If, then, you count me your friend, receive him as you would me.

title: Philemon 1:18
text: If he has caused you any loss, or owes you anything, charge it to me.

title: Philemon 1:19
text: I, Paul, put my own hand to it--I will repay you myself. I say nothing about your owing me your very self.

title: Philemon 1:20
text: Yes, Brother, let me gain something from you because of your union with the Lord. Cheer my heart by your Christlike spirit.

title: Philemon 1:21
text: Even as I write, I have such confidence in your compliance with my wishes, that I am sure that you will do even more than I am asking.

title: Philemon 1:22
text: Please also get a lodging ready for me, for I hope that I shall be given back to you all in answer to your prayers.

title: Philemon 1:23
text: Epaphras, who is my fellow-prisoner for Christ Jesus, sends you his greeting;

title: Philemon 1:24
text: And Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow-workers, send theirs.

title: Philemon 1:25
text: May the blessing of the Lord Jesus Christ rest on your souls.

title: Hebrews 1:1
text: God, who, of old, at many times and in many ways, spoke to our ancestors, by the Prophets,

title: Hebrews 1:2
text: has in these latter days spoken to us by the Son, whom he appointed the heir of all things, and through whom he made the universe.

title: Hebrews 1:3
text: For he is the radiance of the Glory of God and the very expression of his Being, upholding all creation by the power of his word; and, when he had made an expiation for the sins of men, he 'took his seat at the right hand' of God's Majesty on high,

title: Hebrews 1:4
text: having shown himself as much greater than the angels as the Name that he has inherited surpasses theirs.

title: Hebrews 1:5
text: For to which of the angels did God ever say-- 'Thou art my Son; this day I have become thy Father'? or again-- 'I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son'?

title: Hebrews 1:6
text: And again, when God brought the First-born into the world, he said-- 'Let all the angels of God bow down before him.'

title: Hebrews 1:7
text: Speaking of the angels, he said-- 'He makes the winds his angels and the fiery flames his servants';

title: Hebrews 1:8
text: while of the Son he said-- 'God is thy throne for ever and ever; The scepter of his Kingdom is the scepter of Justice;

title: Hebrews 1:9
text: Thou lovest righteousness and hatest iniquity; Therefore God, thy God, has anointed thee with the festal oil more abundantly than thy peers.'

title: Hebrews 1:10
text: Again-- 'Thou, Lord, in the beginning didst lay the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of thy hands.

title: Hebrews 1:11
text: They shall perish, but thou remainest; As a garment they shall all grow old;

title: Hebrews 1:12
text: As a mantle thou wilt fold them up, And as a garment they shall be changed, But thou art the same, and thy years shall know no end.'

title: Hebrews 1:13
text: To which of the angels has God ever said-- 'Sit thou at my right hand until I put thy enemies as a stool for thy feet'?

title: Hebrews 1:14
text: Are not all the angels spirits in the service of God, sent out to minister for the sake of those who are destined to obtain Salvation?

title: Hebrews 2:1
text: Therefore we must give still more heed to what we were taught, for fear we should drift away.

title: Hebrews 2:2
text: For, if the Message which was delivered by angels had its authority confirmed, so that every offence against it, or neglect of it, met with a fitting requital,

title: Hebrews 2:3
text: how can we, of all people, expect to escape, if we disregard so great a Salvation? It was the Master who at the outset spoke of this Salvation, and its authority was confirmed for us by those who heard him,

title: Hebrews 2:4
text: while God himself added his testimony to it by signs, and marvels, and many different miracles, as well as by imparting the Holy Spirit as he saw fit.

title: Hebrews 2:5
text: God has not given to angels the control of that Future World of which we are speaking!

title: Hebrews 2:6
text: No; a writer has declared somewhere-- 'What is Man that thou should'st remember him? Or a Son of Man that thou should'st regard him?

title: Hebrews 2:7
text: Thou hast made him, for a while, lower than angels; With glory and honour thou hast crowned him; Thou hast set him over all that thy hands have made;

title: Hebrews 2:8
text: Thou hast placed all things beneath his feet.' This 'placing of everything' under man means that there was nothing which was not placed under him. As yet, however, we do not see everything placed under man.

title: Hebrews 2:9
text: What our eyes do see is Jesus, who was made for a while lower than angels, now, because of his sufferings and death, crowned with glory and honour; so that his tasting the bitterness of death should, in God's loving-kindness, be on behalf of all mankind.

title: Hebrews 2:10
text: It was, indeed, fitting that God, for whom and through whom all things exist, should, when leading many sons to glory, make the author of their Salvation perfect through suffering.

title: Hebrews 2:11
text: For he who purifies, and those whom he purifies, all spring from One; and therefore he is not ashamed to call them 'Brothers.'

title: Hebrews 2:12
text: He says-- 'I will tell of thy Name to my Brothers, In the midst of the congregation I will sing thy praise.'

title: Hebrews 2:13
text: And again-- 'As for me, I will put my trust in God.' And yet again-- 'See, here am I and the children whom God gave me.'

title: Hebrews 2:14
text: Therefore, since human nature is the common heritage of 'the Children,' Jesus also shared it, in order that by death he might render powerless him whose power lies in death--that is, the Devil--

title: Hebrews 2:15
text: and so might deliver all those who, from fear of death, had all their lives been living in slavery.

title: Hebrews 2:16
text: It was not, surely, to the help of the angels that Jesus came, but 'to the help of the descendants of Abraham.'

title: Hebrews 2:17
text: And consequently it was necessary that he should in all points be made like 'his Brothers,' in order that he might prove a merciful as well as a faithful High Priest in man's relations with God, for the purpose of expiating the sins of his People.

title: Hebrews 2:18
text: The fact that he himself suffered under temptation enables him to help those who are tempted.

title: Hebrews 3:1
text: Therefore, Christian Brothers, you who, all alike, have received the Call from Heaven, fix your attention on Jesus, the Apostle and High Priest of our Religion.

title: Hebrews 3:2
text: See how faithful he was to the God who appointed him, as Moses was in the whole House of God.

title: Hebrews 3:3
text: He has been deemed worthy of far higher honour than Moses, just as the founder of the House is held in greater regard than the House itself.

title: Hebrews 3:4
text: For every House has its founder, and the founder of the universe is God.

title: Hebrews 3:5
text: While the faithful service of Moses in the whole House of God was that of a servant, whose duty was to bear testimony to a Message still to come,

title: Hebrews 3:6
text: the faithfulness of Christ was that of a Son set over the House of God. And we are his House--if only we retain, unshaken to the end, the courage and confidence inspired by our hope.

title: Hebrews 3:7
text: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says-- 'If to-day you hear God's voice,

title: Hebrews 3:8
text: Harden not your hearts, as when Israel provoked me on the day when they tried my patience in the desert,

title: Hebrews 3:9
text: Where your ancestors tried my forbearance, And saw my mighty deeds for forty years.

title: Hebrews 3:10
text: Therefore I was sorely vexed with that generation, And I said-- "Their hearts are always straying; They have never learned my ways";

title: Hebrews 3:11
text: While in my wrath I swore-- "They shall never enter upon my Rest." '

title: Hebrews 3:12
text: Be careful, Brothers, that there is never found in any one of you a wicked and faithless heart, shown by his separating himself from the Living God.

title: Hebrews 3:13
text: Rather encourage one another daily--while there is a 'To-day'--to prevent any one among you from being hardened by the deceitfulness of Sin.

title: Hebrews 3:14
text: For we now all share in the Christ, if indeed we retain, unshaken to the end, the confidence that we had at the first.

title: Hebrews 3:15
text: To use the words of Scripture-- 'If to-day you hear God's voice, harden not your hearts, as when Israel provoked me.'

title: Hebrews 3:16
text: Who were they who heard God speak and yet provoked him? Were not they all those who left Egypt under the leadership of Moses?

title: Hebrews 3:17
text: And with whom was it that God was sorely vexed for forty years? Was not it with those who had sinned, and who fell dead in the desert?

title: Hebrews 3:18
text: And who were they to whom God swore that they should not enter upon his rest, if not those who had proved faithless?

title: Hebrews 3:19
text: We see, then, that they failed to enter upon it because of their want of faith.

title: Hebrews 4:1
