text: We must, therefore, be very careful, though there is a promise still standing that we shall enter upon God's Rest, that none of you even appear to have missed it.

title: Hebrews 4:2
text: For we have had the Good News told us just as they had. But the Message which they heard did them no good, since they did not share the faith of those who were attentive to it.

title: Hebrews 4:3
text: Upon that Rest we who have believed are now entering. As God has said-- 'In my wrath I swore--"They shall never enter upon my Rest;" ' Although God's work was finished at the creation of the world;

title: Hebrews 4:4
text: for, in a passage referring to the seventh day, you will find these words-- 'God rested upon the seventh day after all his work.'

title: Hebrews 4:5
text: On the other hand, we read in that passage-- ' They shall never enter upon my Rest.'

title: Hebrews 4:6
text: Since, then, there is still a promise that some shall enter upon this Rest, and since those who were first told the Good News did not enter upon it, because of their disbelief,

title: Hebrews 4:7
text: again God fixed a day. 'To-day,' he said, speaking after a long interval through the mouth of David, in the passage already quoted-- 'If to-day you hear God's voice harden not your hearts.'

title: Hebrews 4:8
text: Now if Joshua had given 'Rest' to the people, God would not have spoken of another and later day.

title: Hebrews 4:9
text: There is, then, a Sabbath-Rest still awaiting God's People.

title: Hebrews 4:10
text: For he who enters upon God's Rest does himself rest after his work, just as God did.

title: Hebrews 4:11
text: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter upon that Rest, so that none of us fall through such disbelief as that of which we have had an example.

title: Hebrews 4:12
text: God's Message is a living and active power, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing its way till it penetrates soul and spirit--not the joints only but the very marrow--and detecting the inmost thoughts and purposes of the mind.

title: Hebrews 4:13
text: There is no created thing that can hide itself from the sight of God. Everything is exposed and laid bare before the eyes of him to whom we have to give account.

title: Hebrews 4:14
text: We have, then , in Jesus, the Son of God, a great High Priest who has passed into the highest Heaven; let us, therefore, hold fast to the Faith which we have professed.

title: Hebrews 4:15
text: Our High Priest is not one unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who has in every way been tempted, exactly as we have been, but without sinning.

title: Hebrews 4:16
text: Therefore, let us draw near boldly to the Throne of Love, to find pity and love for the hour of need.

title: Hebrews 5:1
text: Every High Priest, taken from among men, is appointed as a representative of his fellow-men in their relations with God, to offer both gifts and sacrifices in expiation of sins.

title: Hebrews 5:2
text: And he is able to sympathize with the ignorant and deluded, since he is himself subject to weakness,

title: Hebrews 5:3
text: and is therefore bound to offer sacrifices for sins, not only for the People, but equally so for himself.

title: Hebrews 5:4
text: Nor does any one take that high office upon himself, till he has been called to do so by God, as Aaron was.

title: Hebrews 5:5
text: In the same way, even the Christ did not take the honour of the High Priesthood upon himself, but he was appointed by him who said to him-- 'Thou art my Son; this day I have become thy Father';

title: Hebrews 5:6
text: and on another occasion also-- 'Thou art a priest for all time of the order of Melchizedek.'

title: Hebrews 5:7
text: Jesus, in the days of his earthly life, offered prayers and supplications, with earnest cries and with tears, to him who was able to save him from death; and he was heard because of his devout submission.

title: Hebrews 5:8
text: Son though he was, he learned obedience from his sufferings;

title: Hebrews 5:9
text: and, being made perfect, he became to all those who obey him the source of eternal Salvation,

title: Hebrews 5:10
text: while God himself pronounced him a High Priest of the order of Melchizedek.

title: Hebrews 5:11
text: Now on this subject I have much to say, but it is difficult to explain it to you, because you have shown yourselves so slow to learn.

title: Hebrews 5:12
text: For whereas, considering the time that has elapsed, you ought to be teaching others, you still need some one to teach you the very alphabet of the Divine Revelation, and need again to be fed with 'milk' instead of with 'solid food.'

title: Hebrews 5:13
text: For every one who still has to take 'milk' knows nothing of the Teaching of Righteousness; he is a mere infant.

title: Hebrews 5:14
text: But 'solid food' is for Christians of mature faith--those whose faculties have been trained by practice to distinguish right from wrong.

title: Hebrews 6:1
text: Therefore, let us leave behind the elementary teaching about the Christ and press on to perfection, not always laying over again a foundation of repentance for a lifeless formality, of faith in God--

title: Hebrews 6:2
text: teaching concerning baptisms and the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead and a final judgement.

title: Hebrews 6:3
text: Yes and, with God's help, we will.

title: Hebrews 6:4
text: For if those who were once for all brought into the Light, and learned to appreciate the gift from Heaven, and came to share in the Holy Spirit,

title: Hebrews 6:5
text: and learned to appreciate the beauty of the Divine Message, and the new powers of the Coming Age--

title: Hebrews 6:6
text: if those, I say, fell away, it would be impossible to bring them again to repentance; they would be crucifying the Son of God over again for themselves, and exposing him to open contempt.

title: Hebrews 6:7
text: Ground that drinks in the showers that from time to time fall upon it, and produces vegetation useful to those for whom it is tilled, receives a blessing from God;

title: Hebrews 6:8
text: but, if it 'bears thorns and thistles,' it is regarded as worthless, it is in danger of being 'cursed,' and its end will be the fire.

title: Hebrews 6:9
text: But about you, dear friends, even though we speak in this way, we are confident of better things--of things that point to your Salvation.

title: Hebrews 6:10
text: For God is not unjust; he will not forget the work that you did, and the love that you showed for his Name, in sending help to your fellow Christians--as you are still doing.

title: Hebrews 6:11
text: But our great desire is that every one of you should be equally earnest to attain to a full conviction that our hope will be fulfilled, and that you should keep that hope to the end.

title: Hebrews 6:12
text: Then you will not show yourselves slow to learn, but you will copy those who, through faith and patience, are now entering upon the enjoyment of God's promises.

title: Hebrews 6:13
text: When God gave his promise to Abraham, since there was no one greater by whom he could swear, he swore by himself.

title: Hebrews 6:14
text: His words were-- 'I will assuredly bless thee and increase thy numbers.'

title: Hebrews 6:15
text: And so, after patiently waiting, Abraham obtained the fulfillment of God's promise.

title: Hebrews 6:16
text: Men, of course, swear by what is greater than themselves, and with them an oath is accepted as putting a matter beyond all dispute.

title: Hebrews 6:17
text: And therefore God, in his desire to show, with unmistakable plainness, to those who were to enter on the enjoyment of what he had promised, the unchangeableness of his purpose, bound himself with an oath.

title: Hebrews 6:18
text: For he intended us to find great encouragement in these two unchangeable things, which make it impossible for God to prove false--we, I mean, who fled for safety where we might lay hold on the hope set before us.

title: Hebrews 6:19
text: This hope is a very anchor for our souls, secure and strong, and it 'reaches into the Sanctuary that lies behind the Curtain,'

title: Hebrews 6:20
text: where Jesus, our Forerunner, has entered on our behalf, after being made for all time a High Priest of the order of Melchizedek.

title: Hebrews 7:1
text: It was this Melchizedek, King of Salem and Priest of the Most High God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and gave him his blessing;

title: Hebrews 7:2
text: and it was to him that Abraham allotted a tithe of all the spoil. The meaning of his name is 'King of Righteousness, ' and besides that, he was also King of Salem, which means 'King of Peace.'

title: Hebrews 7:3
text: There is no record of his father, or mother, or lineage, nor again of any beginning of his days, or end of his life. In this he resembles the Son of God, and stands before us as a priest whose priesthood is continuous.

title: Hebrews 7:4
text: Consider, then the importance of this Melchizedek, to whom even the Patriarch Abraham himself gave a tithe of the choicest spoils.

title: Hebrews 7:5
text: Those descendants of Levi, who are from time to time appointed to the priesthood, are directed to collect tithes from the people in accordance with the Law--that is from their own Brothers, although they also are descended from Abraham.

title: Hebrews 7:6
text: But Melchizedek, although not of this lineage, received tithes from Abraham, and gave his blessing to the very man who had God's promises.

title: Hebrews 7:7
text: Now no one can dispute that it is the superior who blesses the inferior.

title: Hebrews 7:8
text: In the one case the tithes are received by mortal men; in the other case by one about whom there is the statement that his life still continues.

title: Hebrews 7:9
text: Moreover, in a sense, even Levi, who is the receiver of the tithes, has, through Abraham, paid tithes;

title: Hebrews 7:10
text: for Levi was still in the body of his ancestor when Melchizedek met Abraham.

title: Hebrews 7:11
text: If, then, Perfection had been attainable through the Levitical priesthood--and it was under this priesthood that the people received the Law--why was it still necessary that a priest of a different order should appear, a priest of the order of Melchizedek and not of the order of Aaron?

title: Hebrews 7:12
text: With the change of the priesthood a change of the Law became a necessity.

title: Hebrews 7:13
text: And he of whom all this is said belonged to quite a different tribe, no member of which has ever served at the altar.

title: Hebrews 7:14
text: For it is plain that our Lord ad sprung from the tribe of Judah, though of that tribe Moses said nothing about their being priests.

title: Hebrews 7:15
text: All this becomes even yet plainer when we remember that a new priest has appeared, resembling Melchizedek,

title: Hebrews 7:16
text: and that he was appointed, not under a Law regulating only earthly matters, but by virtue of a life beyond the reach of death;

title: Hebrews 7:17
text: for that is the meaning of the declaration-- 'Thou art for all time a priest of the order of Melchizedek.'

title: Hebrews 7:18
text: On the one hand, we have the abolition of a previous regulation as being both inefficient and useless

title: Hebrews 7:19
text: (for the Law never brought anything to perfection); and, on the other hand, we have the introduction of a better hope, which enables us to draw near to God.

title: Hebrews 7:20
text: Then again, the appointment of this new priest was ratified by an oath, which is not so with the Levitical priests,

title: Hebrews 7:21
text: but his appointment was ratified by an oath, when God said to him-- 'The Lord has sworn, and will not change, "Thou art a priest for all time." '

title: Hebrews 7:22
text: And the oath shows the corresponding superiority of the Covenant of which Jesus is appointed the surety.

title: Hebrews 7:23
text: Again, new Levitical priests are continually being appointed, because death prevents their remaining in office;

title: Hebrews 7:24
text: but Jesus remains for all time, and therefore the priesthood that he holds is never liable to pass to another.

title: Hebrews 7:25
text: And that is why he is able to save perfectly those who come to God through him, living for ever, as he does, to intercede of their behalf.

title: Hebrews 7:26
text: This was the High Priest that we needed--holy, innocent, spotless, withdrawn from sinners, exalted above the highest Heaven,

title: Hebrews 7:27
text: one who has no need to offer sacrifices daily as those High Priests have, first for their own sins, and then for those of the People. For this he did once and for all, when he offered himself as the sacrifice.

title: Hebrews 7:28
text: The Law appoints as High Priests men who are liable to infirmity, but the words of God's oath, which was later than the Law, name the Son as, for all time, the perfect Priest.

title: Hebrews 8:1
text: To sum up what I have been saying:--Such is the High Priest that we have, one who 'has taken his seat at the right hand' of the throne of God's Majesty in Heaven,

title: Hebrews 8:2
text: where he ministers in the Sanctuary, in that true Tabernacle set up by the Lord and not by man.

title: Hebrews 8:3
text: Every High Priest is appointed for the purpose of offering gifts and sacrifices to God; it follows, therefore, that this High Priest must have some offering to make.

title: Hebrews 8:4
text: If he were, however, still upon earth, he would not even be a priest, since there are already priests who offer the gifts as the Law directs.

title: Hebrews 8:5
text: (These priests, it is true, are engaged in a service which is only a copy and shadow of the heavenly realities, as is shown by the directions given to Moses when he was about to construct the Tabernacle. 'Look to it,' are the words, 'that thou make every part in accordance with the pattern shown thee on the mountain.')

title: Hebrews 8:6
text: But Jesus, as we see, has obtained a ministry as far excelling theirs, as the Covenant of which he is the intermediary, based, as it is, on better promises, excels the former Covenant.

title: Hebrews 8:7
text: If that first Covenant had been faultless, there would have been no occasion for a second.

title: Hebrews 8:8
text: But, finding fault with the people, God says-- ' "Behold, a time is coming," says the Lord, "when I will ratify a new Covenant with the People of Israel and with the People of Judah--

title: Hebrews 8:9
text: Not such a Covenant as I made with their ancestors on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. For they did not abide by their Covenant with me, And therefore I disregarded them," says the Lord.

title: Hebrews 8:10
text: "This is the Covenant that I will make with the People of Israel After those days," says the Lord. "I will impress my laws on their minds, and will inscribe them on their hearts; And I will be their God, and they shall be my People.

title: Hebrews 8:11
text: There shall be no need for every man to instruct his fellow-citizen, or for a man to say to his Brother 'Learn to know the Lord'; For every one will know me, From the lowest to the highest.

title: Hebrews 8:12
text: For I will be merciful to their wrong-doings, And I will no longer remember their sins." '

title: Hebrews 8:13
text: By speaking of a 'new' Covenant, God at once renders the former Covenant obsolete; and whatever becomes obsolete and loses its force is virtually annulled.

title: Hebrews 9:1
text: It is true that even the first Covenant had its regulations for divine worship, and its Sanctuary--though only a material one.

title: Hebrews 9:2
text: For a Tabernacle was constructed, with an outer part which contained the stand for the lamps, and the table, and the consecrated bread. This is called the Sanctuary.

title: Hebrews 9:3
text: The part of the Tabernacle behind the second Curtain is called the Inner Sanctuary.

title: Hebrews 9:4
text: In it is the gold incense-altar, and the Ark containing the Covenant, completely covered with gold. In the Ark is a gold casket containing the manna, Aaron's rod that budded, and the tablets on which the Covenant was written;

title: Hebrews 9:5
text: while above it, and overshadowing the Cover on which atonement was made, are the Cherubim of the Presence. But I must not now dwell on these things in detail.

title: Hebrews 9:6
text: Such, then, was the arrangement of the Tabernacle. Into the outer part priests are constantly going, in the discharge of their sacred duties;

title: Hebrews 9:7
text: but into the inner only the High Priest goes, and that but once a year, and never without taking the blood of a victim, which he offers on his own behalf, and on behalf of the errors of the People.

title: Hebrews 9:8
text: By this the Holy Spirit is teaching that the way into the Sanctuary was hidden, as long as the outer part of the Tabernacle still remained.

title: Hebrews 9:9
text: For that was only a type, to continue down to the present time; and, in keeping with it, both gifts and sacrifices are offered, though incapable of satisfying the conscience of the worshiper;

title: Hebrews 9:10
text: the whole system being concerned only with food and drink and various ablutions--external ceremonials imposed until the coming of the New Order.

title: Hebrews 9:11
text: But, when Christ came, he appeared as High Priest of that Better System which was established; and he entered through that nobler and more perfect 'Tabernacle,' not made by human hands--that is to say, not a part of this present creation.

title: Hebrews 9:12
text: Nor was it with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, that he entered, once and for all, into the Sanctuary, and obtained our eternal deliverance.

title: Hebrews 9:13
text: For, if the blood of goats and bulls, and the sprinkling of the ashes of a heifer, purify those who have been defiled (as far as ceremonial purification goes),

title: Hebrews 9:14
text: how much more will the blood of the Christ, who, through his eternal Spirit, offered himself up to God, as a victim without blemish, purify our consciences from a lifeless formality, and fit us for the service of the Living God!

title: Hebrews 9:15
text: And that is why he is the intermediary of a new Covenant; in order that, as a death has taken place to effect a deliverance from the offenses committed under the first Covenant, those who have received the Call may obtain the eternal inheritance promised to them.

title: Hebrews 9:16
text: Whenever such a Covenant as a will is in question, the death of the testator must of necessity be alleged.

title: Hebrews 9:17
text: For such a Covenant takes effect only upon death, it does not come into force as long as the testator is alive.

title: Hebrews 9:18
text: This explains why even the first Covenant was not ratified without the shedding of blood.

title: Hebrews 9:19
text: For, when every command had been announced to all the people by Moses in accordance with the Law, he took the blood of the calves and of the goats, with water, scarlet wool, and a bunch of hyssop, and sprinkled even the Book of the Law, as well as all the people,

title: Hebrews 9:20
text: saying, as he did so-- "This is the blood that renders valid the Covenant which God has commanded to be made with you."

title: Hebrews 9:21
text: And in the same way he also sprinkled with the blood the Tabernacle and all the things that were used in public worship.

title: Hebrews 9:22
text: Indeed, under the Law, almost everything is purified with blood; and, unless blood is shed, no forgiveness is to be obtained.

title: Hebrews 9:23
text: While, then, it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly realities to be purified by such means as these, the heavenly realities themselves required better sacrifices.

title: Hebrews 9:24
text: For it was not into a Sanctuary made by human hands, which merely foreshadowed the true one, that Christ entered, but into Heaven itself, that he might now appear in the presence of God on our behalf.

title: Hebrews 9:25
text: Nor yet was it to offer himself may times, as year after year the High Priest entered the Sanctuary with an offering of blood--but not his own blood;

title: Hebrews 9:26
text: for then Christ would have had to undergo death many times since the creation of the world. But now, once and for all, at the close of the age, he has appeared, in order to abolish sin by the sacrifice of himself.

title: Hebrews 9:27
text: And, as it is ordained for men to die but once (death being followed by judgement),

title: Hebrews 9:28
text: so it is with the Christ. He was offered up once and for all, to 'bear away the sins of many'; and the second time he will appear--but without any burden of sin--to those who are waiting for him, to bring Salvation.

title: Hebrews 10:1
text: The Law, though able to foreshadow the Better System which was coming, never had its actual substance. Its priests, with those sacrifices which they offer continuously year after year, can never make those who come to worship perfect.

title: Hebrews 10:2
text: Otherwise, would not the offering of these sacrifices have been abandoned, as the worshipers, having been once purified, would have had their consciences clear from sins?

title: Hebrews 10:3
text: But, on the contrary, these sacrifices recall their sins to mind year after year.

title: Hebrews 10:4
text: For the blood of bulls and goats is powerless to remove sins.

title: Hebrews 10:5
text: That is why, when he was coming into the world, the Christ declared-- 'Sacrifice and offering thou dost not desire, but thou dost provide for me a body;

title: Hebrews 10:6
text: Thou dost take no pleasure in burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin.

title: Hebrews 10:7
text: So I said, "See, I have come' (as is written of me in the pages of the Book), "To do thy will, O God." '

title: Hebrews 10:8
text: First come the words-- ' Thou dost not desire, nor dost thou take pleasure in, sacrifices, offerings, burnt offerings, and sacrifices for sin' (offerings regularly made under the Law),

title: Hebrews 10:9
text: and then there is added-- 'See, I have come to do thy will.' The former sacrifices are set aside to be replaced by the latter.

title: Hebrews 10:10
text: And it is in the fulfilment of the will of God that we have been purified by the sacrifice, once and for all, of the body of Jesus Christ.

title: Hebrews 10:11
text: Every other priest stands day after day at his ministrations, and offers the same sacrifices over and over again--sacrifices that can never take sins away.

title: Hebrews 10:12
text: But, this priest, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins, which should serve for all time, 'took his seat at the right hand of God,'

title: Hebrews 10:13
text: and has since then been waiting 'for his enemies to be put as a stool for his feet.'

title: Hebrews 10:14
text: By a single offering he has made perfect for all time those who are being purified.

title: Hebrews 10:15
text: We have also the testimony of the Holy Spirit. For, after saying--

title: Hebrews 10:16
text: ' "This is the Covenant that I will make with them after those days," says the Lord; "I will impress my laws on their hearts, and will inscribe them on their minds," '

title: Hebrews 10:17
text: then we have-- 'And their sins and their iniquities I will no longer remember.'

title: Hebrews 10:18
text: And, when these are forgiven, there is no further need of an offering for sin.

title: Hebrews 10:19
text: Therefore, Brothers, since we may enter the Sanctuary with confidence, in virtue of the blood of Jesus,

title: Hebrews 10:20
text: by the way which he inaugurated for us--a new and living way, a way through the Sanctuary Curtain (that is, his human nature);

title: Hebrews 10:21
text: and, since we have in him 'a great priest set over the House of God,'

title: Hebrews 10:22
text: let us draw near to God in all sincerity of heart and in perfect faith, with our hearts purified by the sprinkled blood from all consciousness of wrong, and with our bodies washed with pure water.

title: Hebrews 10:23
text: Let us maintain the confession of our hope unshaken, for he who has given us his promise will not fail us.

title: Hebrews 10:24
text: Let us vie with one another in a rivalry of love and noble actions.

title: Hebrews 10:25
text: And let us not, as some do, cease to meet together; but, on the contrary, let us encourage one another, and all the more, now that you see the Day drawing near.

title: Hebrews 10:26
text: Remember, if we sin willfully after we have gained a full knowledge of the Truth, there can be no further sacrifice for sin;

title: Hebrews 10:27
text: there is only a fearful anticipation of judgement, and a burning indignation which will destroy all opponents.

title: Hebrews 10:28
text: When a man disregarded the Law of Moses, he was, on the evidence of two or three witnesses, put to death without pity.

title: Hebrews 10:29
text: How much worse then, think you, will be the punishment deserved by those who have trampled underfoot the Son of God, who have treated the blood that rendered the Covenant valid--the very blood by which they were purified--as of no account, and who have outraged the Spirit of Love?

title: Hebrews 10:30
text: We know who it was that said-- 'It is for me to avenge, I will requite'; and again-- 'The Lord will judge his people.'

title: Hebrews 10:31
text: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the Living God.

title: Hebrews 10:32
text: Call to mind those early days in which, after you had received the Light, you patiently underwent a long and painful conflict.

title: Hebrews 10:33
text: Sometimes, in consequence of the taunts and injuries heaped upon you, you became a public spectacle; and sometimes you suffered through having shown yourselves to be the friends of men who were in the very position in which you had been.

title: Hebrews 10:34
text: For you not only sympathized with those who were in prison, but you even took the confiscation of your possessions joyfully, knowing, as you did, that you had in yourselves a greater possession and a lasting one.

title: Hebrews 10:35
text: Do not, therefore, abandon the confidence that you have gained, for it has a great reward awaiting it.

title: Hebrews 10:36
text: You still have need of patient endurance, in order that, when you have done God's will, you may obtain the fulfillment of his promise.

title: Hebrews 10:37
text: 'For there is indeed but a very little while ere He who is coming will have come, without delay;

title: Hebrews 10:38
text: And through faith the Righteous man shall find his Life, But, if a man draws back, my heart can find no pleasure in him.'

title: Hebrews 10:39
text: But we do not belong to those who draw back, to their Ruin, but to those who have faith, to the saving of their souls.

title: Hebrews 11:1
text: Faith is the realization of things hoped for--the proof of things not seen.

title: Hebrews 11:2
text: And it was for faith that the men of old were renowned.

title: Hebrews 11:3
text: Faith enables us to perceive that the universe was created at the bidding of God--so that we know that what we see was not made out of visible things.

title: Hebrews 11:4
text: Faith made the sacrifice which Abel offered to God a better sacrifice than Cain's, and won him renown as a righteous man, God himself establishing his renown by accepting his gifts; and it is by the example of his faith that Abel, though dead, still speaks.

title: Hebrews 11:5
text: Faith led to Enoch's removal from earth, that he might not experience death. 'He could not be found because God had removed him.' For, before his removal, he was renowned as having pleased God;

title: Hebrews 11:6
text: But without faith it is impossible to please him, for he who comes to God must believe that God exists, and that he rewards those who seek for him.

title: Hebrews 11:7
text: It was faith that enabled Noah, after he had received the divine warning about what could not then be foreseen, to build, in reverent obedience, an ark in which to save his family. By his faith he condemned the world, and became possessed of that righteousness which follows upon faith.

title: Hebrews 11:8
text: It was faith that enabled Abraham to obey the Call that he received, and to set out for the place which he was afterwards to obtain as his own; and he set out not knowing where he was going.

title: Hebrews 11:9
text: It was faith that made him go to live as an emigrant in the Promised Land--as in a strange country--living there in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who shared the promise with him.

title: Hebrews 11:10
text: For he was looking for the City with the sure foundations, whose architect and builder is God.

title: Hebrews 11:11
text: Again, it was faith that enabled Sarah to conceive (though she was past the age for child-bearing), because she felt sure that he who had given her the promise would not fail her.

title: Hebrews 11:12
text: And so from one man--and that when his powers were dead--there sprang a people as numerous 'as the stars in the heavens or the countless grains of sand upon the shore.'

title: Hebrews 11:13
text: All these died sustained by faith. They did not obtain the promised blessings, but they saw them from a distance and welcomed the sight, and they acknowledged themselves to be only aliens and strangers on the earth.

title: Hebrews 11:14
text: Those who speak thus show plainly that they are seeking their fatherland.

title: Hebrews 11:15
text: If they had been thinking of the land that they had left, they could have found opportunities to return.

title: Hebrews 11:16
text: But no, they were longing for a better, a heavenly, land! And therefore God was not ashamed to be called their God; indeed he had already prepared them a city.

title: Hebrews 11:17
text: It was faith that enabled Abraham, when put to the test, to offer Isaac as a sacrifice--he who had received the promises offering up his only son,

title: Hebrews 11:18
text: of whom it had been said-- 'It is through Isaac that there shall be descendants to bear thy name.'

title: Hebrews 11:19
text: For he argued that God was able even to raise a man from the dead--and indeed, figuratively speaking, Abraham did receive Isaac back from the dead.

title: Hebrews 11:20
text: It was faith that enabled Isaac to bless Jacob and Esau, even with regard to the future.

title: Hebrews 11:21
text: Faith enabled Jacob, when dying, to give his blessing to each of the sons of Joseph, and 'to bow himself in worship as he leant upon the top of his staff.'

title: Hebrews 11:22
text: Faith caused Joseph, when his end was near, to speak of the future migration of the Israelites, and to give instructions with regard to his bones.

title: Hebrews 11:23
text: Faith caused the parents of Moses to hide the child for three months after his birth, for they saw that he was a beautiful child; and they would not respect the King's order.

title: Hebrews 11:24
text: It was faith that caused Moses, when he was grown up, to refuse the title of 'Son of a Daughter of Pharaoh.'

title: Hebrews 11:25
text: He preferred sharing the hardships of God's People to enjoying the short-lived pleasures of sin.

title: Hebrews 11:26
text: For he counted 'the reproaches that are heaped upon the Christ' of greater value than the treasures of Egypt, looking forward, as he did, to the reward awaiting him.

title: Hebrews 11:27
text: Faith caused him to leave Egypt, though undaunted by the King's anger, for he was strengthened in his endurance by the vision of the invisible God.

title: Hebrews 11:28
text: Faith led him to institute the Passover and the Sprinkling of the Blood, so that the Destroyer might not touch the eldest children of the Israelites.

title: Hebrews 11:29
text: Faith enabled the people to cross the Red Sea, as if it had been dry land, while the Egyptians, when they attempted to do so, were drowned.

title: Hebrews 11:30
text: Faith caused the walls of Jericho to fall after being encircled for seven days.

title: Hebrews 11:31
text: Faith saved Rahab, the prostitute, from perishing with the unbelievers, after she had entertained the spies with friendliness.

title: Hebrews 11:32
text: Need I add anything more? Time would fail me if I attempted to relate the stories of Gideon, Barak, Samson, and Jephthah, and those of David, Samuel, and the Prophets.

title: Hebrews 11:33
text: By their faith they subdued kingdoms, ruled righteously, gained the fulfilment of God's promises, 'shut the mouths of lions,'

title: Hebrews 11:34
text: quelled the fury of the flames, escaped the edge of the sword, found strength in the hour of weakness, displayed their prowess in war, and routed hostile armies.

title: Hebrews 11:35
text: Women received back their dead raised to life. Some were tortured on the wheel, and refused release in order that they might rise to a better life.

title: Hebrews 11:36
text: Others had to face taunts and blows, and even chains and imprisonment.

title: Hebrews 11:37
text: They were stoned to death, they were tortured, they were swan asunder, they were put to the sword; they wandered about clothed in the skins of sheep or goats, destitute, persecuted, ill-used--

title: Hebrews 11:38
text: men of whom the world was not worthy--roaming in lonely places, and on the mountains, and in caves and holes in the ground.

title: Hebrews 11:39
text: Yet, though they all won renown by their faith, they did not obtain the final fulfilment of God's promise;

title: Hebrews 11:40
text: since God had in view some better thing for us, that they, apart from us, should not attain perfection.

title: Hebrews 12:1
text: Seeing, therefore, that there is on every side of us such a throng of witnesses, let us also lay aside everything that hinders us, and the sin that clings about us, and run with patient endurance the race that lies before us,

title: Hebrews 12:2
text: our eyes fixed upon Jesus, the Leader and perfect Example of our faith, who, for the joy that lay before him, endured the cross, heedless of its shame, and now 'has taken his seat at the right hand' of the throne of God.

title: Hebrews 12:3
text: Weigh well the example of him who had to endure such opposition from 'men who were sinning against themselves,' so that you should not grow weary or faint-hearted.

title: Hebrews 12:4
text: You have not yet, in your struggle with sin, resisted to the death;

title: Hebrews 12:5
text: and you have forgotten the encouraging words which are addressed to you as God's Children-- 'My child, think not lightly of the Lord's discipline, do not despond when he rebukes you;

title: Hebrews 12:6
text: for it is him whom he loves that he disciplines, and he chastises every child whom he acknowledges.'

title: Hebrews 12:7
text: It is for your discipline that you have to endure all this. God is dealing with you as his Children. For where is there a child whom his father does not discipline?

title: Hebrews 12:8
text: If you are left without that discipline, in which all children share, it shows that you are bastards, and not true Children.

title: Hebrews 12:9
text: Further, when our earthly fathers disciplined us, we respected them. Shall we not, then, much rather yield submission to the Father of souls, and live?

title: Hebrews 12:10
text: Our fathers disciplined us for only a short time and as seemed best to them; but God disciplines us for our true good, to enable us to share his holiness.

title: Hebrews 12:11
text: No discipline is pleasant at the time; on the contrary, it is painful. But afterwards its fruit is seen in the peacefulness of a righteous life which is the lot of those who have been trained under it.

title: Hebrews 12:12
text: Therefore 'lift again the down-dropped hands and straighten the weakened knees;

title: Hebrews 12:13
text: make straight paths for your feet,' so that the lame limb may not be put out of joint, but rather be cured.

title: Hebrews 12:14
text: Try earnestly to live at peace with every one, and to attain to that purity without which no one will see the Lord.

title: Hebrews 12:15
text: Take care that no one fails to use the loving help of God, 'that no bitterness is allowed to take root and spring up, and cause trouble,' and so poison the whole community.

title: Hebrews 12:16
text: Take care that no one becomes immoral, or irreligious like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.

title: Hebrews 12:17
text: For you know that even afterwards, when he wished to claim his father's blessing, he was rejected--for he never found an opportunity to repair his error--though he begged for the blessing with tears.

title: Hebrews 12:18
text: It is not to tangible 'flaming fire' that you have drawn near, nor to 'gloom, and darkness, and storm,

title: Hebrews 12:19
text: and the blast of a trumpet, and an audible voice.' Those who heard that voice entreated that they might hear no more,

title: Hebrews 12:20
text: for they could not bear to think of the command-- 'If even an animal touches the mountain, it is to be stoned to death;'

title: Hebrews 12:21
text: and so fearful was the sight that Moses said-- 'I tremble with fear.'

title: Hebrews 12:22
text: No, but it is to Mount Zion that you have drawn near, the City of the Living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to countless hosts of angels,

title: Hebrews 12:23
text: to the festal gathering and assemblage of God's Eldest Sons whose names are enrolled in Heaven, to God the Judge of all men, to the spirits of the righteous who have attained perfection,

title: Hebrews 12:24
text: to Jesus, the intermediary of a new Covenant, and to the Sprinkled Blood that tells of better things than the blood of Abel.

title: Hebrews 12:25
text: Beware how you refuse to hear him who is speaking. For, if the Israelites did not escape punishment, when they refused to listen to him who taught them on earth the divine will, far worse will it be for us, if we turn away from him who is teaching us from Heaven.

title: Hebrews 12:26
text: Then his voice shook the earth, but now his declaration is-- 'Still once more I will cause not only the earth to tremble, but also the heavens.'

title: Hebrews 12:27
text: And those words 'still once more' indicate the passing away of all that is shaken--that is, of all created things--in order that only what is unshaken may remain.

title: Hebrews 12:28
text: Therefore, let us, who have received a kingdom that cannot be shaken, be thankful, and so offer acceptable worship to God, with awe and reverence.

title: Hebrews 12:29
text: For our God is 'a consuming fire.'

title: Hebrews 13:1
text: Let your love for the Brethren continue. :24 Give our greeting to all your Leaders, and to all Christ's People. Our friends from Italy send their greetings to you.

title: Hebrews 13:2
text: Do not neglect to show hospitality; for, through being hospitable, men have all unawares entertained angels.

title: Hebrews 13:3
text: Remember the prisoners, as if you were their fellow-prisoners, and the oppressed, not forgetting that you also are still in the body.

title: Hebrews 13:4
text: Let marriage be honoured by all and the married life be pure; for God will judge those who are immoral and those who commit adultery.

title: Hebrews 13:5
text: Do not let your conduct be ruled by the love of money. Be content with what you have, for God himself has said-- 'I will never forsake you, nor will I ever abandon you.'

title: Hebrews 13:6
text: Therefore we may say with confidence-- 'The Lord is my helper, I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?'

title: Hebrews 13:7
text: Do not forget your Leaders, the men who told you God's Message. Recall the close of their lives, and imitate their faith.

title: Hebrews 13:8
text: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and to-day--yes, and for ever!

title: Hebrews 13:9
text: Do not let yourselves be carried away by the various novel forms of teaching. It is better to rely for spiritual strength upon the divine help, than upon regulations regarding food; for those whose lives are guided by such regulations have not found them of service.

title: Hebrews 13:10
text: We are not without an altar; but it is one at which those who still worship in the Tabernacle have no right to eat.

title: Hebrews 13:11
text: The bodies of those animals whose blood is brought by the High Priest into the Sanctuary, as an offering for sin, are burnt outside the camp.

title: Hebrews 13:12
text: And so Jesus, also, to purify the People by his own blood, suffered outside the gate.

title: Hebrews 13:13
text: Therefore let us go out to him 'outside the camp,' bearing the same reproaches as he;

title: Hebrews 13:14
text: for here we have no permanent city, but are looking for the City that is to be.

title: Hebrews 13:15
text: Through him let us offer, as our sacrifice, continual praise to God--an offering from lips that glorify his Name.

title: Hebrews 13:16
text: Never forget to do kindly acts and to share what you have with others, for such sacrifices are acceptable to God.

title: Hebrews 13:17
text: Obey your Leaders, and submit to their control, for they are watching over your souls, as men who will have to render an account, so that they may do it with joy, and not in sorrow. That would not be to your advantage.

title: Hebrews 13:18
text: Pray for us, for we are sure that our consciences are clear, since our wish is to be occupied with what is good.

title: Hebrews 13:19
text: And I the more earnestly ask for your prayers, that I may be restored to you the sooner.

title: Hebrews 13:20
text: May God, the source of all peace, who brought back from the dead him who, 'by virtue of the blood that rendered valid the unchangeable Covenant, is the Great Shepherd of God's Sheep,' Jesus, our Lord--

title: Hebrews 13:21
text: may God make you perfect in everything that is good, so that you may be able to do his will. May he bring out in us all that is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be all glory for ever and ever. Amen.

title: Hebrews 13:22
text: I beg you, Brothers, to bear with these words of advice. For I have written only very briefly to you.

title: Hebrews 13:23
text: You will be glad to hear that our Brother, Timothy, has been set free. If he comes here soon, we will visit you together.

title: Hebrews 13:24
text: Give our greeting to all your Leaders, and to all Christ's People. Our friends from Italy send their greetings to you.

title: Hebrews 13:25
text: May God bless you all.

title: James 1:1
text: James, a Servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, greets The Twelve Tribes that are living abroad.

title: James 1:2
text: My Brothers, whatever may be the temptations that beset you from time to time, always regard them as a reason for rejoicing,

title: James 1:3
text: Knowing, as you do, that the testing of your faith develops endurance.

title: James 1:4
text: And let endurance do its work perfectly, so that you may be altogether perfect, and in no respect deficient.

title: James 1:5
text: If one of you is deficient in wisdom, let him ask wisdom from the God who gives freely to every one without reproaches, and it will be given to him.

title: James 1:6
text: But let him ask with confidence, never doubting; for the man who doubts is like a wave of the sea driven hither and thither at the mercy of the wind--

title: James 1:7
text: Such a man must not expect that he will receive anything from the Lord,

title: James 1:8
text: Vacillating as he is, irresolute at every turn.

title: James 1:9
text: Let a Brother in humble circumstances be proud of his exalted position, but a rich Brother of his humiliation;

title: James 1:10
text: For the rich man will pass away 'like the flower of the grass.'

title: James 1:11
text: As the sun rises, and the hot wind blows, 'the grass withers, its flower fades,' and all its beauty is gone. So is it with the rich man. In the midst of his pursuits he will come to an untimely end.

title: James 1:12
text: Blessed is the man who remains firm under temptation, for, when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of Life, which the Lord has promised to those who love him.

title: James 1:13
text: Let no one say, when he is tempted, "It is God who is tempting me!" For God, who cannot be tempted to do wrong, does not himself tempt any one.

title: James 1:14
text: A man is in every case tempted by his own passions--allured and enticed by them.

title: James 1:15
text: Then Passion conceives and gives birth to Sin, and Sin, on reaching maturity, brings forth Death.

title: James 1:16
text: Do not be deceived, my dear Brothers.

title: James 1:17
text: Every good thing given us, and every perfect gift, is from above, and comes down to us from the Maker of the Lights in the heavens, who is himself never subject to change or to eclipse.

title: James 1:18
text: Because he so willed, he gave us Life, through the Message of the Truth, so that we should be, as it were, an earnest of still further creations.

title: James 1:19
text: Mark this, my dear Brothers--Let every one be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to get angry;

title: James 1:20
text: For the anger of man does not forward the righteous purpose of God.

title: James 1:21
text: Therefore, have done with all filthiness and whatever wickedness still remains, and in a humble spirit receive that Message which has been planted in your hearts and is able to save your souls.

title: James 1:22
text: Put that Message into practice, and do not merely listen to it--deceiving yourselves.

title: James 1:23
text: For, when any one listens to it and does not practice it, he is like a man looking at his own face in a mirror.

title: James 1:24
text: He looks at himself, then goes on his way,

title: James 1:25
text: But he who looks carefully into the perfect Law, the Law of Freedom, and continues to do so, not listening to it and then forgetting it, but putting it into practice--that man will be blessed in what he does.

title: James 1:26
text: When a man appears to be religious, yet does not bridle his tongue, but imposes upon his own conscience, that man's religious observances are valueless.

title: James 1:27
text: That religious observance which is pure and spotless in the eyes of God our Father is this--to visit orphans and widows in their trouble, and to keep oneself uncontaminated by the world.

title: James 2:1
text: My Brothers, are you really trying to combine faith in Jesus Christ, our glorified Lord, with the worship of rank?

title: James 2:2
text: Suppose a man should enter your Synagogue, with gold rings and in grand clothes, and suppose a poor man should come in also, in shabby clothes,

title: James 2:3
text: And you are deferential to the man who is wearing grand clothes, and say--"There is a good seat for you here," but to the poor man--"You must stand; or sit down there by my footstool,"

title: James 2:4
text: Is not that to make distinctions among yourselves, and show yourselves prejudiced judges?

title: James 2:5
text: Listen, my dear Brothers. Has not God chosen those who are poor in the things of this world to be rich through their faith, and to possess the Kingdom which he has promised to those who love him?

title: James 2:6
text: But you--you insult the poor man! Is not it the rich who oppress you? Is not it they who drag you into law-courts?

title: James 2:7
text: Is not it they who malign that honorable Name which has been bestowed upon you?

title: James 2:8
text: Yet, if you keep the royal law which runs--'Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thou dost thyself,' you are doing right;

title: James 2:9
text: But, if you worship rank, you commit a sin, and stand convicted by that same law of being offenders against it.

title: James 2:10
text: For a man who has laid the Law, as a whole, to heart, but has failed in one particular, is liable for breaking all its provisions.

title: James 2:11
text: He who said 'Thou shalt not commit adultery' also said 'Thou shalt not murder.' If, then, you commit murder but not adultery, you are still an offender against the Law.

title: James 2:12
text: Therefore, speak and act as men who are to be judged by the 'Law of Freedom.'

title: James 2:13
text: For there will be justice without mercy for him who has not acted mercifully. Mercy triumphs over Justice.

title: James 2:14
text: My Brothers, what is the good of a man's saying that he has faith, if he does not prove it by actions? Can such faith save him?

title: James 2:15
text: Suppose some Brother or Sister should be in want of clothes and of daily bread,

title: James 2:16
text: And one of you were to say to them--"Go, and peace be with you; find warmth and food for yourselves," and yet you were not to give them the necessaries of life, what good would it be to them?

title: James 2:17
text: In just the same way faith, if not followed by actions, is, by itself, a lifeless thing.

title: James 2:18
text: Some one, indeed, may say--"You are a man of faith, and I am a man of action." "Then show me your faith," I reply, "apart from any actions, and I will show you my faith by my actions."

title: James 2:19
text: It is a part of your Faith, is it not, that there is one God? Good; yet even the demons have that faith, and tremble at the thought.

title: James 2:20
text: Now do you really want to understand, you foolish man, how it is that faith without actions leads to nothing?

title: James 2:21
text: Look at our ancestor, Abraham. Was not it the result of his actions that he was pronounced righteous after he had offered his son, Isaac, on the altar?

title: James 2:22
text: You see how, in his case, faith and actions went together; that his faith was perfected as the result of his actions;

title: James 2:23
text: And that in this way the words of Scripture came true-- "Abraham believed God, and that was regarded by God as righteousness," and "He was called the friend of God."

title: James 2:24
text: You see, then, that it is as the result of his actions that a man is pronounced righteous, and not of his faith only.

title: James 2:25
text: Was not it the same with the prostitute, Rahab? Was not it as the result of her actions that she was pronounced righteous, after she had welcomed the messengers and hastened them away by a different road?

title: James 2:26
text: Exactly as a body is dead without a spirit, so faith is dead without actions.

title: James 3:1
text: I do not want many of you, my Brothers, to become teachers, knowing, as you do, that we who teach shall be judged by a more severe standard than others.

title: James 3:2
text: We often make mistakes, every one of us. Any one who does not make mistakes when speaking is indeed a perfect man, able to bridle his whole body as well.

title: James 3:3
text: When we put bits into horses' mouths, to make them obey us, we control the rest of their bodies so.

title: James 3:4
text: Again, think of ships. Large as they are, and even when driven by fierce winds, they are controlled by a very small rudder and steered in whatever direction the man at the helm may determine.

title: James 3:5
text: So is it with the tongue. Small as it is, it is a great boaster. Think how tiny a spark may set the largest forest ablaze!

title: James 3:6
text: And the tongue is like a spark. Among the members of our body it proves itself a very world of mischief; it contaminates the whole body; it sets the wheels of life on fire, and is itself set on fire by the flames of the Pit.

title: James 3:7
text: For while all sorts of beasts and birds, and of reptiles and creatures in the sea, are tameable, and actually have been tamed by man,

title: James 3:8
text: No human being can tame the tongue. It is a restless plague! It is charged with deadly poison!

title: James 3:9
text: With it we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men who are made 'in God's likeness.'

title: James 3:10
text: From the very same mouth come blessings and curses! My Brothers, it is not right that this should be so.

title: James 3:11
text: Does a spring give both good and bad water from the same source?

title: James 3:12
text: Can a fig tree, my Brothers, bear olives? or a vine bear figs? No, nor can a brackish well give good water.

title: James 3:13
text: Who among you claims to be wise and intelligent? Let him show that his actions are the outcome of a good life lived in the humility of true wisdom.

title: James 3:14
text: But, while you harbor envy and bitterness and a spirit of rivalry in your hearts, do not boast or lie to the detriment of the Truth.

title: James 3:15
text: That is not the wisdom which comes from above; no, it is earthly, animal, devilish.

title: James 3:16
text: For, where envy and rivalry exist, there you will also find disorder and all kinds of base actions.

title: James 3:17
text: But the wisdom from above is, before every thing else, pure; then peace-loving, gentle, open to conviction, rich in compassion and good deeds, and free from partiality and insincerity.

title: James 3:18
text: And righteousness, its fruit, is sown in peace by those who work for peace.

title: James 4:1
text: What is the cause of the fighting and quarreling that goes on among you? Is not it to be found in the desires which are always at war within you?

title: James 4:2
text: You crave, yet do not obtain. You murder and rage, yet cannot gain your end. You quarrel and fight. You do not obtain, because you do not ask.

title: James 4:3
text: You ask, yet do not receive, because you ask for a wrong purpose--to spend what you get upon your pleasures.

title: James 4:4
text: Unfaithful people! Do not you know that to be friends with the world means to be at enmity with God? Therefore whoever chooses to be friends with the world makes himself an enemy to God.

title: James 4:5
text: Do you suppose there is no meaning in the passage of Scripture which asks--'Is envy to result from the longings of the Spirit which God has implanted within you?'

title: James 4:6
text: No; the gift that God gives is for a nobler end; and that is why it is said--'God is opposed to the haughty, but gives help to the humble.'

title: James 4:7
text: Therefore submit to God; but resist the Devil, and he will flee from you.

title: James 4:8
text: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Make your hands clean, you sinners; and your hearts pure, you vacillating men!

title: James 4:9
text: Grieve, mourn, and lament! Let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your happiness to gloom!

title: James 4:10
text: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.

title: James 4:11
text: Do not disparage one another, Brothers. He who disparages his Brother, or passes judgement on his Brother, disparages the Law and passes judgement on the Law. But, if you pass judgement on the Law, you are not obeying it, but judging it.

title: James 4:12
text: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge--he who has the power both to save and to destroy. But who are you that pass judgement on your neighbor?

title: James 4:13
text: Listen to me, you who say 'To-day or to-morrow we will go to such and such a town, spend a year there, and trade, and make money,'

title: James 4:14
text: And yet you do not know what your life will be like to-morrow! For you are but a mist appearing for a little while and then disappearing.

title: James 4:15
text: You ought, rather, to say 'If the Lord wills, we shall live and do this or that.'

title: James 4:16
text: But, as it is, you are constantly boasting presumptuously! All such boasting is wicked.

title: James 4:17
text: He, then, who knows what is right but fails to do it--that is sin in him.

title: James 5:1
text: Listen to me, you rich men, weep and wail for the miseries that are coming upon you!

title: James 5:2
text: Your riches have wasted away, and your clothes have become moth-eaten.

title: James 5:3
text: Your gold and silver are rusted; and the rust on them shall be evidence against you, and shall eat into your very flesh. It was fire, so to speak, that you stored up for yourselves in these last days.

title: James 5:4
text: I tell you, the wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you have been fraudulently keeping back, are crying out against you, and the outcries of your reapers have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts!

title: James 5:5
text: You have lived on earth a life of extravagance and luxury; you have indulged your fancies in a time of bloodshed.

title: James 5:6
text: You have condemned, you have murdered, the Righteous One! Must not God be opposed to you?

title: James 5:7
text: Be patient, then, Brothers, till the Coming of the Lord. Even the farmer has to wait for the precious fruit of the earth, watching over it patiently, till it has had the spring and summer rains.

title: James 5:8
text: And you must be patient also, and not be discouraged; for the Lord's Coming is near.

title: James 5:9
text: Do not make complaints against one another, Brothers, or judgement will be passed upon you. The Judge is already standing at the door!

title: James 5:10
text: Brothers, as an example of the patient endurance of suffering, take the Prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

title: James 5:11
text: We count those who displayed such endurance blessed! You have heard, too, of Job's endurance, and have seen what the Lord's purpose was, for 'the Lord is full of pity and compassion.'

title: James 5:12
text: Above all things, my Brothers, never take an oath, either by heaven, or by earth, or by anything else. With you let 'Yes' suffice for yes, and 'No' for no, so that you may escape condemnation.

title: James 5:13
text: If any of you is in trouble, let him pray; if any one is happy, let him sing hymns.

title: James 5:14
text: If any one of you is ill, let him send for the Officers of the Church, and let them pray over him, after anointing him with oil in the name of the lord.

title: James 5:15
text: The prayer offered in faith will save the man who is sick, and the Lord will raise him from his bed; and if he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.

title: James 5:16
text: Therefore, confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be cured. Great is the power of a good man's fervent prayer.

title: James 5:17
text: Elijah was only a man like ourselves, but, when he prayed fervently that it might not rain, no rain fell upon the land for three years and a half.

title: James 5:18
text: And, when he prayed again, the clouds brought rain, and the land bore crops.

title: James 5:19
text: My Brothers, should one of you be led astray from the Truth, and some one bring him back again,

title: James 5:20
text: Be sure that he who brings a sinner back from his mistaken ways will save that man's soul from Death, and throw a veil over countless sins.

title: I Peter 1:1
text: To the People of God who are living abroad, dispersed throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Roman Asia, and Bithynia,

title: I Peter 1:2
text: and who were chosen in accordance with the foreknowledge of God the Father, through the consecration of the Spirit, to learn obedience, and to be purified by the sprinkling of the Blood of Jesus Christ, from Peter, an Apostle of Jesus Christ. May blessing and peace be yours in ever-increasing measure.

title: I Peter 1:3
text: Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has, in his great mercy, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

title: I Peter 1:4
text: given us the new Life of undying hope, that promises an inheritance, imperishable, stainless, unfading, which has been reserved for you in Heaven--

title: I Peter 1:5
text: for you who, through faith, are being guarded by the power of God, awaiting a Salvation that is ready to be revealed in the last days.

title: I Peter 1:6
text: At the thought of this you are full of exultation, though (if it has been necessary) you have suffered for the moment somewhat from various trials;

title: I Peter 1:7
text: that the genuineness of your faith--a thing far more precious than gold, which is perishable, yet has to be tested by fire--may win praise and glory and honour at the Appearing of Jesus Christ.

title: I Peter 1:8
text: Though you have never seen him, yet you love him; though you do not even now see him, yet you believe in him, and exalt with a triumphant happiness too great for words,

title: I Peter 1:9
text: as you receive the reward of your faith in the Salvation of your souls!

title: I Peter 1:10
text: It was this Salvation that the Prophets, who spoke long ago of the blessing intended for you, sought, and strove to comprehend;

title: I Peter 1:11
text: as they strove to discern what that time could be, to which the Spirit of Christ within them was pointing, when foretelling the sufferings that would befall Christ, and the glories that would follow.

title: I Peter 1:12
text: And it was revealed to them that it was not for themselves, but for you, that they were acting as Ministers of the truths which have now been told to you, by those who, with the help of the Holy Spirit sent from Heaven, have brought you the Good News--truths into which even angels long to look.

title: I Peter 1:13
text: Therefore concentrate your minds, with the strictest self-control, and fix your hopes on the blessing that is coming for you at the Appearing of Jesus Christ.

title: I Peter 1:14
text: Be like obedient children; do not let your lives be shaped by the passions which once swayed you in the days of your ignorance,

title: I Peter 1:15
text: but in your whole life show yourselves to be holy, after the pattern of the Holy One from whom you received your Call.

title: I Peter 1:16
text: For Scripture says-- 'You shall be holy, because I am holy.'

title: I Peter 1:17
text: And since you call upon him as 'Father,' who judges every one impartially by what he has done, let reverence be the spirit of your lives during the time of your stay upon earth.

title: I Peter 1:18
text: For you know that it was not by perishable things, such as silver and gold, that you were Ransomed from the aimless way of living which was handed down to you from your ancestors,

title: I Peter 1:19
text: but by precious blood, as it were of a lamb, unblemished and spotless, the Blood of Christ.

title: I Peter 1:20
text: Destined for this before the beginning of the world, he has been revealed in these last days for your sakes,

title: I Peter 1:21
text: who, through him, are faithful to God who raised him from the dead and gave him honour, so that your faith and hope are now in God.

title: I Peter 1:22
text: Now that, by your obedience to the Truth, you have purified your lives, so that there is growing up among you a genuine brotherly affection, love one another earnestly with all your hearts;

title: I Peter 1:23
text: since your new Life has come, not from perishable, but imperishable, seed, through the Message of the Everliving God.

title: I Peter 1:24
text: For-- 'All earthly life is but as grass, And all its splendor as the flower of grass. The grass fades, Its flower falls,

title: I Peter 1:25
text: But the teaching of the Lord remains for ever.' And that is the Teaching of the Good News which has been told to you.

title: I Peter 2:1
text: Now that you have done with all malice, all deceitfulness, insincerity, jealous feelings, and all back-biting,

title: I Peter 2:2
text: like newly born infants, crave pure spiritual milk, so that you may be enabled by it to grow till you attain Salvation--

title: I Peter 2:3
text: since 'you have found by experience that the Lord is kind.'

title: I Peter 2:4
text: Come to Him, then, as to a living stone, rejected, indeed, by men, but in God's eyes choice and precious;

title: I Peter 2:5
text: and, as living stones, form yourselves into a spiritual House, to be a consecrated Priesthood, for the offering of spiritual sacrifices that will be acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.

title: I Peter 2:6
text: For there is a passage of Scripture that runs-- 'See, I am placing in Zion a choice and precious corner-stone; And he who believes in him shall have no cause for shame.'

title: I Peter 2:7
text: It is to you, then, who believe in him that he is precious, but to those who do not believe he is 'a stone which, though rejected by the builders, has now itself become the corner-stone,'

title: I Peter 2:8
text: and 'a stumbling-block, and a rock which shall prove a hindrance.' They stumble because they do not accept the Message. This was the fate destined for them.

title: I Peter 2:9
text: But you are 'a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a consecrated nation, God's own People,' entrusted with the proclamation of the goodness of him who called you out of Darkness into his wonderful Light.

title: I Peter 2:10
text: Once you were 'not a people,' but now you are 'God's People'; once you 'had not found mercy,' but now you 'have found mercy.'

title: I Peter 2:11
text: Dear friends, I urge you, as pilgrims and strangers upon earth, to refrain from indulging the cravings of your earthly nature, for they make war upon the soul.

title: I Peter 2:12
text: Let your daily life among the Gentiles be so upright, that, whenever they malign you as evil-doers, they may learn, as they watch, from the uprightness of your conduct, to praise God 'at the time when he shall visit them.'

title: I Peter 2:13
text: Submit to all human institutions for the Lord's sake, alike to the emperor as the supreme authority,

title: I Peter 2:14
text: and to governors as the men sent by him to punish evil-doers and to commend those who do right.

title: I Peter 2:15
text: For God's will is this--that you should silence the ignorance of foolish people by doing what is right.

title: I Peter 2:16
text: Act as free men, yet not using your freedom as those do who make it a cloak for wickedness, but as Servants of God.

title: I Peter 2:17
text: Show honour to every one, Love the Brotherhood, 'revere God, honour the emperor.'

title: I Peter 2:18
text: Those of you who are domestic servants should always be submissive and respectful to their masters, not only to those who are good and considerate, but also to those who are arbitrary.

title: I Peter 2:19
text: For this wins God's approval when, because conscious of God's presence, a man who is suffering unjustly bears his troubles patiently.

title: I Peter 2:20
text: What credit can you claim when, after doing wrong, you take your punishment for it patiently? But, on the other hand, if, after doing right, you take your sufferings patiently, that does win the approval of God.

title: I Peter 2:21
text: For it was to this that you were called! For Christ, too, suffered--on your behalf--and left you an example, that you should follow in his steps.

title: I Peter 2:22
text: He 'never sinned, nor was anything deceitful ever heard from his lips.'

title: I Peter 2:23
text: He was abused, but he did not answer with abuse; he suffered, but he did not threaten; he entrusted himself to him whose judgements are just.

title: I Peter 2:24
text: And he 'himself carried our sins' in his own body to the cross, so that we might die to our sins, and live for righteousness. 'His bruising was your healing.'

title: I Peter 2:25
text: Once you were straying like sheep, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Guardian of your souls.

title: I Peter 3:1
text: Again, you married women should submit to your husbands, so that if any of them reject the Message, they may, apart from the Message, be won over, by the conduct of their wives,

title: I Peter 3:2
text: as they watch your submissive and blameless conduct.

title: I Peter 3:3
text: Yours should be, not the external adornment of the arrangement of the hair, the wearing of jewelry, or the putting on of dresses,

title: I Peter 3:4
text: but the inner life with the imperishable beauty of a quiet and gentle spirit; for this is very precious in God's sight.

title: I Peter 3:5
text: It was by this that the holy women of old, who rested their hopes on God, adorned themselves; submitting to their husbands,

title: I Peter 3:6
text: as Sarah did, who obeyed Abraham, and called him master. And you are her true children, as long as you live good lives, and let nothing terrify you.

title: I Peter 3:7
text: Again, those of you who are married men should live considerately with their wives, showing due regard to their sex, as weaker than their own, and not forgetting that they share with you in the gift of Life. Then you will be able to pray without hindrance.

title: I Peter 3:8
text: Lastly, you should all be united, sympathetic, full of brotherly love, kind-hearted, humble-minded;

title: I Peter 3:9
text: never returning evil for evil, or abuse for abuse, but, on the contrary, blessing. It was to this that you were called--to obtain a blessing!

title: I Peter 3:10
text: 'He who would enjoy life And see happy days-- let him keep his tongue from evil And his lips from deceitful words,

title: I Peter 3:11
text: Let him turn from evil and do good, Let him seek for peace and follow after it;

title: I Peter 3:12
text: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, And his ears are attentive to their prayers, But the face of the Lord is set against those who do wrong.'

title: I Peter 3:13
text: Who, indeed, is there to harm you, if you prove yourselves to be eager for what is good?

title: I Peter 3:14
text: Even if you should suffer for righteousness, count yourselves blessed! 'Do not let men terrify you, or allow yourselves to be dismayed.'

title: I Peter 3:15
text: Revere the Christ as Lord in your hearts; always ready to give an answer to any one who asks your reason for the hope that you cherish, but giving it humbly and in all reverence,

title: I Peter 3:16
text: and keeping your consciences clear, so that, whenever you are maligned, those who vilify your good and Christian conduct may be put to shame.

title: I Peter 3:17
text: It is better that you should suffer, if that should be God's will, for doing right, than for doing wrong.
